motivering: Vänsterpartiet has tabled its own motions (Samuel Gonzalez Westling et al., motions 14 and 15) on student grants during sick leave and for people with disabilities, which the committee rejects. V emphasises the right to support for the sick and people with disabilities, and a humane sickness insurance. Voting No entails support for Reservation 7 and the party's own motions.

citations.quote: you who live with a disability should be able to trust that you will receive the support you need, and that your right to participate in society in the way you wish is not constantly questioned and obstructed.
citations.princip: support and rights for people with disabilities

citations.quote: Vänsterpartiet wants to see a humane sickness insurance and an end to the forcing of sick people out of benefits.

motivering: Vänsterpartiet wants 'all children and young people to be given the same right to education' and supports a compensatory school that provides more support to those with weaker starting conditions. Children's influence and participation is a natural part of this equality perspective. The committee's rejection of the motions on children's influence contradicts the party's view on the rights of children and young people in society.

citations.quote: Swedish preschool and school shall be equal and gender-equal, where all children and young people are given the same right to education.
A school that gives children equal chances is also compensatory, that is, it is capable of providing more support to those who come from worse starting conditions.

motivering: V's own motions 23 and 24 (Nooshi Dadgostar et al.) are rejected by the committee. The election platform emphasises that heavy transport must be directed to the railways and that vital public infrastructure must be taken back into public ownership. Reservation 9 is likely V's own reservation on the conditions for SJ AB. V votes No to support its reservation on state railway ownership.

citations.quote: Heavy transport needs to be directed to rail and sustainable shipping.
It is high time to act and take back the vital public operations and infrastructure that have been privatised.

motivering: Vänsterpartiet has tabled its own motion 2 (Tony Haddou et al.) which the committee proposal explicitly rejects. The manifesto establishes that no one should 'be dependent on the employer to be allowed to stay in Sweden' — a raised income requirement tied to the specific employment risks reinforcing this dependency. The party supports its own reservation and votes No.

citations.quote: None of us should have to endure racism in the workplace or be dependent on the employer to be allowed to stay in Sweden.
Wage dumping, economic crime, and exploitation are central threats today.
citations.princip: combat wage dumping through own means

motivering: Vänsterpartiet considers that integration is promoted by a secure and permanent existence and that discrimination against people with a foreign background must be actively stopped. The motions on the establishment of newly arrived women in the labour market and on civic orientation (samhällsorientering) are in line with these principles. V votes no to the committee's rejection and supports Reservation 11.

citations.quote: On the contrary, it is through a secure and permanent existence in society that we human beings put down roots.
Discrimination and racism in the labour market must be stopped.

motivering: Vänsterpartiet (the Left Party) has motion item 9 on the price and wage adjustment (pris- och löneomräkning) that the committee wishes to reject; V should vote No and support Reservation 1. The PLO system's built-in productivity deduction genuinely reduces agency resources year after year, which works against V's demand that resources are what is primarily needed in public services and welfare — not automated efficiency requirements.

citations.quote: It is resources that are primarily needed, not forms for quality assurance, new booking systems for hospital beds, or yet another management consultant who knows nothing about the operations.
The combination of market solutions, bureaucracy, and resource shortages has created near-inhumane conditions for the essential workers we cannot do without.

motivering: V's election manifesto is clear: public investments should increase state ownership and everyone's democratic influence, and the state must strengthen its control over infrastructure and resources. No V motion item is explicitly named among the rejected ones, but Reservation 2 likely reflects a demand for stronger democratic ownership governance of state-owned companies — in line with the party's core position.

citations.quote: It is investments that increase state ownership and thereby everyone's democratic influence.
The state must increase its control over the infrastructure and resources needed to implement the climate transition.

motivering: The election manifesto does not address the Allmänna arvsfonden (General Inheritance Fund) specifically. The committee's proposal is a neutral administrative acknowledgment that the fund's work has functioned well. Without information on which motion is being rejected and what it contains, the party chooses to support the committee's neutral position to note the report.

citations.quote: Children, the sick, and the unemployed must of course have the same right as working people to live good lives.

motivering: The committee's proposal notes the report (lägger skrivelsen till handlingarna) with reference to the National Board of Health and Welfare's (Socialstyrelsen) ongoing work — the matter is not closed but is referred to the agencies. V lacks its own motion item and has no reason to support SD's reservation. Noting the government's response is consistent with V's demand for a functioning sick-leave certification process, as the National Board of Health and Welfare is in fact working on the guidelines.

citations.quote: It is not acceptable that large resources, which are needed for people with complex or long-term care needs, instead go to online medical services to treat common colds and other minor ailments in healthy people.

When you fall ill, you must worry not only about your health, but also about what your healthcare options look like and about whether the Swedish Social Insurance Agency (Försäkringskassan) will approve the medical certificate.

motivering: Vänsterpartiet demands that policy strengthen climate policy instruments; GDP indexation is a minimum for preserving the real effect of environmental taxes. The committee's decision to reject the indexation and prepare for the abolition of the waste tax weakens environmental fiscal policy, which conflicts with V's demand for stricter climate policy. V should support the reservation and vote No against the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: The transition needs to happen immediately and all political decisions need to take into account the acute crisis we are in.
citations.princip: climate crisis demands stronger policy instruments

citations.quote: Today, one hundred companies in the world account for seventy percent of carbon dioxide emissions. Policy can and must demand that industry transitions.
Reuse and recycling of materials need to increase.

motivering: V is a consistent opponent of increased militarization and wishes to tear up the host country agreement with NATO. The motions from S, C, and SD point toward strengthened military defense and deeper NATO integration — precisely what V explicitly rejects. The committee's rejection of these motions aligns with the party's line; Reservation 1 (likely S's demand for strengthened defense policy) should not be supported.

citations.quote: Vänsterpartiet considers that Sweden should be a voice for peace and justice, not for increased militarization.
Vänsterpartiet is opposed to Sweden's ever-deeper military cooperation with NATO.
Vänsterpartiet wants Sweden to tear up the host country agreement with NATO.

motivering: The committee rejects V's motion item 3 (Karin Rågsjö et al.) on increased resources — a demand that directly follows from the election manifesto. Vänsterpartiet supports its reservation 4 and votes no. The manifesto explicitly demands more resources for healthcare and elderly care in order to address the staff shortage and improve care and working conditions.

citations.quote: invest more resources in healthcare and elderly care, and invest in staff so that we simultaneously eliminate the staff shortage and strengthen the staff's terms and working conditions
citations.princip: more resources for healthcare and staff

citations.quote: Sweden needs to rebuild the entire healthcare sector in order to handle the more normal fluctuations in care needs but also to be able to scale up capacity in times of crisis.

motivering: The fribeloppet (income ceiling for students receiving study support) — the income threshold for students receiving student aid — is not explicitly addressed in V's election manifesto. V's solution is to raise the study aid amounts, not to adjust income thresholds that enable more work alongside studies, which is more characteristic of C's market-adapted approach. The committee's rejection of these motions is more consistent with V's direction.

citations.quote: raise study support so that more people can choose to pursue further education
citations.princip: raise support levels, not income thresholds

citations.quote: It must become easier to pursue education after primary school regardless of who you are, the thickness of your wallet, or where in the country you live.

motivering: The committee approves the confidentiality provision on individuals' personal circumstances (Chapter 28, Section 4a §) and rejects V's motion by Nooshi Dadgostar et al. (as well as those from S, C, and MP). Vänsterpartiet supports reservation 1 and votes no. The party champions democratic governance of welfare administration and transparent handling of electricity support.

citations.quote: The public sector should take over responsibility for the electricity grid, which will lead to reduced fees for households.
Welfare is society's responsibility and should be governed democratically.

motivering: The committee rejects V's motion item 20 (Nooshi Dadgostar et al.) on regional development policy. V demands that the value of natural resources stays locally and that the conditions for living and working throughout the country are improved. The party should vote No and support Reservation 1, which covers motion item 20.

citations.quote: More of the value of natural resources must remain where they are extracted and produced.
citations.princip: local return of natural resource value

citations.quote: Regardless of where in the country we live, we have a shared interest in ensuring that rural areas are not depleted.

motivering: Vänsterpartiet emphasizes that genuine integration requires a secure and permanent existence, not directed settlement that limits newly arrived persons' opportunities to put down roots. The motions from MP, C, and S likely aim to improve the outcomes of the Settlement Act (bosättningslagen) for newly arrived persons, in line with V's view on integration. V should vote No and support Reservation 1.

citations.quote: it is through a secure and permanent existence in society that we as people put down roots
citations.princip: secure settlement for newly arrived persons

citations.quote: None of us should have to endure racism in the workplace or be dependent on the employer to be allowed to stay in Sweden.
citations.princip: newly arrived persons' independence and rights

motivering: The committee rejects Vänsterpartiet's own motions (Mia Sydow Mölleby et al. (V) motion items 1–3) on the new Riksbank Act. Reservation 1 represents the party's position. The election manifesto emphasizes democratic influence and state control over important institutions, in conflict with the new law's strengthened Riksbank independence. The party supports its own reservation.

citations.quote: It is investments that increase state ownership and thereby everyone's democratic influence.
It is not possible to hand over the future to the arbitrariness of market forces; the future belongs to us all.
citations.princip: against institutional autonomy without democratic control

motivering: Among the rejected motions is the Left Party's own motion (Nooshi Dadgostar et al., V) on a pre-emption law (förköpslag). The party explicitly demands 'an active land policy' and state support for housing construction; a pre-emption law is a central instrument for precisely this. Reservation 7 is likely the Left Party's own reservation, and the party votes No to support its own position.

citations.quote: The Left Party wants to see a state construction company, investment support for increased housing construction, and an active land policy.
The ability to live well at a reasonable cost has played an important role in the building of an equal society

motivering: The committee rejects the Left Party's own motion (Vasiliki Tsouplaki et al. (V), point 2) on stronger requirements for restraint in gambling advertising. Reservation 12 represents the party's position for stronger regulation that protects vulnerable groups. The party advocates regulation over market logic and supports its own reservation.

citations.quote: In recent decades, policy has relied on the market to meet our needs for security, but market-based solutions have eroded our shared welfare
Children, the sick, and the unemployed must of course have the same right as working people to live good lives.

motivering: The Tidö agreement binds SD to support the government's bills. The temporary tax is EU-mandated and is directed at fossil fuel companies' extraordinary profits — not at ordinary corporate tax. The revenues protect households against electricity price shocks, a goal the Tidö agreement explicitly states. The tax is temporary and EU-ordered, which reduces the conflict with SD's general tax policy. The committee's proposal to approve the bill and reject the Centre Party's motion is supported.

citations.quote: The cooperation parties commit to voting for the government's budget so that the budget as a whole is passed by the Riksdag.
citations.princip: budget commitment in the Tidö agreement

citations.quote: A high-cost protection scheme for affected households and businesses as soon as practically possible — with retroactive payment.
citations.princip: high-cost protection against electricity price shocks

omvarld.faktor: Electricity price SE3 SEK 3.27/kWh (30-day average December 2022)
omvarld.effekt: Extremely high electricity prices reinforce the need for household support and make the purpose of the solidarity tax directly compatible with the Tidö agreement's goal of protection against electricity price shocks

omvarld.faktor: Inflation (CPI) 11.5% year-on-year
omvarld.effekt: Steep price increases raise the financial pressure on households and strengthen the rationale for redistributing fossil fuel companies' extraordinary profits to consumer relief

motivering: Members of parliament's financial conditions are not addressed in the Centre Party's election manifesto. The identified motion is from V (the Left Party), and it is unclear whether Reservation 1 reflects C's (the Centre Party's) position. In the absence of specific policy support for the current demand, the party should follow the committee's majority decision and vote Yes.

citations.quote: We want to make it harder to amend the constitution, protect the position of the opposition in the Riksdag, and strengthen the independence of the courts.

motivering: The Sweden Democrats' (SD) motions on uranium extraction are not supported by the Centre Party's green transition agenda, which focuses on renewable energy sources and innovation-critical metals. C does not cooperate with SD. The committee's rejection of these motions is consistent with C's policy, and C votes Yes.

citations.quote: To manage the green transition, we must make use of Sweden's natural resources. It is better for Sweden to take responsibility and extract more minerals and metals instead of continuing to import them from countries with a larger climate footprint and worse working conditions.
citations.princip: green mineral extraction for the transition

citations.quote: The Centre Party is now the only centre-right party that will not cooperate with the Sweden Democrats or give them power over how Sweden is governed.

motivering: The Centre Party had its own motion on GPS monitoring for prisoner transports and leave of absence (Ulrika Liljeberg et al. (C), motion item 42), which the committee rejects. C's manifesto calls for more resources for the prison and probation service and stricter tools against crime. Reservation 11 represents C's own position, and the party should vote No.

citations.quote: Society must not give in to the gangs. Defeating them requires better efforts to prevent recruitment of new members, more resources for the police, prosecutors, courts and the prison and probation service, and stricter punishments.
The crime victim's perspective must be strengthened. Those who have been victims of crime should receive redress and better support.

motivering: The Centre Party defends press freedom and increased transparency in society. Restricting the searchability of personal data in public registers risks limiting press freedom and the principle of public access to official documents, which the party consistently supports. No C motion is affected, and the committee refers to ongoing work; the party should vote Yes.

citations.quote: Press freedom shall be protected and independent public service defended.
Sweden shall become even more transparent. We want to establish an anti-corruption agency, tighten rules against corruption, and introduce a lobbying register.

motivering: The Centre Party's motion on following up the effects of the law (Anders W Jonsson et al.) is rejected by the committee. The manifesto upholds effective healthcare and society's preparedness; a follow-up ensures that the law genuinely strengthens the health and medical care sector's supply preparedness. The party supports Reservation 3, which calls for a follow-up, and votes No.

citations.quote: Civil defense is also vital. We must strengthen civil defense and society's preparedness for war and crisis.
Sweden needs healthcare and social care that puts patients, users and staff at the center. This is a top priority for the Centre Party ahead of the next parliamentary term.
citations.princip: healthcare and social care at the center

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motion (Bergenblock et al., motion item 44) on harm reduction within addiction care, which the committee proposes to reject. The manifesto's call for improved psychiatric care and a simple, unified point of entry into care bears directly on this issue. The party should support Reservation 10 and vote No.

citations.quote: Psychiatric care must be improved for both young and old. Those seeking support should be met with a unified and simple point of entry into care and be offered better self-care while waiting for treatment.
Support for people with mental ill health must be improved, not least for young people. Those seeking help should have a simple and unified point of entry into care.
citations.princip: simple point of entry into care

motivering: C's manifesto calls for better efforts to prevent the recruitment of young people into gang crime and for preventive work to permeate the whole of society. The Social Democrats' (S) motion on coordinated efforts for young offenders is substantively consistent with this. The committee's reference to ongoing work is insufficient given C's willingness to take active action.

citations.quote: Society must not give in to the gangs. Defeating them requires better efforts to prevent recruitment of new members, more resources for the police, prosecutors, courts and the prison and probation service, and stricter punishments.
citations.princip: prevent gang recruitment among young people

citations.quote: Preventive work must start early and permeate the whole of society.

motivering: The Centre Party has an explicit commitment to introduce a lobbying register and tighten the rules on party financing in order to strengthen liberal democracy. Malin Björk's (C) motion on regulating lobbyists is rejected by the committee with reference to ongoing government work, which conflicts with this concrete commitment.

citations.quote: Sweden shall become even more transparent. We want to establish an anti-corruption agency, tighten rules against corruption, and introduce a lobbying register.

Political parties are vulnerable to influence and infiltration. The rules on financing of political parties should be tightened and their resilience against external influence and infiltration strengthened.

motivering: The committee rejects motions from SD and V on the right to activity compensation and sickness compensation, with reference to ongoing work. No C motion is identified in this matter, and the election manifesto does not specifically regulate activity/sickness compensation. Based on the party's line of upholding the work-first principle and more flexible sick leave, there is no clear basis to deviate, so the party votes Yes.

citations.quote: The work-first principle must be upheld, and those who are able to work should not live on taxpayers' money.
citations.princip: the work-first principle must be upheld

citations.quote: We want to make sick leave more flexible and improve rehabilitation.

motivering: C's own motion (Lööf et al., motion items 142 and 144) on energy taxes is rejected by the committee, despite the party's clear demand for maximally reduced tax on biofuels. The party maintains its position via the reservation and votes No.

citations.quote: Reduce the tax as much as possible on biofuels blended into petrol and diesel.
The total tax burden must come down during the next parliamentary term.

motivering: V's (the Left Party's) motion concerns restrictions on the ability to evict families with children, which would expand national restrictions on property owners. C's manifesto emphasizes property rights as a fundamental right that should be strengthened. The party's liberal, market-based stance argues against supporting V's restriction motion.

citations.quote: We want to strengthen, among other things, property rights, the prohibition of discrimination, minority protection and the status of minority languages, and give constitutional protection to the right to abortion and reproductive health.

motivering: C's own motion (Martina Johansson et al., motion items 21, 22 and 24) on studies and work within social insurance is rejected by the committee. The party wants to see more flexibility and security in transition and studies while upholding the work-first principle, and therefore votes No to the rejection.

citations.quote: The Swedish labor market needs both more flexibility and more security. Support for transition and further education/training must be improved.
The work-first principle must be upheld, and those who are able to work should not live on taxpayers' money.
citations.princip: the work-first principle must be upheld

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motions on climate adaptation of crisis preparedness (Mikael Larsson et al. (C) claim 6, Annie Lööf et al. (C) claim 25) which the committee majority rejects. The manifesto explicitly demands that civil defence and society's preparedness be strengthened, and climate adaptation is a priority issue. The party supports Reservation 10 and votes No.

citations.quote: Civil defence is also vital. We must strengthen civil defence and society's preparedness for war and crisis.
citations.princip: strengthen civil defence and crisis preparedness

citations.quote: The Centre Party puts the climate first, because the future must be green.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own claims (nos. 26, 35) in the part of the committee report concerning housing issues in elderly care, which the committee rejects. The manifesto states that freedom of choice in care must be defended and that services should be provided close to care recipients. The party should vote No to stand behind Reservation 28 and its own proposals.

citations.quote: We want to defend freedom of choice in care and provide services close to care recipients. Responsibility for healthcare should not be moved from the regions to the state.
citations.princip: freedom of choice and care close to home

citations.quote: We want to shorten queues and create more care places where needed through investments in more nurses and better state support to the regions, adapted to their circumstances and needs.
citations.princip: better quality of healthcare and care

motivering: The Centre Party had its own motion on reviewing the Discrimination Act (Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist et al. (C) claim 12), which the committee rejects. The Centre Party's manifesto demands that more be done against discrimination and that the authorities' work be strengthened. Reservation 18 represents the Centre Party's own position, and the party should vote No.

citations.quote: More must be done against discrimination. We want to strengthen the authorities' work against discrimination and raise compensation for those affected, as well as add sex and disability as grounds for hate crimes.
We are liberals because we believe in individual freedom and the equal worth of all people.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motions on this matter (Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist et al. (C) claims 13 and 14), which the committee proposes to reject. The manifesto commits the party to 'clean up the regulatory swamp for entrepreneurs, large and small.' The party supports its own reservation (alternative A) and votes no to the committee's proposal to reject.

citations.quote: Clean up the regulatory swamp for entrepreneurs, large and small.
It should be easy to start and run a business; it should pay off to take the leap and invest.

motivering: The Social Democrats' motion for an expanded mandate to the National Institute of Economic Research (Konjunkturinstitutet) to analyze companies' pricing implies increased state interference in market pricing. The manifesto emphasizes that Sweden should use freer markets and better competition to curb prices, not state price control. The Centre Party supports the committee's rejection and votes yes.

citations.quote: By creating freer markets and improving competition, we can further curb prices.
citations.princip: market solution versus state price control

citations.quote: Sweden needs more free trade and international cooperation, not protectionism and closed borders.
citations.princip: free market as a basic principle

motivering: The Centre Party's election manifesto explicitly states that it wants to strengthen the status of minority languages, as part of further developing liberal democracy. The Centre Party's own motion on mother tongue and minority languages is among the motions the committee proposes to reject, which speaks in favor of supporting the reservation instead of the rejection. Vote No.

citations.quote: strengthen, among other things, property rights, the prohibition of discrimination, minority protection and the status of minority languages
citations.princip: strengthen the status of minority languages

citations.quote: That is why we should have equitable preschools and schools throughout the country.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own claims (54–56) in the committee report on regulation and control of the haulage industry (åkerinäringen), which the committee rejects. The manifesto demands that expensive and complicated regulations be cleared away for rural industries. Reservation 1 is the only counter-proposal and likely carries the Centre Party's line, which is why the party votes No.

citations.quote: Expensive, complicated and innovation-inhibiting regulations lie like a wet blanket over parts of the countryside. We shall clean up excessive rules and bureaucracy.
It should be easy to start and run a business; it should pay off to take the leap and invest.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own claims (18 and 20) on mineral compensation, which the committee rejects. The manifesto explicitly states that more of the value created from natural resources should remain local, and that compensation for land taken into use should be raised substantially. Reservation 11 carries the Centre Party's line, and the party votes No.

citations.quote: More of the value created from natural resources — for example wind power, hydropower and mines — should remain local.
Likewise, compensation for land taken into use should be paid at a substantially higher amount than today.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motion on the Planning and Building Act (Alireza Akhondi et al. (C) claim 13), which is rejected by the committee. The manifesto demands the clearing away of 'expensive, complicated and innovation-inhibiting regulations' and reform of the shoreline protection (strandskydd). The party supports Reservation 1 and votes No.

citations.quote: Expensive, complicated and innovation-inhibiting regulations lie like a wet blanket over parts of the countryside. We shall clean up excessive rules and bureaucracy.
Shoreline protection (strandskydd) should be reformed so it becomes easier to build and live in rural areas.

motivering: The election manifesto states that culture should be available throughout the country and that the whole country should thrive, from rural areas to cities. The Centre Party's own motion on cinemas in smaller localities is among the motions the committee rejects, which speaks in favor of supporting the reservation rather than the rejection. Vote No.

citations.quote: Providing culture throughout the country is an important starting point for the Centre Party.
The whole country is needed, from suburb to industrial town, from big city to countryside.

motivering: The Left Party's and Social Democrats' motions want to give public housing companies (allmännyttan) special treatment in the procurement regulations, which distorts competition. The Centre Party's manifesto emphasizes that it should be easy to run a business and that the market should function with free competition. With no motions of its own on this matter, the Centre Party supports the committee's rejection and votes yes.

citations.quote: It should be easy to start and run a business; it should pay off to take the leap and invest.
Without small businesses, Sweden grinds to a halt.
citations.princip: the importance of the private market

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motion (Ulrika Liljeberg et al. (C) claim 77) among the procedural law proposals that are rejected. The manifesto states that the rule of law and individual rights must be defended and calls for increased access to legal counsel. With its own claim in the matter, the party supports Reservation 8 and votes No.

citations.quote: The rule of law and the individual's rights vis-à-vis the state must be defended. We therefore say no to stop-and-search zones, collective punishment, reversed burden of proof, anonymous witnesses, preventive wiretapping, and restrictions on freedom of religion.
citations.princip: rule of law and individual rights

citations.quote: Everyone living in Sweden should be able to have their case tried. Processing times for casework and the exercise of authority in courts and government agencies must be shortened, and access to legal counsel must be improved.
citations.princip: right to have one's case tried

motivering: The committee rejects the Left Party's (V) and Social Democrats' (S) motions on improvement and alteration work in rental housing (hyresrätter). The Centre Party's (C) manifesto does not take a specific position on tenants' rights to make alterations, but the party's emphasis on property rights and its opposition to expanded regulation argue against supporting V's and S's reservations. The committee's rejection is consistent with C's liberal view of the housing market.

citations.quote: We want to strengthen, among other things, property rights, the prohibition against discrimination, minority protection and the status of minority languages, and give constitutional protection to the right to abortion and reproductive health.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motion (motion 41 by Daniel Bäckström et al.) on international animal welfare work, which the committee wants to reject. The party's programme advocates sustainable agriculture with biological diversity and an international trade policy geared toward environmental goals. Since Alternative A (Reservation 7) likely reflects the party's own positions, C should vote No.

citations.quote: We will work for more locally grown and climate-smart food and a living, sustainable agriculture that contributes to biological diversity.
Sweden needs an even more competitive agriculture.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motions on this matter (Stina Larsson et al. (C), motions 14, 15 and 17, and Annie Lööf et al. (C), motions 48, 50, 180 and 181) on environmental requirements in public procurement, which the committee proposes to reject. The manifesto states that 'it should cost more to pollute.' The party supports its own reservation (Alternative A) and votes no.

citations.quote: It should cost more to pollute.
citations.princip: environmental price signal, strengthening environmental requirements

citations.quote: Set stricter requirements on working conditions, the environment and climate in trade agreements.

motivering: According to its election manifesto, C wants to strengthen the status of minority languages and give constitutional protection to key rights, including through a constitutional court. C's own motion on national minorities and minority languages is among the rejected proposals, which argues for supporting the reservation. Vote No.

citations.quote: strengthen, among other things, property rights, the prohibition against discrimination, minority protection and the status of minority languages
citations.princip: strengthening the status of minority languages

citations.quote: A constitutional court is important for safeguarding, among other things, these rights.

motivering: The Centre Party has submitted several motions on the circular economy (Stina Larsson et al., motions 1, 3, 5, 6, 74, and Annie Lööf et al., motions 177, 178, 185) which the committee wants to reject. The programme explicitly states that Sweden should become the world's most resource-efficient country and the economy more circular. Alternative A (Reservation 1) reflects these commitments and C should vote No.

citations.quote: Sweden should become the world's most resource-efficient country and the economy more circular. With the right support and simplified regulations, we can recycle and reuse everything from clothing to minerals and metals.

The climate cannot wait for expensive and complicated regulations. It is time to halve the time it takes to get permits for green investments and reform the Environmental Code so that a project's climate benefit is given greater weight in environmental assessments.

motivering: The Centre Party has an explicit commitment to zero tolerance of honour-based oppression and forced marriage. The party is in opposition to a government supported by the Sweden Democrats (SD) and should actively work for concrete legislative measures rather than accepting the committee's reference to 'ongoing work.' The manifesto's priority of zero tolerance toward honour-based oppression and child marriage points toward supporting Reservation 19 instead of the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: No one should be subjected to honour-based oppression in Sweden.
All municipalities should have action plans to prevent men's violence against women, and all schools should have action plans against honour-based oppression.

motivering: The Centre Party's reform agenda for crime prevention focuses on stopping gang recruitment, strengthening the judicial chain, and broadening preventive efforts — not on a separate gender-based action plan for young offenders. The Left Party's motion does not fit within the party's concrete commitments. The committee's reference to ongoing inquiries is consistent with the party's line of constructive, evidence-based reforms.

citations.quote: Society must not give way to the gangs. Defeating them requires better efforts to prevent new recruitment, more resources for the police, prosecutors, courts and the prison and probation service, and stricter punishments.
Sweden needs more police officers, harsher punishments and better preventive efforts — with strong action against gang crime, violence against children and men's violence against women alike.

motivering: The Centre Party has several of its own motions on climate issues in planning (Stina Larsson et al. (C), motions 20, 25, 26, 31, and Alireza Akhondi et al. (C), motions 41-43) which the committee rejects. The manifesto demands that climate benefit be given greater weight in environmental assessments and that permit processes for green investments be halved. The party supports Reservation 15 and votes No.

citations.quote: The climate cannot wait for expensive and complicated regulations. It is time to halve the time it takes to get permits for green investments and reform the Environmental Code so that a project's climate benefit is given greater weight in environmental assessments.
citations.princip: climate benefit in planning and assessment

citations.quote: The Centre Party puts the climate first, because the future must be green.

motivering: The committee rejects the Left Party's (V) and Sweden Democrats' (SD) motions on controls and supervision in the taxi industry; C has no motions of its own in this part. C's focus on regulatory simplification and on not placing new obstacles on businesses argues against supporting additional supervisory rules. C votes Yes and endorses the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Expensive, complicated and innovation-inhibiting regulations lie like a wet blanket over parts of the countryside. We will clear away superfluous rules and bureaucracy.

motivering: SD's motions on the free movement of goods go in a protectionist direction. The manifesto is categorical: 'Sweden needs more free trade and international cooperation, not protectionism and closed borders.' C supports the committee's rejection of SD's trade-restricting proposals and votes yes.

citations.quote: Sweden needs more free trade and international cooperation, not protectionism and closed borders.
Sweden cannot manage without free trade. Open up more markets for Swedish goods and services.

motivering: The Centre Party's gender equality agenda demands concrete steps toward economic equality in working life, including upgrading the status of female-dominated professions. C's own motions on precisely this issue are among those the committee rejects, and the reservation reflects that line. Vote No in support of the reservation.

citations.quote: We want to upgrade the status of female-dominated professions and improve working conditions in the public sector, including through career positions and the right to skills development.
We cannot let gender equality problems continue for another term of office.

motivering: The government's proposal gives the Swedish Tax Agency (Skatteverket) tools to combat fraud in the population register, with built-in privacy safeguards. The manifesto emphasizes that 'the work-first principle must be upheld, and those who can work should not live on taxpayers' money,' which argues for balanced measures against welfare crime. SD's reservation (Alternative A) does not reflect C's line; C votes yes with the committee.

citations.quote: The work-first principle must be upheld, and those who can work should not live on taxpayers' money.
The rule of law and the individual's rights vis-à-vis the state must be defended.

motivering: The Centre Party wants to lead the fight for a gender-equal Sweden and does not accept that gender equality problems are allowed to continue for another electoral term. The party's own motions on the goals of gender equality policy are among those the committee rejects. Vote No in support of the reservation (dissenting opinion).

citations.quote: It is therefore self-evident for the Centre Party that we should lead the fight for a gender-equal Sweden that creates opportunities and justice for everyone.
citations.princip: lead the fight for gender equality

citations.quote: We cannot let the gender equality problems continue for another electoral term.

motivering: The Centre Party's motion (Vilhelmsson et al.) on the VAT exemption for non-profit associations' internal services is rejected together with the motions of the Green Party and the Left Party, a broad cross-opposition dissatisfaction. The party strongly upholds the conditions of civil society, including the sports movement and free popular education (folkbildning), and votes No in support of the joint reservation (dissenting opinion).

citations.quote: The sports movement and Sweden's popular movements make valuable contributions to building trust and community.
Independent popular education (folkbildning) is of very great importance in times when democratic values are being questioned.

motivering: The election manifesto lacks a rental-housing policy of its own, but the party's market-liberal line advocates freer markets rather than further regulation. Without a clear stance of its own on precisely these motions, the Centre Party follows the committee's rejection. Vote Yes.

citations.quote: By creating freer markets and improving competition, we can dampen prices further.

motivering: The election manifesto does not address Middle East policy specifically. The Centre Party's own motion (Kerstin Lundgren et al., item 62) is nevertheless among the rejected proposals, and the party generally advocates active foreign-policy leadership rather than simply following the government's line. This weakly suggests No, but the basis is uncertain.

citations.quote: Sweden also needs political leadership that sees the rest of the world as an opportunity, not as a threat
Around the world a struggle is under way between supporters of liberal democracy and authoritarian forces. That struggle we must win.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motion (Malin Björk et al. (C), item 4) on an inquiry into the opposition's standing, which the committee proposes to reject. The manifesto explicitly commits to 'protect the opposition's standing in the Riksdag'. The party supports its reservation (alternative A) and votes No.

citations.quote: We want to make it harder to change the constitution, protect the opposition's standing in the Riksdag, and strengthen the independence of the courts.
Liberal democracy must never be taken for granted. It must be nurtured, safeguarded and further developed — today and for future generations.

motivering: The committee rejects the Social Democrats' and the Green Party's motions on other compensation issues in mineral policy; the Centre Party has no motions of its own here. The Centre Party's manifesto supports domestic mineral extraction and Sweden taking responsibility for its resources, which points toward not accepting the Social Democrats' and the Green Party's alternative arrangements. The Centre Party votes Yes.

citations.quote: It is better for Sweden to take responsibility and extract more minerals and metals instead of continuing to import them from countries with a larger climate footprint and worse working conditions.
More of the value created from natural resources — for example wind power, hydropower and mines — should stay local.

motivering: The Centre Party is pursuing items 75-76 (Stina Larsson et al.) on the reuse and recycling of innovation-critical materials. The programme explicitly advocates that Sweden take responsibility for domestic extraction and recycling of metals and minerals in order to reduce the climate footprint and import dependence. The committee rejects the Centre Party's motion; the Centre Party should vote No and support Reservation 10 (dissenting opinion).

citations.quote: It is better for Sweden to take responsibility and extract more minerals and metals instead of continuing to import them from countries with a larger climate footprint and worse working conditions.
citations.princip: Responsible domestic extraction of critical materials

citations.quote: Sweden shall become the world's most resource-efficient country and the economy more circular. With the right support and simplified rules we can recycle and reuse everything from clothes to minerals and metals.
citations.princip: Circular recycling of minerals and metals

motivering: No Centre Party motion is among the rejected proposals on language issues in public service broadcasting and film, and the election manifesto does not address demands on language content specifically. The manifesto does, however, emphasize that independent public service broadcasting should be defended, which argues against new political mandates in this area. Vote Yes with the committee.

citations.quote: Freedom of the press shall be protected and independent public service broadcasting defended.
Diverse, independent and viable media coverage throughout the country is crucial for democracy.

motivering: No Centre Party motions are included in this sub-matter; it is exclusively the Left Party's motions (Maj Karlsson et al. (V), items 22 and 23) that are being examined. Without a motion of its own and without a reservation, the Centre Party accepts the committee's reference to ongoing work; the party's basic support for the rights of people with disabilities is not sufficient on its own to justify approving the Left Party's specific claims.

citations.quote: If you have a disability, you should get the support you need, and the state should take greater responsibility for making LSS (the Act on Support and Service for Persons with Certain Functional Impairments) work.

motivering: The Centre Party has no motions of its own in this vote. The rejected motions belong to the Sweden Democrats (Tobias Andersson) and the Social Democrats (Fredrik Olovsson). The party categorically rejects cooperation with the Sweden Democrats, and without a stance of its own on the substantive issue, it follows naturally that it supports the committee's rejection of the Sweden Democrats' and the Social Democrats' claims.

citations.quote: The Centre Party is now the only centre-right party that will not cooperate with the Sweden Democrats or give them power over how Sweden is to be governed.
citations.princip: no cooperation with the Sweden Democrats

citations.quote: Our fundamental rights must not be taken for granted. We want to strengthen, among other things, property rights

motivering: The Centre Party has no motion of its own in this vote on zoo operations, and the election manifesto lacks specific positions on zoo regulation. The committee refers to ongoing international work. Reservation 33 (dissenting opinion) is likely from the Sweden Democrats or the Green Party and does not reflect the Centre Party's documented priorities. The Centre Party supports the committee's position.

citations.quote: We shall work for more locally grown and climate-smart food and a living, sustainable agriculture that contributes to biological diversity.

motivering: The Centre Party's own motion (Lööf et al., items 145 and 149) on migration and asylum policy is rejected by the committee. The party pursues an open line that safeguards labour immigration and rapid integration for newcomers, and votes No in support of its reservation (dissenting opinion).

citations.quote: Safeguard labour immigration. In order for Swedish companies to be able to compete, they must be able to quickly find, recruit and hire the right skills.
Create an intensive year for faster integration. Those who are granted a residence permit should be quickly integrated and given the opportunity to support themselves.

motivering: The election manifesto does not specifically address firearms licensing. The party generally supports more resources for the justice system but has no position of its own on this particular detail, so C reasonably aligns with the committee's rejection, citing ongoing investigative work. Vote Yes.

citations.quote: better efforts are needed to prevent new recruitment, more resources for the police, prosecutors, courts and the prison and probation service, and harsher penalties

motivering: C's own motion on industry schools (branschskolor) (item 67) is the only motion rejected under this point, which makes it highly likely that the reservation reflects C's position. The election manifesto wants vocational education to be based on the needs of the labor market and for it to become easier to hire students in vocational programs. Vote No.

citations.quote: The education system needs to be based, to a considerably greater extent, on the needs of the labor market.
citations.princip: vocational education based on labor market needs

citations.quote: Make it easier to hire students in vocational programs as apprentices by increasing compensation for companies' costs associated with the training.
citations.princip: strengthened apprenticeship training in vocational programs

motivering: The motion being rejected on digitizing the film heritage comes solely from the Left Party; C has no motion of its own on the issue and the election manifesto does not mention the film heritage. C's principle of an arm's-length distance in cultural policy argues against new political mandates in this area. Vote Yes with the committee.

citations.quote: Politics should contribute good conditions but keep an arm's-length distance.

motivering: Gambling policy and ANDTS issues (alcohol, narcotics, doping, tobacco and gambling) are not specifically covered by C's manifesto. SD's motions (Linda Lindberg et al.) are among those the committee rejects, and C does not cooperate with SD. In the absence of its own motions or a reservation in the matter, C supports the committee's rejection and votes yes.

citations.quote: The Centre Party is now the only centre-right party that will not cooperate with the Sweden Democrats or give them power over how Sweden is to be governed.
The Centre Party will always defend your right to shape your own life.
citations.princip: individual freedom as a founding principle

motivering: No C proposal is identified among the rejected motions on family-reunification immigration; only V's motion is named. The election manifesto does not specifically address family-reunification immigration. In the absence of any other stated C position, the party votes Yes in line with the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: Regardless of who you are or where you come from, you should have the freedom and the opportunity to decide for yourself where you are heading.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motion on the crisis preparedness system (Mikael Larsson et al., C, item 8) which the committee majority rejects. The manifesto demands that civil defense and society's preparedness be strengthened in light of Russia's invasion and the risk of war. The party supports Reservation 1 and votes No.

citations.quote: Civil defense too is vital. We must strengthen civil defense and society's preparedness for war and crisis.
citations.princip: strengthen civil defense and crisis preparedness

citations.quote: Sweden must be defended. Russia's invasion in violation of international law has shown that we cannot rule out Sweden being drawn into war. Ukraine's heroic defense of its country's freedom and survival has shown that it is possible to stand up to despots. The Centre Party wants to strengthen the armed forces, reinforce Sweden's civil preparedness, and complete Sweden's accession to NATO.
citations.princip: defense preparedness against the threat of invasion

motivering: C has submitted several motions (Annie Lööf, item 68; Helena Vilhelmsson, items 1 and 4) in this committee report that the committee rejects. Reservation 8 likely represents C's own position on the issues. The manifesto's principle that the individual's rights against the state must be defended leads C to support its reservation and vote No.

citations.quote: The rule of law and the individual's rights against the state must be defended. We therefore say no to stop-and-search zones, collective punishment, reversed burden of proof, anonymous witnesses, preventive wiretapping, and restrictions on freedom of religion.
citations.princip: the individual's rights against the state

citations.quote: Sweden should become even more transparent. We want to establish an anti-corruption authority, tighten rules against corruption, and introduce a lobbying register.

motivering: The vote concerns the rejection of the Left Party's motion on incitement against an ethnic or national group (hets mot folkgrupp). C has no motion of its own on this matter, and the committee refers to ongoing work. C's manifesto supports anti-discrimination efforts but makes no specific commitment regarding V's item 2 in particular. C accepts the committee's assessment that the issues are under preparation.

citations.quote: More must be done against discrimination. We want to strengthen authorities' work against discrimination and increase compensation for those affected
we defend openness, democracy and the principle of the equal value of all people
citations.princip: equal value of all people and democracy

motivering: C's own motion (Lööf et al., item 128) on VAT rates is rejected by the committee. The party wants to lower the overall tax burden and build a more resource-efficient, circular economy, and therefore votes No to the rejection.

citations.quote: The overall tax burden must come down during the next parliamentary term.
Sweden should become the world's most resource-efficient country and the economy more circular.

motivering: C's own motion (Malin Björk et al., items 13 and 16) on party financing is among the proposals rejected. The election manifesto explicitly wants to tighten the rules on party financing and strengthen parties' resilience against outside influence and infiltration. Vote No to support the reservation.

citations.quote: The rules for financing of political parties should be tightened and their resilience against outside influence and infiltration strengthened.
We want to establish an anti-corruption authority, tighten rules against corruption, and introduce a lobbying register.

motivering: The committee rejects V's and S's motions on working environment issues within the haulage and taxi industries; C has no motions of its own in this part. The manifesto emphasizes labor market flexibility rather than further regulation. C supports the committee's position and votes Yes.

citations.quote: The Swedish labor market needs both more flexibility and more security. Support for transition and further training must be improved.

motivering: C has a motion (Malin Björk et al., item 22) on state administration and statistics that the committee rejects. The manifesto emphasizes transparency and decentralization in public administration. C likely supports its reservation (Reservation 3) for a more efficient and more open state administration and votes No.

citations.quote: Sweden should become even more transparent. We want to establish an anti-corruption authority, tighten rules against corruption, and introduce a lobbying register.
Decentralize more. People should get to decide more for themselves, and political decisions should be made close to those affected.

motivering: C's own motion 25 (Kerstin Lundgren et al.) is among the motions the committee wants to reject. C cannot vote to reject its own motion. C is assumed to have a reservation in the committee (reservation 5 or another) that reflects motion 25. C's liberal-democratic profile supports international cooperation and multilateral aid.

citations.quote: Sweden cannot manage without free trade. Open up more markets for Swedish goods and services.
liberal democracy is threatened. We must never take it for granted or underestimate its opponents.
citations.princip: support for the liberal world order

motivering: The rejected motions belong to SD (Per Söderlund, motions 28 and 32) concerning coordination numbers. Reservation 9 represents SD's position, presumably more restrictive toward immigrants. C's manifesto emphasizes safeguarding labor immigration and actively distances itself from SD's nationalist immigration policy. C supports the committee's rejection of SD's motions.

citations.quote: Safeguard labor immigration. For Swedish companies to be able to compete, they must be able to quickly find, recruit and hire the right expertise. Let labor migrants count their study time in Sweden when applying for permanent residence permits.
It is possible to build coalitions that stem neither from the xenophobic right's nationalism nor the socialist left's stifling collectivism.

motivering: Three Centerpartiet motions on the right to a victim's counsel (målsägandebiträde) (Ulrika Liljeberg et al., C, motions 46 and 22, Annie Lööf et al., C, motion 67) are rejected by the committee. The manifesto states that the ability to litigate should not be 'a right reserved for those with high income' and that individuals should be able to get compensation for legal representation. The party supports Reservation 13 and votes No.

citations.quote: The ability to litigate against the state or a municipality, when one has good reason to have one's case tried, should not, in a liberal democracy, be a right reserved for those with high income. We want to create a possibility for individuals to obtain compensation for legal representation in administrative matters when they had reason to have their case tried.
citations.princip: right to legal aid regardless of income

citations.quote: Everyone living in Sweden should be able to have their case tried. Processing times for case handling and administrative decisions in courts and authorities must be shortened and access to legal representation improved.

motivering: Centerpartiet is pursuing motions 1-4 and 32 (Muharrem Demirok et al.) on a new resource allocation system for the school voucher (skolpengen) which the committee wants to reject. The program stipulates that the school voucher should be adapted to pupils' circumstances and needs, in line with the Swedish National Audit Office's recommendations. C should vote No to support its reservation.

citations.quote: The school voucher should be adapted to the responsibilities of the principal organizers and to pupils' circumstances and needs.
Among other things, we want to see high quality requirements for continued operation and profit distribution, and we want to tighten supervision of schools and their owners.
citations.princip: quality requirements and an equitable school system

motivering: Centerpartiet wants to lead Sweden toward an end to men's violence against women and has this as one of its main reform priorities. A zero vision against violence in close relationships, which the committee proposes as a tillkännagivande (formal request to the government), is directly in line with this commitment. Vote Yes.

citations.quote: We shall lead Sweden toward an end to men's violence against women. Men who hit should not get away with it.
Stop men's violence against women and honor-related oppression

motivering: The motion is from the Social Democrats (Anna-Caren Sätherberg). C has not submitted its own motion on this matter. The committee assesses that Sweden already conducts clear chemicals work and that ongoing work covers the issues. C has no specific commitment on legislation on hormone-disrupting substances specifically and accepts the committee's assessment.

citations.quote: For Centerpartiet, care for the environment and climate is a central part of politics, never a lower priority or a special interest.
citations.princip: environment and climate as core policy

citations.quote: Sweden shall become the world's most resource-efficient country and the economy more circular.

motivering: The election manifesto does not address a reflection period (betänketid) for divorce. The party's general principle on the individual's right to shape their own life gives no clear direction on this detailed issue, and the government is already set to map the property division problem. C therefore aligns with the committee's rejection. Vote Yes.

citations.quote: Centerpartiet will always defend your right to shape your own life.

motivering: Centerpartiet wants to strengthen the crime victim perspective and ensure that those subjected to crime receive redress and better support. Giving children exploited in child pornography formal crime-victim status is in line with this commitment rather than the committee's rejection. Vote No in support of the reservation.

citations.quote: The crime victim perspective must be strengthened. Those subjected to crime should receive redress and better support.

motivering: Centerpartiet wants to strengthen the crime victim perspective in general but has no stated demand for an entirely new, dedicated crime victims act. The committee refers to ongoing reform work, which C reasonably trusts in the absence of its own position on this specific issue. Vote Yes.

citations.quote: The crime victim perspective must be strengthened. Those subjected to crime should receive redress and better support.

motivering: Centerpartiet has its own motions (Niels Paarup-Petersen et al., motions 10, 31-33, 35, 37-39) on copyright which the committee wants to reject. The party safeguards artistic and academic freedom as well as property rights as a basis for intellectual property protection. C should vote No and pursue its reservation.

citations.quote: Academic and artistic freedom, as well as free culture, are cornerstones of a vital civil society.
Culture shall be free and independent, sport equitable and inclusive.

motivering: Centerpartiet has five of its own motions on the housing market (Alireza Akhondi et al., C, motions 1, 6, 7, 11 and 13) which the committee rejects. The manifesto demands the abolition of the enhanced amortization requirement and no measures that 'make housing more expensive.' The party supports Reservation 1 and votes No.

citations.quote: The enhanced amortization requirement — forced saving for those with the lowest incomes — should be abolished now that interest rates are normalizing.
We will not participate in any tax increases that harm jobs, personal savings, or make housing more expensive.
citations.princip: no measures that raise housing costs

motivering: The election manifesto does not specifically address courts' competence in custody cases. The committee refers to ongoing work, which is close to Centerpartiet's general line on swift and legally secure case processing. Without its own stated position on this particular, narrow issue, the party votes with the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: Processing times for case handling and administrative decisions in courts and authorities must be shortened and access to legal representation improved.

motivering: Among the motions that the committee proposes to reject are the Centre Party's own motions (Lööf motion 29, Lindahl motion 20) concerning the municipal economic equalization system, which aims to give rural areas a fairer share of public revenue. The party maintains its own position and therefore votes No to the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Those who live in rural areas but pay for things that the public sector covers in urban areas should be compensated.
Rural areas should get their fair share of public services and revenue

motivering: Several Centre Party motions (Annie Lööf, Ulrika Heie, Stina Larsson, Alireza Akhondi) on the green tax deduction and green tax shift are among those rejected. The green deduction (grönt avdrag) is an explicit commitment in the election manifesto to lower households' costs for energy efficiency improvements and solar panels. C votes No to uphold its own reserved position.

citations.quote: We can solve this by broadening and scaling up the green deduction and making it easier to install solar panels on multi-family buildings.
with a green deduction for energy efficiency improvements at home, we can lower households' electricity costs
citations.princip: lower household costs via the green deduction

motivering: The committee's proposal approves that authorities should work in a more advisory and solution-oriented way in permit processes. This directly matches the Centre Party's manifesto demand for halved permit processing times and a reformed Environmental Code (miljöbalken) to enable the green transition. C votes Yes for a more efficient permit process.

citations.quote: It is time to halve the time it takes to obtain permits for green investments and reform the Environmental Code so that a project's climate benefit is given greater weight in environmental review.
To manage the green transition, we must make use of Sweden's natural resources.

motivering: C has an explicit election manifesto pledge to allow farm-gate sales (gårdsförsäljning) of alcohol to strengthen rural tourism. C's motion (Niels Paarup-Petersen et al.) on alcohol legislation is rejected by the committee. C supports its own reservation (Reservation 4) and votes No in order to realize this clear commitment.

citations.quote: It is unreasonable that local producers of alcoholic beverages cannot sell their products to visitors. Allow farm-gate sales of alcohol to strengthen the tourism industry and develop rural areas.

Simplified regulations, tax cuts, farm-gate sales of alcohol, and more growth-friendly shoreline protection rules are just some of the reforms that must be put in place to strengthen rural competitiveness and increase people's freedom and self-determination.

motivering: C's own motions do not appear in this particular sub-matter concerning regulation via detailed development plans (detaljplan). The named motions include the Left Party's (V) motions (items 12-13), which likely concern tightened planning regulation, a direction that conflicts with C's demand for simplified regulation and shortened permit processes. The committee's reference to ongoing work is acceptable when V's and the rest of the left's regulatory ambitions are rejected; C supports the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: The climate cannot wait for expensive and complicated regulations. It is time to halve the time it takes to obtain permits for green investments and reform the Environmental Code so that a project's climate benefit is given greater weight in environmental review.
citations.princip: regulatory simplification in the planning process

citations.quote: Expensive, complicated, and innovation-inhibiting regulations lie like a wet blanket over parts of rural areas. We will clear away excessive rules and bureaucracy.

motivering: The committee rejects the Social Democrats' (S) motion on Natura 2000 permits in mineral policy; C has no motions of its own here. C's manifesto emphasizes that Sweden should extract more minerals and metals for the green transition, and S's motions are assessed as pointing toward stricter requirements that would hinder this. C votes Yes.

citations.quote: It is better for Sweden to take responsibility and extract more minerals and metals instead of continuing to import them from countries with a larger climate footprint and worse working conditions.
Sweden's natural environment shall be cared for and biodiversity developed.

motivering: The election manifesto does not specifically take a position on youth monitoring as a sanction for young offenders. The committee refers to ongoing investigative work, and without a stated position of its own on this particular issue, the party follows the committee's line rather than the Sweden Democrats' (SD) motion.

citations.quote: Society must not yield to the gangs. To defeat them requires better efforts to prevent recruitment, more resources for the police, prosecutors, courts and the prison and probation service, and stricter punishments.

motivering: Among the rejected motions is the Centre Party's own motion (Bäckström motion 18) on supervision of shooting ranges and firearms licenses, which is consistent with the party's line of clearing away complicated regulations that affect rural areas. The party maintains its own position and votes No to the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Expensive, complicated, and innovation-inhibiting regulations lie like a wet blanket over parts of rural areas. We will clear away excessive rules and bureaucracy.

motivering: The committee proposes rejecting several public health motions, including the Centre Party's own motions (Jonsson et al. 12, 14, 19; Deremar 22). This is in line with the party's focus on preventive health work and care close to people, so the party maintains its line and votes No.

citations.quote: Do more to prevent, counteract, and rehabilitate stress-related mental ill-health.
Close and secure healthcare and social care throughout the country.

motivering: C has seven motions on sustainable business and free trade rejected (Kerstin Lundgren, Stina Larsson, Annie Lööf, Malin Björk). The manifesto demands free trade with high environmental and climate requirements in trade agreements. C supports its own reservation (Reservation 25) on responsible and sustainable trade policy and votes No.

citations.quote: Sweden cannot manage without free trade. Open up more markets for Swedish goods and services. Set stricter requirements on working conditions, the environment, and climate in trade agreements.
We shall use trade policy to cut fossil subsidies around the world and pressure major emitters such as China to shut down their coal power plants.

motivering: C's two own motions (Heie et al. and Lööf et al.) on energy tax on electric public transport are rejected by the committee. The party wants to make emission-free public transport smoother and cheaper, in line with the motto that it should be easy to do the right thing, and votes No to the rejection.

citations.quote: Emission-free transport, bicycles, electric cars, and public transport shall become smoother and more attractive.
It should be easy to do the right thing in everyday life.
citations.princip: cheap to do the right thing

motivering: The Centre Party has no identifiable motion of its own in this vote on mink farming, and the election manifesto lacks a specific position on mink breeding. The committee rejects motions from the Green Party (MP), the Sweden Democrats (SD), the Left Party (V), and the Social Democrats (S). Reservation 16 is likely from one of these parties and does not reflect C's own commitments. C should vote Yes with the committee.

citations.quote: Sweden needs an even more competitive agricultural sector. A long-term sustainable food supply with increased security of supply and increased food production requires simplified regulations and tax cuts

motivering: The motion on a raised basic tax allowance comes from the Left Party (Ida Gabrielsson). C does support lower taxes for low-income earners but prefers the earned-income tax credit (jobbskatteavdraget) — tied to work — over a general basic allowance that does not strengthen the incentive to move from benefits to work. C has no motion of its own and accepts the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: it should pay off more to move from benefits to work,
That is why we want to cut taxes, especially for those with lower incomes and for the important small businesses.

motivering: The committee's proposal means that the Riksdag approves Sweden's accession to NATO and the necessary legislative amendments, which is an explicit top priority in the Centre Party's manifesto. The party demands that Sweden 'complete its entry into NATO' and strengthen collective defence capability. Voting Yes is directly in line with the party's most central security-policy commitment.

citations.quote: The Centre Party wants to rearm the defence forces, strengthen Sweden's civil preparedness, and complete the entry into NATO.
Sweden needs to spend two percent of GDP on defence as soon as practically possible and join NATO.
citations.princip: NATO accession as a defence priority

motivering: All the named motions on housing supply originate from MP, V and S and point toward state-directed housing solutions, increased regulation and municipal quota systems — lines that conflict with C's market-based and cost-conscious housing policy. C supports the committee's rejection of these left-leaning proposals.

citations.quote: We will not participate in any tax increases that harm jobs, personal savings, or make housing more expensive.
The overall tax burden must come down in the next term of office.
citations.princip: lower tax burden and market freedoms

motivering: The motion being rejected is the Centre Party's own claim (Jonsson, claim 9) on sexual and reproductive health and rights, an area where the party explicitly wants to give constitutional protection to the right to abortion and reproductive health. The party maintains its own line and votes no to the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: give constitutional protection to the right to abortion and reproductive health

motivering: C's motion (Ulrika Liljeberg et al., claim 21) on information exchange between authorities and privacy is rejected by the committee. The manifesto states that the individual's rights against the state must be defended and that preventive wiretapping should be rejected. C supports its reservation (Reservation 1) on strengthened privacy protection and votes No.

citations.quote: The rule of law and the individual's rights vis-à-vis the state must be defended. We therefore say no to search zones, collective punishment, reversed burden of proof, anonymous witnesses, preventive wiretapping, and restrictions on freedom of religion.
citations.princip: the individual's rights against the state

citations.quote: Sweden should become even more transparent. We want to establish an anti-corruption authority, tighten rules against corruption, and introduce a lobbying register.
citations.princip: transparency but not abuse of power

motivering: The committee proposes rejecting several rental-housing motions, including the Centre Party's own claim (Akhondi, claims 3-4). This is in line with the party's market-liberal stance, and the party maintains its own position by voting no to the rejection.

citations.quote: By creating freer markets and improving competition, we can further dampen prices.

motivering: The Centre Party's own motions on protection for vulnerable women in migration cases are rejected by the committee with reference to existing rules. The party's manifesto pushes hard to stop men's violence against women and to strengthen support for crime victims, which argues for sticking to the party's own line via the reservation rather than accepting the rejection.

citations.quote: We shall lead Sweden toward an end to men's violence against women. Men who hit should not get away with it.
It is also important that crime victims receive better support and that after-violence effects are combated.

motivering: The Centre Party has several of its own claims (Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist et al. and Niels Paarup-Petersen et al.) on regulatory simplification for businesses that the committee now wants to reject. Regulatory simplification is a core commitment in the election manifesto — the party actively wants to clear away complicated regulatory frameworks. C should vote No.

citations.quote: Expensive, complicated and innovation-inhibiting regulatory frameworks lie like a wet blanket over parts of the countryside. We shall clear away excessive rules and bureaucracy.
Clear out the regulatory swamp for entrepreneurs, large and small. We want to introduce a new and simplified business form for micro-enterprises, so that more people dare to try running a business.

motivering: Five motions by Annie Lööf et al. (C) on climate tariffs and trade in climate-smart goods are rejected. The manifesto demands that trade policy be used to cut fossil subsidies and impose strict climate requirements in trade agreements. C supports its reservation (Reservation 11) on a climate-ambitious trade policy and votes No.

citations.quote: We shall use trade policy to cut fossil subsidies around the world and pressure major emitters like China to shut down their coal power plants.
Impose tougher requirements on labour conditions, environment and climate in trade agreements.
The EU's emissions trading system is among the most effective tools we have, and we want to make it even more ambitious and open it up to more countries that want to join.

motivering: C's motions (Martina Johansson, claim 24, Annie Lööf, claim 94) on registering children at two addresses in the population register are rejected. The manifesto emphasizes individuals' right to shape their own lives and families' freedom. The ability to register a child at both parents' addresses in shared custody strengthens families' autonomy. C supports its reservation (Reservation 5) and votes No.

citations.quote: The Centre Party will always defend your right to shape your own life. Regardless of who you are or where you come from, you should have the freedom and the ability to decide for yourself where you are headed.

We want to make preschool and after-school activities accessible to everyone, without these costs falling on the municipalities, in order to facilitate integration, strengthen equality, and give every child a good start in life.

motivering: The motion on flag-flying rules was submitted by SD. The Centre Party has clearly stated that it will not cooperate with SD or give them power. The committee's proposal to reject the motion is in line with this basic principle. Specific rules on flag-flying are not directly covered by the documents, but the rejection of SD's political agenda is the load-bearing factor.

citations.quote: The Centre Party is now the only centre-right party that will not cooperate with the Sweden Democrats or give them power over how Sweden is to be governed. We stand firm on that.
In a stormy political climate we stand firm in our values. When others pit person against person, group against group, we defend openness, democracy and the principle of equal worth for all.

motivering: The election manifesto does not address adoption issues specifically, and the motion being rejected (Westerlund, MP) is not the Centre Party's own. Without a clear position of its own on this particular issue, the party follows the committee's proposal to reject it.

citations.quote: We must continue the work for a Sweden where no one is disadvantaged because of gender, origin or disability

motivering: The committee rejects C's own motion (Daniel Bäckström et al., C, motion 1) on safeguarding Swedish hunting and wildlife management. The reservation (Alternative A: Reservation 18) likely represents C's own proposal for strengthened local influence and voluntariness in wildlife management. C votes No in order to uphold its position.
