citations.quote: Sweden's nature must be cared for and biodiversity developed. More must be done to restore wetlands, combat invasive species, and make it easier for landowners to contribute, since voluntariness and property rights are the foundation of better nature conservation.
citations.princip: voluntariness and property rights in nature conservation

citations.quote: Expensive, complicated, and innovation-inhibiting regulations lie like a wet blanket over parts of the countryside. We will clear away superfluous rules and bureaucracy.

motivering: Among the rejected motions is one from the Sweden Democrats (Tobias Andersson, motion 2). C has no own motion identified in this matter and, as a matter of principle, does not cooperate with SD. Without knowledge of reservation 24's sponsor, a No risks implying support for an SD position, which C's document explicitly rules out.

citations.quote: The Centre Party is now the only centre-right party that will not cooperate with the Sweden Democrats or give them power over how Sweden is to be governed.
We will not participate in any tax increases that harm jobs, personal savings, or make housing more expensive.

motivering: S's specific motion on the permit requirement for municipalities in a procedural-law context is not directly covered by C's manifesto. C's fundamental position of safeguarding the rule of law and the rights of the individual vis-à-vis public authorities provides no support for granting municipalities expanded powers without clear justification. The committee's rejection, with reference to ongoing work, is accepted.

citations.quote: The rule of law and the rights of the individual vis-à-vis the state must be defended. We therefore say no to stop-and-search zones, collective punishment, reversed burden of proof, anonymous witnesses, preventive surveillance, and restrictions on freedom of religion.
citations.princip: the rule of law's protection against state overreach

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motions (nos. 23, 28) in the part of the committee report concerning health-preventive work in elderly care, which the committee rejects. The manifesto emphasizes that preventive measures against mental ill health should be implemented and rehabilitation strengthened. The party should vote No to support reservation 39 and its own proposals.

citations.quote: Do more to prevent, counteract, and rehabilitate stress-related mental ill health. We want to make sick leave more flexible and improve rehabilitation.
We want to defend freedom of choice in healthcare and care services and operate services close to care recipients. Responsibility for healthcare should not be moved from the regions to the state.
citations.princip: care that is close and equitable

motivering: The committee rejects the Left Party's motion on a so-called class-based voucher (klasspeng). A class-based voucher undermines the individual free school choice that the Centre Party explicitly upholds. Reservation 3 is the Left Party's reservation, and C should not support the Left Party's school policy. C votes Yes with the committee.

citations.quote: To achieve that, we must safeguard and further develop free school choice, and address the shortcomings that exist.
The school voucher should be adapted to the responsibilities of school providers and the circumstances and needs of students.

motivering: The matter concerns the Centre Party's own motion for more prison and remand places, which the committee wants to reject. The party's program explicitly calls for more resources for the correctional service and a tougher stance against crime, which argues for standing firm on its own position in the reservation. No to the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: more resources for the police, prosecutors, courts, and the correctional service, and stricter penalties
citations.princip: more resources for the correctional service

citations.quote: Sweden needs more police officers, tougher penalties, and better preventive measures

motivering: The committee rejects C's own motions on building-permit-exempt measures (Alireza Akhondi et al., C, motions 20 and 30, and Annie Lööf et al., C, motion 147). C's manifesto calls for a simpler and cheaper process for installing solar panels and charging infrastructure without bureaucratic obstacles. The reservation (Alternative A: Reservation 30) likely represents C's own proposal, which is why C votes No.

citations.quote: It should be easy and cheap to install solar panels, build charging for electric cars, and reduce energy use at home — whether you live in a house or an apartment.

The climate cannot wait for expensive and complicated regulations. It is time to halve the time it takes to obtain permits for green investments and reform the Environmental Code so that a project's climate benefit is given greater weight in the environmental assessment.
citations.princip: regulatory simplification for the green transition

motivering: The Centre Party is pursuing motion 18 (Stina Larsson et al.) on pastures, grazing land, and hay meadows, which the committee wants to reject. The program advocates a living, sustainable agriculture that contributes to biodiversity and a competitive farming sector. Reservation 29 likely reflects C's own positions, and the party should vote No.

citations.quote: We will work for more locally grown and climate-smart food and a living, sustainable agriculture that contributes to biodiversity.

Sweden needs an even more competitive agricultural sector. A long-term sustainable food supply with increased security of supply and increased food production requires regulatory simplifications and tax cuts, including a substantial agricultural tax deduction and a biofuel premium that makes sustainable farming more profitable.

motivering: Catarina Deremar's (C) motion on social security systems for cultural entrepreneurs is rejected with reference to ongoing work. The Centre Party wants to reform the social security systems so that more people, including entrepreneurs, get better conditions, and works to make it pay to run a business, which argues for supporting the reservation rather than the rejection.

citations.quote: We want to reform the social security system so that more women can pursue entrepreneurship
citations.princip: reformed social security system for entrepreneurs

citations.quote: Cut taxes on work and entrepreneurship, especially for small businesses and sole proprietors. It should pay to run a business and create jobs.

motivering: The committee rejects a large number of C motions on aid priorities (Kerstin Lundgren et al., motions 2–4, 6, 10, 12–20 and others, and Annie Lööf et al., motions 17–21). C's strong commitment to global democracy and liberal values is a central aid priority in the manifesto. The reservation (Alternative A: Reservation 6) likely represents C's own aid positions, which is why C votes No.

citations.quote: Around the world, a struggle is underway between supporters of liberal democracy and authoritarian forces. We must win it.
We will use trade policy to cut fossil fuel subsidies around the world and pressure major emitters such as China to shut down their coal power plants.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motion (Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist, motion 8) on impact assessments, which the committee wants to reject. Strengthened requirements for impact analysis when introducing new rules is a tool for reducing the regulatory burden the party consistently criticizes. C should vote No.

citations.quote: Expensive, complicated, and innovation-inhibiting regulations lie like a wet blanket over parts of the countryside. We will clear away superfluous rules and bureaucracy.
Clean up the regulatory jungle for entrepreneurs, large and small.

motivering: The committee rejects C's own motion on lead ammunition (Daniel Bäckström et al., C, motion 19). C's position balances nature conservation with voluntariness and property rights, and the reservation (Alternative A: Reservation 13) likely represents C's stance on how the lead ammunition issue should be handled with regard to the interests of hunting and landowners. C votes No.

citations.quote: Sweden's nature must be cared for and biodiversity developed. More must be done to restore wetlands, combat invasive species, and make it easier for landowners to contribute, since voluntariness and property rights are the foundation of better nature conservation.
citations.princip: voluntariness and property rights in nature conservation

motivering: The question concerns ownership forms for the Prison and Probation Service's (Kriminalvården) premises, a technical issue raised by the Sweden Democrats (SD) that is not addressed in the Centre Party's documents. The party's program instead emphasizes resources for the Prison and Probation Service's operations and responsible management of tax funds, without specifying any particular ownership form. Without a position of its own, the party follows the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Politics should manage taxpayers' money responsibly.
more resources for the police, prosecutors, courts and the Prison and Probation Service, and stricter sentences
citations.princip: resources for the Prison and Probation Service

motivering: The Centre Party's own motion by Helena Lindahl et al. (C), item 23, on the earned income tax credit (jobbskatteavdrag) and regional tax reduction is among those rejected. The earned income tax credit is a central commitment in the Centre Party's reform agenda to make work pay. C votes No in order to uphold its own reserved position and avoid voting against its own motion.

citations.quote: Cut taxes on work and enterprise, especially for small businesses and the self-employed. It should pay to run a business and create jobs.
it should pay more to move from benefits to work, and more people with shorter education and less experience should have the chance to get entry-level jobs.
citations.princip: earned income tax credit and work incentives

motivering: Several Centre Party members (Bäckström, Johansson) have submitted broad motions on social security systems for business owners, which are rejected with reference to ongoing work. The party wants to see a labor market with more security and better transition support, which provides grounds for not accepting the rejection but instead supporting the reservation.

citations.quote: The Swedish labor market needs both more flexibility and more security. Support for transition and further education/training must improve.
citations.princip: security and transition support for business owners

citations.quote: We want to reform the social security system so that more women can pursue entrepreneurship
citations.princip: reformed social security system for entrepreneurs

motivering: Several Centre Party motions by Ulrika Liljeberg and Annie Lööf on offenses involving violation of personal integrity (fridskränkningsbrott) and the criminalization of controlling behavior are among those rejected. These issues are an explicit priority area in the Centre Party's election manifesto. C votes No in order to uphold its commitments to stricter legislation against gross violation of integrity and controlling behavior.

citations.quote: We want to increase the penalties for sexual offenses, gross violation of integrity, and gross violation of a woman's integrity. In addition, we want to criminalize controlling behavior.
citations.princip: increased penalties and criminalization of controlling behavior

citations.quote: The victim's perspective must be strengthened and post-separation violence must end.

motivering: The proposal combats fraud in the national population register (folkbokföring) and supports responsible tax policy, which aligns with the Centre Party's demand for responsible management of tax funds. The law includes built-in privacy safeguards (limited storage period, strong confidentiality protection). The specific measures C opposes — stop-and-search zones, preventive wiretapping, and others — concern law enforcement, not administrative data analysis with these safeguards.

citations.quote: Politics should manage taxpayers' money responsibly. More money should be spent on the core of the welfare system, less on benefits.

The rule of law and the individual's rights vis-à-vis the state must be defended. We therefore say no to stop-and-search zones, collective punishment, reversed burden of proof, anonymous witnesses, preventive wiretapping, and restrictions on religious freedom.
citations.princip: The individual's rights against the state

motivering: The motions include the Sweden Democrats' (SD) proposals (Enholm et al.) on municipal issues, and C does not cooperate with SD or give them influence. C's principle of decentralization protects municipal self-determination, but the documents give no specific support for the direction of the proposals in question. C votes with the committee and rejects the motions.

citations.quote: The Centre Party is now the only center-right party that will not cooperate with the Sweden Democrats or give them power over how Sweden is governed.
Decentralize more. People should get to decide more for themselves, and political decisions should be made close to those affected.

motivering: The motion on social intervention groups (sociala insatsgrupper) concerns preventive work against youth crime, an area where the Centre Party wants to see better efforts against recruitment into gangs. However, it is the Left Party's proposal, and the committee refers to ongoing inquiries. Without a stated position of its own on this particular tool, the party follows the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: better efforts that prevent [gang] recruitment
Society must not give in to the gangs.

motivering: The question concerns mandatory education for those convicted of purchasing sex, within the Prison and Probation Service. The Centre Party's program focuses on increased penalties for sexual offenses and early preventive efforts against men's violence, but does not specifically address mandatory education for those convicted of buying sex. Without an explicit position of its own on this particular issue, the party follows the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: We want to increase the penalties for sexual offenses, gross violation of integrity, and gross violation of a woman's integrity.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own proposals (nos. 2-5) in the section of the committee report on healthcare within elderly care, which the committee rejects. The manifesto demands shorter queues, more care places, and freedom of choice for patients throughout the country. The party should vote No to support reservation 23 and its own proposals for better healthcare for the elderly.

citations.quote: We want to shorten the queues and create more care places where needed through investments in more nurses and better state support for the regions, tailored to their conditions and needs.
citations.princip: shorter queues and more care places

citations.quote: We want to defend freedom of choice in healthcare and social care and run operations close to the people receiving care. Responsibility for healthcare should not be moved from the regions to the state.
citations.princip: freedom of choice and decentralized healthcare

motivering: The committee rejects the Centre Party's own proposal on citizen influence in physical planning (Alireza Akhondi et al., C, item 23). C's principle of decentralization and its demand that decisions be made close to the citizens affected is a fundamental line in the manifesto. The reservation (Alternative A: Reservation 11) likely represents the party's own proposals, which is why C votes No.

citations.quote: Decentralize more. People should get to decide more for themselves, and political decisions should be made close to those affected.

The shoreline protection (strandskydd) should be reformed to make it easier to build and live in rural areas. It's time to give rural residents more self-determination over their own land, and through simplified regulations make it easier to build and live in rural areas.

motivering: The Centre Party's own motions on increased housing construction and reduced segregation (Liljeberg, items 9 and 10, and Akhondi, item 24) are rejected by the committee. The manifesto explicitly pushes for simplified regulations and reformed shoreline protection to facilitate housing construction and living in rural areas. Reservation 18 reflects the party's own proposals, which is why the party votes No.

citations.quote: The shoreline protection (strandskydd) should be reformed to make it easier to build and live in rural areas. It's time to give rural residents more self-determination over their own land, and through simplified regulations make it easier to build and live in rural areas.
citations.princip: reformed shoreline protection for housing construction

citations.quote: The reinforced amortization requirement — a form of forced saving for those with the lowest incomes — should be abolished now that interest rates are normalizing.

motivering: The motion on banning PFAS is the Centre Party's own (Stina Larsson et al., item 83). The committee rejects it, but C's environmental goals require that children be able to swim without being exposed to toxins — a commitment that directly covers PFAS in water. C should vote No and support its reservation (Alternative A).

citations.quote: Save Sweden's lakes, watercourses and seas. Our children should be able to swim without being exposed to toxins, littering or algal blooms.
Sweden should become the world's most resource-efficient country and the economy more circular.

motivering: The proposal requires stockpiling of healthcare products and expands APL's mandate to maintain operations during crisis and war. This is directly consistent with the Centre Party's commitment to civil defence preparedness. The alternative (Reservation 4, V and S) deviates from this direction. C should vote Yes.

citations.quote: Civil defence is also vital. We must build up civil defence and society's preparedness for war and crisis.
citations.princip: build up civil defence and preparedness

citations.quote: You should have access to a secure welfare system that follows you throughout your life.

omvarld.faktor: Sweden's accession to NATO was approved by the Riksdag in April 2023
omvarld.effekt: Strengthens the priority given to civil defence preparedness, including the supply of healthcare products during heightened alert

motivering: The specific proposals on other environmental taxes (chemicals, alcohol, aviation, waste, etc.) are not directly covered by the election manifesto. However, the party's general line on reduced regulatory burden and relief for local producers, e.g. farm-gate sales, gives a weak indication toward accepting the rejection of the party's own motions.

citations.quote: We shall clear away superfluous rules and bureaucracy.
citations.princip: reduced regulatory burden for rural areas

citations.quote: Allow farm-gate sales of alcohol to strengthen the visitor industry and develop rural areas.

motivering: The matter concerns the organisation of public health work around mental health, with motions from SD and S. The Centre Party wants to see more preventive work against mental ill-health among young people, but the committee refers to work already under way in the area, and the motions are not the party's own. Without a specific position of its own, the party follows the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Mental ill-health among our children and young people is far too high, and we must work more preventively
citations.princip: prevent mental ill-health among young people

motivering: C's election manifesto explicitly demands stricter requirements on working conditions, environment and climate in trade agreements. The Green Party's motion on revised sustainability requirements in trade agreements coincides directly with this commitment. C votes No against the committee and supports Alternative A/Reservation 5.

citations.quote: Set stricter requirements on working conditions, environment and climate in trade agreements.
Sweden cannot manage without free trade. Open up more markets for Swedish goods and services.

motivering: The committee rejects the Centre Party's own tax policy motions (Annie Lööf motion item 58, Helena Lindahl motion item 24). The election manifesto is clear: the total tax burden must come down, and C does not want to contribute to tax increases that harm jobs. C should vote No and support its Reservation 13.

citations.quote: The total tax burden must come down next term of office. We will not contribute to any tax increases that harm jobs, personal savings, or make it more expensive to live.
Cut taxes on work and enterprise, especially for small businesses and sole proprietors. It should pay to run a business and create jobs.
citations.princip: lower tax on work and enterprise

motivering: C's manifesto states that Sweden needs free trade, not protectionism. SD's motions on international trade are marked by nationalism and protectionism, which directly contradicts C's free-trade line. C does not support SD's positions and votes with the committee.

citations.quote: Sweden needs more free trade and international cooperation, not protectionism and closed borders.
The Centre Party is now the only centre-right party that will not cooperate with the Sweden Democrats or give them power over how Sweden is governed.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motions (items 9, 10, 121, 133) in the report on the organisation of the Armed Forces, which the committee rejects. The manifesto demands that Sweden be rearmed militarily quickly and forcefully and that 2% of GDP be spent on defence. The party should vote No in order to stand behind Reservation 3 and its own positions on a stronger Armed Forces.

citations.quote: We want to rearm the military defence quickly, forcefully and for the long term. Sweden needs to spend two percent of GDP on defence as soon as practically possible and join NATO.
Sweden shall be defended. Russia's invasion in violation of international law has shown that we cannot rule out Sweden being drawn into war.

motivering: The motions on multilateral aid priorities were submitted by V and MP, not by C. The committee rejects them with reference to ongoing work. C's liberal approach differs from V's and MP's left-leaning aid policy, and C can accept that work is ongoing. C should vote Yes with the committee.

citations.quote: It is possible to build coalitions that stem neither from the xenophobic right's nationalism nor the socialist left's stifling collectivism.
Sweden needs more free trade and international cooperation, not protectionism and closed borders.

motivering: The committee rejects SD's and V's motions on accessibility and mapping of mineral resources; C has no motions of its own here. Both motions deviate from C's balanced line that combines extraction with environmental consideration. C supports the committee's rejection and votes Yes.

citations.quote: To manage the green transition we must make use of Sweden's natural resources. It is better for Sweden to take responsibility and extract more minerals and metals instead of continuing to import them from countries with a larger climate footprint and worse working conditions.

motivering: The issue concerns exit programmes to help individuals leave criminal gangs, an S motion. The Centre Party's programme emphasises that society must not yield to the gangs and invests in preventing new recruitment, but does not specifically mention exit programmes. Without a clear position of its own on this specific issue, the party follows the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Society must not yield to the gangs.
better measures that prevent new recruitment

motivering: The Centre Party strongly advocates decentralisation and that political decisions be made close to those affected. Strengthened local influence over wildlife management is directly in line with the party's principle of property rights and local self-determination in nature conservation. Reservation 3 supports local influence and the party votes No.

citations.quote: Decentralise more. People should be able to decide more for themselves, and political decisions should be made close to those affected.

More must be done to restore wetlands, combat invasive species and make it easier for landowners to contribute, since voluntariness and property rights are the foundation of better nature conservation.
citations.princip: property rights as the foundation of nature conservation

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motion (Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist, item 2) on the organisation of the Regulatory Council (Regelrådet), which the committee wants to reject. A well-functioning Regulatory Council is a key tool for achieving the party's goal of simplifying regulations and reducing the administrative burden on businesses. C should vote No.

citations.quote: Clear out the regulatory swamp for entrepreneurs, large and small. We want to introduce a new and simplified business form for micro-enterprises, so that more people will dare to try running a business.
Expensive, complicated and innovation-inhibiting regulations lie like a wet blanket over parts of rural Sweden. We shall clear away superfluous rules and bureaucracy.

motivering: The committee's proposal rejects motions from V, MP and S that want to make NATO accession conditional on demands regarding nuclear weapons and foreign troops. The Centre Party advocates unreserved NATO entry, and the party's documents state no such restrictions. The party should vote Yes to support full and unrestricted NATO membership.

citations.quote: The Centre Party wants to rearm the defence forces, strengthen Sweden's civil preparedness and complete the entry into NATO.
Sweden must be defended. Russia's invasion in violation of international law has shown that we cannot rule out Sweden being drawn into war.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motions (Niels Paarup-Petersen et al., claims 34 and 36) concerning copyright-protected artworks in public spaces, which the committee wants to reject. The party emphasises artistic freedom and free culture as cornerstones of civil society. C should vote No and pursue its reservation (dissenting opinion).

citations.quote: Academic and artistic freedom, as well as free culture, are cornerstones of a vital civil society.
Providing culture throughout the country is an important starting point for the Centre Party. Culture must be free and independent

motivering: The motion from the Left Party proposes a crime victim ombudsman. The Centre Party wants to strengthen the crime victim perspective and provide better support to victims of crime, but the party's programme does not identify an ombudsman institution as a tool for this. Without its own stated line on this specific institutional proposal, the party follows the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: The crime victim perspective must be strengthened. Those who have been subjected to crime should receive redress and better support.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motions (Bäckström et al., claims 9-10, and Lööf et al., claim 3) on regulatory simplification in agricultural policy, which the committee proposes rejecting. The manifesto's demand to clear away excessive regulations and strengthen the competitiveness of farming bears directly on these claims. The party should support Reservation 12 (dissenting opinion) and vote No against the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Expensive, cumbersome and innovation-hampering regulations lie like a wet blanket over parts of the countryside. We must clear away excessive regulations and bureaucracy.

Sweden needs an even more competitive agricultural sector. A long-term sustainable food supply with increased security of supply and increased food production requires regulatory simplifications and tax cuts, including a powerful agricultural tax deduction and a biofuel premium that makes sustainable farming more profitable.

motivering: The Centre Party has a clear and repeated line of lowering the tax on biofuels to reduce motorists' costs and dependence on oil, as well as lowering the overall tax burden. Several C members' motions on fuel tax are rejected by the committee, which contradicts this stated line.

citations.quote: Cut taxes on biofuels blended into petrol and diesel as much as possible. This would lower motorists' costs, benefit the climate, create jobs and reduce Sweden's dependence on oil.
The overall tax burden must come down next parliamentary term. We will not participate in any tax increases that harm jobs, personal savings, or make housing more expensive.

motivering: V's motions on restricting subcontractors and imposing reasonable terms in procurement entail increased state regulation, which conflicts with C's deregulation line. C wants to clear away regulatory red tape for entrepreneurs and opposes leftist collectivist policy. C votes with the committee.

citations.quote: Clear away the regulatory swamp for entrepreneurs, large and small.
It is possible to build coalitions that stem neither from the xenophobic right's nationalism nor the socialist left's suffocating collectivism.

motivering: The matter concerns illegal trading in rental contracts, an issue not addressed in the Centre Party's documents. The party's programme generally promotes freer markets to curb prices, but gives no specific guidance on trading in rental contracts or tenancy rights. Without a documented line of its own, the party follows the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: By creating freer markets and improving competition, we can curb prices further.

motivering: The election manifesto lacks a specific position on the organisation of public health work; C's healthcare priorities concern waiting lists, continuity of doctor contact, and staff conditions, not organisational restructuring. None of C's own motions are among those rejected. Without a conflicting commitment of its own, C supports the committee's proposal to reject the motions.

citations.quote: Sweden needs healthcare and social care that puts patients, users and staff at the centre. This is a main priority for the Centre Party for the next parliamentary term.

motivering: The Centre Party's own motion (Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist et al., claim 19) on procedural legal matters is rejected by the committee. The manifesto explicitly states that access to legal counsel must be improved and that the ability to have one's case tried must not be reserved for those with high incomes. Reservation 18 (dissenting opinion) reflects the party's claims, and the party votes No.

citations.quote: Everyone who lives in Sweden should be able to have their case tried. Processing times for handling and administrative decisions in courts and government agencies must be shortened, and access to legal counsel improved.
citations.princip: access to legal review and counsel

citations.quote: The ability to bring a case against the state or a municipality, when one has good reason to have one's case tried, should not, in a liberal democracy, be a right reserved for those with high incomes. We want to create a possibility for individuals to receive compensation for legal counsel in administrative matters where they had reason to have their case tried.
citations.princip: fair access to legal counsel regardless of income

motivering: The motion on limit values for PFAS in drinking water is the Centre Party's own (Stina Larsson et al., claim 82). The committee rejects it, but C's programme demands clean water free of toxins. Limit values for PFAS are a direct application of this environmental commitment. C should vote No and support its reservation 13 (dissenting opinion).

citations.quote: Save Sweden's lakes, watercourses and seas. Our children should be able to swim without being exposed to toxins, littering or algal blooms.
Sweden shall become the world's most resource-efficient country and the economy more circular.

motivering: The motion on expanded international chemicals work is the Centre Party's own (Stina Larsson et al., claim 79). The committee rejects it. C's programme emphasises international environmental cooperation via the EU's emissions trading system and trade policy to reduce emissions globally. C should vote No and support its reservation (Alternative A).

citations.quote: The EU's emissions trading system is among the most effective tools we have, and we want to make it even more ambitious and open it up to more countries wishing to join.
With the Centre Party's reform agenda, Sweden can also do much more to reduce emissions in other countries.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motions (Bäckström, claim 1, and Larsson, claim 20) on the direction of the food strategy, which the committee proposes rejecting. The manifesto demands a strategy with increased security of supply, increased food production, and competitive agriculture as stated goals. The party should support Reservation 14 (dissenting opinion) and vote No.

citations.quote: A long-term sustainable food supply with increased security of supply and increased food production requires regulatory simplifications and tax cuts, including a powerful agricultural tax deduction and a biofuel premium that makes sustainable farming more profitable.
Food production must increase, in the short and long term.

motivering: The Centre Party explicitly wants to make sick leave more flexible and improve rehabilitation. Martina Johansson's (C) extensive motions on the rehabilitation chain are rejected by the committee with reference to ongoing work, which runs counter to the party's own reform line.

citations.quote: Do more to prevent, counteract and rehabilitate stress-related mental ill health. We want to make sick leave more flexible and improve rehabilitation.
citations.princip: more flexible sick leave and rehabilitation

citations.quote: The Swedish labour market needs both more flexibility and more security. Support for retraining and further education must be improved.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motions (Deremar et al. claim 6 and Lööf et al. claim 21) among those the committee proposes to reject. The manifesto demands strengthened protection for people in the media and in institutions that uphold democracy. C votes No and supports Alternative A in line with its own claims.

citations.quote: Hatred, threats, harassment and violence directed at institutions that uphold democracy must cease. We shall strengthen protection for people active in, among other things, the media, religious communities and public administration.
citations.princip: protection for institutions that uphold democracy

citations.quote: Comprehensive, independent and viable media coverage throughout the country is crucial for democracy. Press freedom must be protected and independent public service defended.

motivering: The Centre Party wants to increase freedom of choice and let in more care providers in the welfare sector, which argues against Social Democratic proposals to limit profits in welfare. No C motion is among those rejected. C therefore supports the committee's proposal to reject the motions on profit limits.

citations.quote: We want to open up for more care providers and increase freedom of choice so that patients, together with their doctor, can choose a care provider and a time when surgery or treatment best suits the patient's needs.
citations.princip: freedom of choice, more care providers

citations.quote: We want to defend freedom of choice in care and welfare and to run operations close to care recipients.
citations.princip: defend freedom of choice in welfare

motivering: The Centre Party has no claims of its own in this vote. However, the question of targets for simplification policy is a central theme in the party's programme. Reservation 1 represents a stronger commitment to simplification policy in line with the party's direction of creating clear and ambitious targets for reduced regulatory burden.

citations.quote: It should be easy to start and run a business; it should pay off to take the leap and make an investment.
Expensive, complicated and innovation-hampering regulations lie like a wet blanket over parts of the countryside. We shall clean up excessive rules and bureaucracy.

motivering: The motions on extending the Elderly Care Boost (Äldreomsorgslyftet) are rejected with reference to ongoing work. The Centre Party supports the principle of skills development for care staff but has no claims of its own in the matter and advocates regional self-determination over state-directed grant programmes. Without a C reservation, the party votes Yes with the committee.

citations.quote: Those who work in care and welfare should be able to grow and develop further in their profession. We want to give all nursing assistants and nurses the right to skills development.
We want to defend freedom of choice in care and welfare and to run operations close to care recipients. Responsibility for care should not be moved from the regions to the state.

motivering: The Centre Party's own motions on aid levels and aid priorities (Kerstin Lundgren, claims 21-23) are rejected by the committee. The manifesto emphasises international cooperation and a global commitment to liberal democracy, which motivates an active aid policy. Reservation 1 reflects the party's claims and the party votes No.

citations.quote: Sweden needs more free trade and international cooperation, not protectionism and closed borders.
Around the world a struggle is under way between supporters of liberal democracy and authoritarian forces. We must win it.

motivering: C's own motions on gender equality, men's violence and honour-related oppression (Liljeberg, Lööf, Vilhelmsson) are among the motions rejected in this vote. The election manifesto sets out concrete commitments such as criminalising controlling behaviour and action plans against honour-related oppression in all schools. C votes No to assert its own reservation.

citations.quote: We want to raise the penalties for sexual offences, gross violation of integrity and gross violation of a woman's integrity. In addition, we want to criminalise controlling behaviour.
All municipalities shall have action plans to prevent men's violence against women, and all schools shall have action plans against honour-related oppression.
citations.princip: action plans against violence and honour-related oppression

motivering: The Centre Party's own motions on cybersecurity and peacetime crisis preparedness (Niels Paarup-Petersen, claims 24, 31 and 39) are rejected by the committee. The manifesto explicitly states that civil defence and society's preparedness must be armed for war and crisis; building knowledge in the field of cybersecurity is part of this. The party supports Reservation 12 and votes No.

citations.quote: Civil defence, too, is vital. We must arm civil defence and society's preparedness for war and crisis.
citations.princip: arm civil defence and crisis preparedness

citations.quote: Russia's illegal invasion has shown that we cannot rule out Sweden being drawn into war. Ukraine's heroic defence of its country's freedom and survival has shown that it is possible to stand up to despots. The Centre Party wants to arm the defence forces, strengthen Sweden's civil preparedness and complete accession to NATO.
citations.princip: strengthened civil preparedness and NATO accession

motivering: Reindeer husbandry is not specifically addressed in the Centre Party's election manifesto, and no C motion is affected by this rejection decision. The rejected motion is from the Social Democrats, and it is unknown whether Reservation 45 represents C's values. In the absence of a specific position, the party should follow the committee's decision and vote Yes.

citations.quote: We want to strengthen, among other things, property rights, the prohibition on discrimination, the protection of minorities and the status of minority languages, and give constitutional protection to the right to abortion and reproductive health.

motivering: The election manifesto does not address VAT issues specifically, so Helena Lindahl's (C) motion on other value-added tax matters is not directly covered by the documents. The party's general position on tax relief for business provides a weak indication against accepting the rejection.

citations.quote: Lower the tax on work and business, especially for small businesses and sole proprietors. It should pay to run a business and create jobs.
The total tax burden must come down next parliamentary term.

motivering: The Centre Party had its own motion on regulatory simplification (Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist et al. (C), claim 6) which the committee rejects. The party's manifesto demands that one 'clear out the regulatory swamp for entrepreneurs' and reduce the administrative burden. Reservation 4 represents C's own reservation line. The party should vote No to support its own position.

citations.quote: Clear out the regulatory swamp for entrepreneurs, large and small. We want to introduce a new, simplified business form for micro-enterprises, so that more people dare to try running a business.
Expensive, complicated and innovation-hampering regulations lie like a wet blanket over parts of the countryside. We shall clean up excessive rules and bureaucracy.

motivering: The only motion rejected in this vote is C's own, on compensation for violation and debt recovery for crime victims. The election manifesto states that the crime victim perspective must be strengthened and that crime victims should receive redress and better support. C votes No to assert its own reservation.

citations.quote: The crime victim perspective must be strengthened and after-violence must cease.
It is also important that crime victims receive better support and that after-violence is combated.

motivering: The Government's proposal strengthens supply preparedness with requirements on healthcare products and expands the mandate of Apotek Produktion & Laboratorier (Pharmacy Production & Laboratories) ahead of crises and war. C's manifesto emphasizes that civil defence is vital and that society's preparedness must be strengthened. The proposal aligns well with the party's agenda for secure healthcare and strengthened crisis preparedness.

citations.quote: Civil defence too is vital. We must strengthen civil defence and society's preparedness for war and crisis.
You should have access to secure welfare that follows you throughout your life.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motions (Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist, item 17, and Annie Lööf, item 19) on strengthened conditions for mineral extraction, directly in line with the election manifesto's explicit commitment that Sweden should extract more minerals and metals and halve permit processing times. The committee's proposal to reject these motions runs counter to the party's own priorities. C votes No to support reservation 18 (Alternative A).

citations.quote: It is better for Sweden to take responsibility and extract more minerals and metals instead of continuing to import them from countries with a larger climate footprint and worse working conditions.

It is time to halve the time it takes to obtain permits for green investments and reform the Environmental Code so that a project's climate benefit is given greater weight in environmental assessments.
Expensive, cumbersome, and innovation-stifling regulations lie like a wet blanket over parts of the countryside. We will clear away excessive rules and bureaucracy.

motivering: The motions on penalties were submitted by the Sweden Democrats (SD) (Richard Jomshof, item 1) and the Social Democrats (S) — not by C. C explicitly rejects SD's criminal policy methods such as stop-and-search zones and collective punishment. The committee's rejection is consistent with C's liberal rule-of-law principles. C should vote Yes with the committee.

citations.quote: We therefore say no to stop-and-search zones, collective punishment, reversed burden of proof, anonymous witnesses, preventive wiretapping, and restrictions on freedom of religion.
citations.princip: liberal rule-of-law principles against SD measures

citations.quote: The rule of law and the individual's rights vis-à-vis the state must be defended.
citations.princip: protection of the rule of law

motivering: The election manifesto does not mention any specific vaccination programme for the elderly, and the rejected motions come from V (the Left Party) and S (the Social Democrats), not from C. Without any conflicting commitment of its own, and since the committee refers to ongoing work, C supports the proposal to reject the motions.

citations.quote: Accessible and secure healthcare and care throughout the country.

motivering: The committee rejects V's motion on equipment to protect healthcare staff. The overarching bill in the same report already covers personal protective equipment as a healthcare product. C's manifesto emphasizes that responsibility for healthcare should lie with the regions, not be centralized nationally through further V-driven mandates.

citations.quote: We want to defend freedom of choice in healthcare and care and run operations close to care recipients. Responsibility for healthcare should not be shifted from the regions to the state.

motivering: The Centre Party has its own motion (Bäckström et al., item 2) on food supply security in the strategic plan for 2023-2027, which the committee proposes to reject. The manifesto's strong commitment to increased food production and sustainable food supply bears directly on this motion. The party should support Reservation 1 and vote No.

citations.quote: Food production must increase, in the short and long term.

A long-term sustainable food supply with increased supply security and increased food production requires simplified regulations and tax cuts, including a substantial agricultural deduction and a biofuel premium that makes sustainable farming more profitable.

motivering: The Centre Party's motions on the development of the rescue services (Mikael Larsson, items 1 and 5) are rejected by the committee. The manifesto emphasizes that civil defence and society's preparedness against war and crisis must be strengthened, and the rescue services are a central part of peacetime crisis preparedness. Reservation 3 reflects the party's motions and the party votes No.

citations.quote: Civil defence too is vital. We must strengthen civil defence and society's preparedness for war and crisis.

Public services should be accessible and reliable throughout the country. Everyone should have a secure police presence, an equivalent school, and secure, accessible healthcare and care — regardless of where they live.
citations.princip: accessible and reliable public services throughout the country

motivering: The motions on gender equality and SRHR (sexual and reproductive health and rights) in multilateral aid are V's (items 2, 5, 8). Although C strongly upholds SRHR and gender equality, the election manifesto lacks specific positions on these topics in multilateral aid. The committee refers to ongoing work, and C's liberal view on aid differs from V's. C votes Yes with the committee.

citations.quote: It is possible to build coalitions that are based neither on the xenophobic right's nationalism nor on the socialist left's stifling collectivism.
give constitutional protection to the right to abortion and reproductive health

motivering: Several of C's own motions on knowledge within the judicial system regarding intimate partner violence (Liljeberg, Lööf) are among the rejected proposals. The election manifesto calls for a strengthened crime-victim perspective, tougher penalties, and training to detect and handle violence. C votes No in support of its own reservation.

citations.quote: The crime-victim perspective must be strengthened and post-separation violence must end.
We want to increase the penalties for sexual offences, gross violation of integrity, and gross violation of a woman's integrity. We also want to criminalize controlling behaviour.
citations.princip: tougher penalties for intimate partner violence

motivering: The Centre Party's own motions on housing for the elderly (Alireza Akhondi, items 18 and 19) are rejected by the committee. The manifesto stresses that care in old age should be accessible and equivalent throughout the country. Reservation 24 reflects the party's motions and the party votes No.

citations.quote: We can improve our shared welfare, from the best school when you are young, to the best healthcare when you become ill, and the best care in old age.
We want to defend freedom of choice in healthcare and care and run operations close to care recipients. Responsibility for healthcare should not be shifted from the regions to the state.
citations.princip: freedom of choice and accessible healthcare and care

motivering: The committee's proposal rejects SD's and S's motions on the rights of the elderly. The Centre Party has no motions of its own on the matter and the documents do not specifically cover the proposed SD/S models. Without a C reservation, the party votes Yes with the committee, in line with the party's support for regional responsibility and freedom of choice in elderly care.

citations.quote: We want to defend freedom of choice in healthcare and care and run operations close to care recipients. Responsibility for healthcare should not be shifted from the regions to the state.
citations.princip: freedom of choice and regional responsibility

citations.quote: You should have access to secure welfare that follows you throughout your life.

motivering: C's election manifesto contains an explicit commitment to allow farm-gate sales of alcohol to strengthen rural areas and the visitor industry. Several C motions (Bäckström, Thand Ringqvist, Larsson, Lööf) are among the items the committee proposes to reject. C votes No and supports Alternative A/Reservation 8.

citations.quote: It is unreasonable that local producers of alcoholic beverages cannot sell their products to visitors. Allow farm-gate sales of alcohol to strengthen the visitor industry and develop rural areas.

motivering: The motion rejected in this vote comes from SD and concerns the municipal sector's mandate; C has no corresponding commitment in its election manifesto and does not share SD's position on the issue. C therefore supports the committee's proposal to reject the motion.

citations.quote: Decentralize more. People should be able to decide more for themselves, and political decisions should be made close to those affected.

motivering: Among the rejected motions are four C motions (Bergenblock, Liljeberg, Annie Lööf, Malin Björk) on aggravating circumstances. C's election manifesto demands tougher sentences for sexual offenses and gross violation of a person's integrity, as well as criminalization of controlling behavior. Reservation 32 likely reflects C's own proposals; C should vote No.

citations.quote: We want to increase the penalties for sexual offenses, gross violation of a person's integrity and gross violation of a woman's integrity. We also want to criminalize controlling behavior.
citations.princip: tougher sentences and criminalization of controlling behavior

citations.quote: We shall lead Sweden toward an end to men's violence against women. Men who hit should not get away with it.
citations.princip: tougher action against men's violence against women

motivering: The Centre Party has several of its own motions (Larsson, items 2, 19, 21 and 62; Lööf, item 58) on sustainable design and circular economy that are rejected by the committee. The manifesto clearly commits to Sweden becoming the world's most resource-efficient country and to a more circular economy. The party should support Reservation 4 and vote No.

citations.quote: Sweden shall become the world's most resource-efficient country and the economy more circular. With the right support and simplified regulations we can recycle and reuse everything from clothes to minerals and metals.
The climate cannot wait for expensive and complicated regulations.

motivering: C's election manifesto does not specifically address regulation of AI and personal data privacy. The committee's reference to ongoing work does not conflict with C's general principles. Without specific documentary support for MP's proposal and with ongoing inquiry work as background, C votes with the committee.

citations.quote: The rule of law and the individual's rights vis-à-vis the state must be defended.
citations.princip: the individual's rights against the state

motivering: Several of C's own motions (Johansson, Liljeberg, Lööf, Vilhelmsson) on custody, residence and contact in cases of domestic violence are among the rejected proposals. The election manifesto emphasizes protection for women and children exposed to violence, including the right to change surname when under protected identity and a stronger crime-victim perspective. C votes No in support of its own reservation.

citations.quote: Women with protected identity should more easily be able to change their children's surname.
citations.princip: protection for women and children in cases of violence

citations.quote: The crime-victim perspective must be strengthened and the after-violence must end.

motivering: KD's documents contain no position on the financial terms of Riksdag members. The motions from V are rejected by the Committee on the Constitution. As a governing party, KD supports the committee's proposal, and nothing in the external circumstances warrants a deviation.

citations.quote: The cooperation parties commit to voting for the government's budget so that the budget as a whole is passed in the Riksdag.

omvarld.faktor: KD is a governing party (M+KD+L)
omvarld.effekt: The absence of its own documents means coalition discipline determines the vote against V's reservation

motivering: SD's proposals on uranium extraction concern energy security. The Tidöavtalet (the Tidö agreement) and election manifesto invest heavily in nuclear power, but domestic uranium mining is not explicitly addressed. The committee rejects SD's proposals 17 and 18. KD, as a party to the Tidö agreement's energy cooperation, acts within the coalition's overall line and votes Yes with the committee.

citations.quote: The conditions for investment in nuclear power shall be strengthened through special state credit guarantees amounting to SEK 400 billion, with more generous terms than the current system.
Invest in nuclear power with long-term conditions to develop. Extend the operation of existing reactors and build out new reactors.

motivering: The Tidö agreement commits to tightened furlough rules and a heavily expanded prison and probation service within the Crime cooperation project. C's motion on GPS tracking during prisoner transport is rejected with reference to ongoing inquiries – work led by KD's coalition. KD supports its own coalition's preparatory work and votes Yes.

citations.quote: The right to furlough is restricted
The prison and probation service is expanded significantly

motivering: The Tidö agreement establishes that the freedom of the media shall be safeguarded. S's motion on limiting the searchability of personal data in public documents concerns press freedom. The committee rejects the motion with reference to ongoing work; KD supports the committee's assessment and safeguards the freedom of the media.

citations.quote: The freedom of the media shall be safeguarded, and the diversity of different media shall be promoted.

motivering: KD prioritizes patient safety with national standards, and the Tidö agreement puts the patient's best interest at the center. The government's legislative proposal on strengthened supply preparedness in healthcare is directly consistent with these priorities. The committee's rejection of C's and S's motions on specific follow-up gives the government a mandate to carry out the reform on its own responsibility.

citations.quote: Ensure patient safety with national standards and technical specifications for all digital healthcare information.
The patient's best interest shall be at the center of the reform work.
citations.princip: The patient's best interest at the center

motivering: KD and the Tidö agreement prioritize cohesive addiction care and treatment via the regions. The committee rejects the motions on harm minimization. KD's position on regional responsibility and cohesive care is in line with the committee's rejection; the party does not support harm-reduction models as a replacement for care.

citations.quote: People with substance abuse problems and addiction disorders shall be given cohesive care and treatment. Responsibility shall lie with the regions, and a long-term plan shall be drawn up for better addiction care throughout the country.

motivering: The Tidö agreement gives the state expanded responsibility for young serious offenders and prioritizes crime-prevention work during the parliamentary term. S's motion on coordinated measures is rejected with reference to ongoing inquiries within this coalition work. KD supports its own reform package for youth crime and votes Yes.

citations.quote: The state should therefore take greater responsibility for young people who commit serious crimes.
Crime-prevention work shall be prioritized during the next parliamentary term.

motivering: The Tidö agreement contains its own, delimited public administration reforms (e.g. reinstated civil servant liability) but no wording on lobbyist regulation. Since the committee refers to the government already working on related issues and that the cooperation parties should not unilaterally cooperate with the opposition, KD votes Yes and rejects the MP/S/C motions.

citations.quote: Appoint a special investigator tasked with presenting proposals for what a reinstated civil servant liability could look like
the participating parties do not unilaterally cooperate with other parties in the Riksdag on the issues covered by the directives for the cooperation projects

motivering: The Tidö agreement establishes that sickness insurance is to be reformed at its own pace with a focus on rehabilitation and fewer sick leaves, handled within the government cooperation's own processes rather than through opposition motions. The committee's rejection of the motions on activity compensation and sickness compensation, citing ongoing work, is in line with this. KD should vote Yes on the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: Sickness insurance shall provide financial security for those who cannot work due to illness.
All proposals in the project that affect the budget bill shall be handled in the regular budget process, where expenditures must be weighed against each other.

motivering: The Tidö agreement states that tax proposals with an impact on the budget shall be handled in the regular budget process, not through individual motions on various excise taxes. The government basis's own line is instead lower fuel prices and reduced cost pressure via the budget. KD should therefore vote Yes on the committee's rejection of the motions in question.

citations.quote: All proposals in the project that affect the budget bill shall be handled in the regular budget process, where expenditures must be weighed against each other.
citations.princip: tax issues via the budget process

citations.quote: Substantially lower petrol and diesel prices for everyone, mainly by reducing the blending of expensive biofuel.
citations.princip: own line for lower fuel prices

motivering: KD's housing policy in the Tidö agreement emphasizes broadened ownership and more housing rather than expanded tenant protection, which could hamper the supply of rental housing. The Left Party's (V) motion on stricter eviction protection for families with children lacks direct support in KD's document. The committee majority, which includes KD, rejects the motion, and KD votes Yes.

citations.quote: Reforms that contribute to broadened ownership, for example regarding housing, savings and pensions, should be implemented.

motivering: According to the Tidö agreement, the social security systems for students and sickness insurance are to be reformed through the government cooperation's own projects and the regular budget process, not through individual opposition motions. The committee's rejection of the motions, citing ongoing work, is therefore in line with KD's position. Vote Yes.

citations.quote: Sickness insurance shall provide financial security for those who cannot work due to illness.
All proposals in the project that affect the budget bill shall be handled in the regular budget process, where expenditures must be weighed against each other.

motivering: Neither the election manifesto nor the Tidö agreement specifically covers climate adaptation of crisis preparedness. KD is part of the government coalition, and the Tidö agreement binds the parties not to unilaterally cooperate with other parties in the Riksdag; the committee majority rejects the motions citing ongoing work, which KD follows.

citations.quote: The cooperation also means that the participating parties do not unilaterally cooperate with other parties in the Riksdag on the issues covered by the directives for the cooperation projects.
Our joint climate and environmental policy is based on the idea of stewardship and strives to find the most cost-effective measures, which at the same time do not harm industries and rural areas.

motivering: KD's election manifesto advocates for more sheltered housing and communal housing for the elderly. The committee rejects the motions from V, C and SD citing ongoing work, which is consistent with the government's own agenda. As a government party, KD trusts that the ongoing work within the Tidö framework addresses housing issues for the elderly. KD votes Yes.

citations.quote: More sheltered housing, communal housing for the elderly.
The cooperation parties commit to voting for the government's budget so that the budget as a whole is passed in the Riksdag.

motivering: KD's priorities in the Tidö agreement concern specific measures against honor-related oppression and the criminalization of controlling behavior, not a general review of the Discrimination Act. The motions from MP, C and V lack grounding in KD's own commitments, and the committee majority — including KD — rejects them. KD votes Yes.

citations.quote: Legislation against honor-related oppression shall be tightened, support for those affected improved, and the work of authorities made more efficient.
Significantly tighten the penalties for sexual offenses. 25 years in prison for aggravated rape, chemical castration as a condition for parole, and life imprisonment for aggravated rape of a child.

motivering: KD's election manifesto and the Tidö agreement lack specific commitments regarding the design of procurement rules for SMEs. As a government party in the coalition, KD acts in accordance with the committee's joint assessment and the reference to existing regulations and ongoing investigative work.

citations.quote: The cooperation parties collectively decide on the issues covered by the cooperation after coordination.
Facilitate employee ownership and generational transfer of companies - so that more companies can be run on by the staff if the owner wants to stop.

motivering: The National Institute of Economic Research's (Konjunkturinstitutet) assignment on companies' pricing is not covered by KD's election manifesto or the Tidö agreement. As a government party, KD supports the committee's rejection and the reference to the government having already begun work to make public administration more efficient.

citations.quote: The cooperation parties commit to voting for the government's budget so that the budget as a whole is passed in the Riksdag.

motivering: The Tidö agreement's school project already establishes that an inquiry shall review mother-tongue instruction and that the legal special status of minority languages shall be taken into account, i.e. the issue is handled within the government cooperation's own process. The committee's rejection of the motions, citing ongoing work, is therefore in line with KD's own commitment. KD votes Yes.

citations.quote: the special status of the national minority languages in the law shall be taken into account.
citations.princip: special status of minority languages respected

citations.quote: Review of mother-tongue instruction

motivering: KD's documents contain no specific commitments regarding the regulation and control of the haulage industry. As a government party bound by the Tidö agreement, KD generally supports a lighter regulatory burden and lower administrative costs for businesses, and follows the committee's line of rejecting motions from V, C, SD and S that are not part of the coalition's joint reform program.

citations.quote: Lower administrative costs for businesses.
Regulatory changes and cost relief for Swedish agriculture to increase Sweden's self-sufficiency and strengthen the competitiveness of agriculture

motivering: KD has no specific commitments regarding mineral compensation. The committee rejects motions from SD, C, and MP. The Tidö agreement (Tidöavtalet) supports simplifying permit processes and securing industrial competitiveness, but through the coalition's own reforms rather than opposition motions. KD supports the committee's line, and the reservation does not provide support for KD's interests.

citations.quote: An inquiry will be established to simplify and shorten the environmental permit review under the Environmental Code by making it more flexible, efficient and predictable.
The purpose is to secure the competitiveness of business, Swedish industrial production, and to promote a green transition with the export of climate-friendly products and technology.

Supporting the Social Democrats' (S) motion on reindeer husbandry via Reservation 45 falls directly within MP's line on indigenous rights.

citations.quote: strengthen the rights of national minorities and the Sami indigenous people, and that Sweden should commit to complying with the international convention on indigenous rights (ILO 169)

motivering: MP wants to sharply reduce VAT on sharing services such as car pools, which suggests supporting proposals to change VAT rather than rejecting them outright. citations.quote: sharply reduce VAT on car pools and other sharing services and make it easier for those who want to share, rather than own, a car.

motivering: The election manifesto takes no position on simplifying regulations for businesses in general. Without guidance and without its own MP reservation, the party supports the committee's rejection. MP's fundamental stance is strong regulation for the environment and consumer protection, not general deregulation — which argues against supporting the motions.

citations.quote: impose legal requirements that products be easy and inexpensive to repair and update

motivering: The election manifesto lacks a specific commitment on compensation for violation of personal integrity and the recovery of damages for crime victims. Without a clear corresponding principle to rely on, the default position is to support the committee's rejection of the motions.

citations.quote: Everything we do is built on solidarity in word and deed

motivering: The proposal strengthens healthcare's supply preparedness — including medicines and protective equipment — and expands APL's societal mandate ahead of crises. citations.quote: invest a larger share of defense funding in civil defense, and increase appropriations for crisis preparedness
improve care for the elderly and strengthen resources for home healthcare

motivering: MP's election manifesto lacks an explicit mineral policy, but the party's commitment to protecting 30 percent of Sweden's nature and opposing short-term thinking and profit-seeking argues against a tillkännagivande (formal request to the government) that would strengthen the conditions for extraction through more solution-oriented authorities in permit processes. Reservation 18 is the alternative that best reflects MP's nature conservation ambitions.

citations.quote: protect 30 percent of Sweden's nature, including our unique contiguous mountain forests and forests worth protecting throughout the country.

solidarity with animals, nature and the ecological system

motivering: MP's election manifesto does not cover general sentencing issues. One of the motions is from Richard Jomshof (SD), who routinely advocates harsher penalties without a focus on rehabilitation — an approach MP opposes. Without knowledge of the content of Reservation 35, the cautious choice is to vote Yes and support the committee's procedural rejection.

citations.quote: make a major investment in preventive work in socioeconomically disadvantaged areas

motivering: The manifesto generally highlights improved care for the elderly but does not specifically mention vaccination programs. In the absence of a concrete commitment on this particular point, the outcome is support for the committee's rejection of the motions.

citations.quote: improve care for the elderly and strengthen resources for home healthcare.

motivering: MP's manifesto calls for a good working environment in healthcare. The Left Party's (V) motion on protective equipment specifically for healthcare staff is directly linked to this priority and goes further than what the main proposal guarantees. MP supports V's reservation for stronger protection.

citations.quote: raise wages and secure a good working environment in healthcare

motivering: MP wants to strengthen Swedish agriculture's self-sufficiency, which directly supports the Centre Party's (C) motion's focus on supply security in the EU's strategic plan 2023–2027. Reservation 1 aligns with this principle. Russia's invasion of Ukraine makes the food supply issue urgent and reinforces the need to act.

citations.quote: strengthen Swedish agriculture for increased self-sufficiency in staple foods, and support the transition to ecological and sustainable agriculture with fossil-free machinery

omvarld.faktor: Russia's invasion of Ukraine creates uncertainty in European food supply
omvarld.effekt: Strengthens the argument for supply security in the EU's strategic plan, in line with MP's position

motivering: MP's own motion in the matter concerning the development of the rescue service reflects the manifesto's demand for enhanced civil preparedness and increased appropriations for crisis preparedness. The party should vote against the committee's rejection and support the reservation that wants to strengthen the rescue service further.

citations.quote: invest a larger share of defense funding in civil defense, and increase appropriations for crisis preparedness
We have learned a great deal from the crises of recent years, and now we must equip Sweden to stand strong no matter what happens.

motivering: MP's election manifesto demands that Sweden's feminist foreign and development policy be strengthened, including support for sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) globally. The committee's proposal rejects the Left Party's (V) motions on gender equality and SRHR in multilateral aid, which directly counteracts MP's commitments. MP should vote No and support Reservation 1.

citations.quote: develop and strengthen Sweden's feminist foreign and development policy
that aid should help build sustainable, climate-smart societies, protect oceans, promote biological diversity and ecosystem services

motivering: The question of increased knowledge in the judicial system about violence in close relationships and honor-related violence is closely aligned with the manifesto's demand for strengthened efforts and equal support against honor-related violence throughout the country, in a matter that also includes the Green Party's (MP) own motion. This justifies support for the reservation over the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: strengthen efforts against honor-related violence and oppression so that equal help is provided throughout the country.
citations.princip: strengthened competence against violence in close relationships

citations.quote: Women should be able to live their lives in safety.

motivering: The Green Party (MP) has its own motion on housing for the elderly in this matter, in line with the manifesto's goal of a secure home for everyone without high financial barriers. Since the motion points to a need that the committee does not address, the party should vote against the rejection and support the reservation.

citations.quote: Everyone needs a home.
The new green people's home shall be built with climate-smart housing at low cost, so that everyone has the opportunity to create a home of their own, alone or together with others.

motivering: The election manifesto prioritizes improved care for the elderly. The committee's rejection of motions on the rights of the elderly, justified by ongoing work, is insufficient for the Green Party (MP), which wants to see concrete reinforcements. MP supports Reservation 1 and emphasizes that the rights of the elderly require more active measures.

citations.quote: improve care for the elderly and strengthen the resources for home healthcare
raise the guarantee pension and reform the pension system with the aim of raising pensions, most for those with the lowest pensions
citations.princip: strengthened economic security for the elderly

motivering: The election manifesto lacks a specific alcohol policy or position on farm-gate sales. MP's general emphasis on public health and social protection supports backing the committee's rejection of these liberalization proposals.

citations.quote: invest in primary care and increase access to care for mental ill health

motivering: The manifesto does not address the general mandate of the municipal sector or the content of the current SD motion. Without a clear corresponding principle, the default position is to support the committee's rejection of the motion.

citations.quote: Everything we do is built on solidarity in word and deed

motivering: MP wants no one to be subjected to discrimination on grounds including sexual orientation and wants to strengthen the rights of transgender people. The motions on aggravating circumstances include several from the Centre Party (C), likely including ones on hate crimes and LGBTQI protection. The committee's rejection of these motions works against MP's principle of strengthened protection against discrimination, which is why voting No in support of Reservation 32 is consistent.

citations.quote: In our Sweden, no one shall be subjected to racism or discrimination on the basis of, for example, faith, sexual orientation or disability
strengthen the rights of transgender people through a new Gender Recognition Act, and introduce a third legal gender

motivering: One of the motions the committee wants to reject is MP's own motion by Per Bolund et al. (item 22) on sustainable design, production and consumption. MP naturally supports its own position and should vote No to signal support for Reservation 4, which presumably reflects MP's own demands.

citations.quote: impose statutory requirements that products must be easy and cheap to repair and update
ban products manufactured to break prematurely

motivering: The committee rejects MP's own motion (Märta Stenevi et al., item 30) on artificial intelligence and privacy. The manifesto emphasizes the protection of democracy and individual rights against infringement. Reservation 5 likely reflects MP's position on strengthened privacy protection in the use of AI, which is why MP votes no.

citations.quote: Free speech, minority rights and protection against discrimination are important for democratic development, together with a strong and independent rule of law.
citations.princip: protection of democracy and individual rights

motivering: The manifesto explicitly states that children's right to safety outweighs violent parents' rights to their children, and that children should be protected from contact with a violent parent.
