citations.quote: protect children from being forced into contact with a violent parent.
citations.princip: protect children from a violent parent

citations.quote: In our Sweden, children's right to safety weighs heavier than violent parents' rights to their children.

motivering: The manifesto does not address the financial terms of members of parliament. The Social Democrats (S) have no reservation in this matter, and it is the Left Party's (V) motions that are being rejected. Without a clear party compass in the documents, the committee's proposal is supported.

citations.quote: We are equal before the paragraphs of the law book, and in our public authorities dutiful officials with high integrity work.
citations.princip: equal treatment under the rule of law

motivering: The manifesto does not explicitly mention uranium extraction, but the Social Democrats' (S) strong climate and environmental commitments argue against opening up for new mining operations with major environmental impact. The Sweden Democrats' (SD) motions on uranium extraction run counter to S's goal of Sweden transitioning to a fossil-free society and protecting ecosystems. The committee's rejection of these motions is consistent with S's environmental profile.

citations.quote: The climate transition is the defining issue of our time. We risk destroying our only planet and the conditions for living in many places, which will lead to enormous migration pressure.

Strengthen preparedness against extreme weather. Otherwise, cloudbursts risk flooding cities, drought risks wiping out entire harvests, and wildfires risk spreading. We want to continue the major investments so that municipalities can adapt to climate change locally.

motivering: The vote concerns the rejection of the Centre Party's (C) motion (item 42) on GPS tracking for prisoner transports and furloughs. The committee refers to ongoing inquiries. The Social Democrats' (S) crime policy emphasizes being uncompromising against crime, but is based on systematic and investigated measures. S supports the committee's rejection and votes Yes.

citations.quote: The fight against crime must be uncompromising. The full strength of society must be mobilized to push back the criminals

motivering: S's own motion (Ida Karkiainen et al., item 9) on limited searchability of personal data is rejected by the committee. The manifesto's principle of protected public service and independent media supports regulating the online searchability of personal data. S supports its reservation 8 and votes no.

citations.quote: We want to give public service constitutional protection. Media support should create the conditions for independent, locally rooted news reporting throughout the country.
citations.princip: protection of media freedom and integrity

motivering: The manifesto demands that oversight of healthcare be stepped up to guarantee quality. S's motion (Fredrik Lundh Sammeli et al., S, item 3) requests follow-up on the effects of the new legislation and is rejected by the committee. Requiring follow-up and evaluation of new laws' impact is consistent with S's oversight ambitions, and S supports Reservation 3.

citations.quote: Oversight of healthcare must be stepped up to guarantee quality.
No one should have to worry about receiving care in time.

motivering: The manifesto does not take a specific position on ANDTS policy (alcohol, narcotics, doping, tobacco and gambling) or harm reduction in addiction care. S has no reservation on this matter and no explicit motion among those rejected. Without a clear party position, the committee's proposal is supported.

citations.quote: In the biggest and hardest moments, the welfare state should be there — when a child is born, when someone falls ill, perhaps hovering between life and death, when we need extra support in old age, or when we have stumbled in life.

motivering: S submitted a motion (Åsa Westlund et al., item 20) on coordinated efforts against young offenders, which the committee proposes to reject. The manifesto clearly emphasizes the need for cooperation between police, social services and schools to stop youth crime. S supports its reservation (Alternative A) and votes No against the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: More cooperation is needed between the police, school health services, social services and schools.
No young person should become a criminal. The recruitment of new members must be stopped. We want to see more and further-reaching social measures

motivering: The question of regulating lobbyists and party financing concerns two S motions of its own (Hultqvist, Karkiainen), which the committee rejects. The manifesto does not specifically address lobbyist regulation, but the party's basic view on integrity and the rule of law, together with its active engagement on precisely this issue, argues for supporting the reservation rather than the rejection.

citations.quote: We are equal before the paragraphs of the law book, and in our government agencies dutiful officials with high integrity are at work.

motivering: The rejected motions on activity compensation and sickness compensation come from SD and V, with no S motion of its own on this point. citations.quote: we safeguard the principle that anyone too ill to work should be able to rely on sickness insurance
citations.princip: safeguard the security of sickness insurance

citations.quote: Even in illness, greater financial security is necessary.

motivering: The election manifesto lacks concrete positions on excise duties on electricity, fuel, alcohol, tobacco, air travel or waste. There is no S motion among those rejected. The party's line of a responsible fiscal policy framework and cautious economic policy argues for supporting the committee's rejection of the opposition's tax proposals.

citations.quote: We stand up for the fiscal policy framework and want to develop it to meet the societal problems of our time.
Economic policy needs to be conducted with great caution and respect for the finances of ordinary households.

motivering: The vote concerns the rejection of V's motion (item 19) on protection against the eviction of families with children. The manifesto does not take an explicit position on eviction rules, and V's more radical line does not coincide with S's housing policy position on rental housing for ordinary people. S supports the committee's rejection and votes Yes.

citations.quote: We will continue to build rental housing that ordinary people can afford to live in.

motivering: Among the rejected motions are the Social Democrats' own claims (Haraldsson, Ygeman) on social insurance. The party wants to continue strengthening the social security systems and keep working on improved sickness compensation, which argues for supporting the reservation rather than the committee's rejection of its own claim.

citations.quote: continue working on the proposals to improve sickness compensation
we safeguard the principle that anyone too ill to work should be able to rely on sickness insurance

motivering: The election manifesto demands that preparedness against extreme weather be strengthened and that municipalities continue to be given opportunities to adapt to climate change locally, and that civil defense and crisis preparedness be reinforced. S supports the reservation (Alternative A) against the proposal and votes No.

citations.quote: Strengthen preparedness against extreme weather. Otherwise cloudbursts risk flooding cities, drought risks wiping out entire harvests, and wildfires risk spreading. We want to continue the large investments so that municipalities can adapt to climate change locally.
The work of reinforcing civil defense and crisis preparedness must continue, including through increased resources to equip and build emergency stockpiles for healthcare

citations.quote: It should be safe to grow old in Sweden. We want everyone with home care services to have a designated care contact for greater security.

C's claims on women's participation in post-conflict reconstruction align directly with these principles. S should vote No to support reservation 2.

citations.quote: The UN must continue to pursue issues of women, peace and security.
The rights of girls and women must be strengthened globally.

motivering: The vote concerns rejecting motions (MP, C, V, and others) on the Discrimination Act. citations.quote: Discrimination in the labor market shall be combated.
Decisive action to stop honor-related violence, sexual offenses, and men's violence against women.
citations.princip: decisive action against men's violence against women

S supports the committee's proposal to reject the motions from SD and C.

citations.quote: public employers and procurers shall be role models in working for fair competition. It must never pay off to commit crimes or gain competitive advantages by neglecting employees' right to a safe working environment.

citations.quote: A policy is needed to ease the consequences of the Putin prices.
Guarantee the credibility of the Swedish economy. The Social Democrats will never contribute to undermining Sweden's economy.

motivering: The question of mother-tongue and minority-language instruction includes S's own motion (Åsa Westlund, item 27) among those rejected, together with motions from C, SD, V, and MP. citations.quote: Strong values of equality, gender equality, and mutual respect between people.

Preschool, school, and after-school care are the best tools we have to lift children out of dysfunctional environments and give them a better future. It gives more time to succeed with language and schoolwork.

motivering: S's own motions — Helmersson Olsson and Svantorp, item 31 — on regulating and monitoring the haulage industry are rejected by the committee. citations.quote: Decisive action against work-life crime. Work-life crime must not exist in the Swedish labor market, and public employers and procurers shall be role models in working for fair competition.

citations.quote: It must never pay off to commit crimes or gain competitive advantages by neglecting employees' right to a safe working environment.
citations.princip: safe working environment in the haulage industry

motivering: The manifesto does not take a specific position on mineral compensation. S has no motion of its own in the vote, and the committee's proposal rejects motions from SD, C, and MP. citations.quote: Strengthen the long-term conditions for entrepreneurship and innovation.

citations.quote: Segregation is not broken by special solutions for the resource-poor. Housing and tenure forms shall be mixed. Overcrowding shall be combated. We shall continue to build rental housing that ordinary people can afford to live in.
citations.princip: mixed housing tenure and housing construction

motivering: The election manifesto does not specifically address support for cinemas in smaller towns. Without a divergent S position, the party follows the committee's rejection of the motions.

citations.quote: Sweden shall have a vibrant, free, and independent cultural life that both strengthens togetherness and challenges.
citations.princip: vibrant cultural life throughout the country

citations.quote: Media subsidies shall provide the conditions for independent and locally rooted news reporting throughout the country.

motivering: The committee wants to reject the motion by Jennie Nilsson et al. (S), item 21 — S's own proposal on public housing companies (allmännyttan) and the Public Procurement Act (LOU). Reservation 10 is the party's own line. The manifesto's promise of rental housing for ordinary people and democratic control of welfare supports requiring social criteria in procurement. The party should vote No.

citations.quote: We shall continue to build rental housing that ordinary people can afford to live in.
Enough is enough. The Swedish people shall govern Swedish welfare, and money shall not fatten venture capitalists instead of securing welfare throughout our country.

motivering: S has its own motions (Eva Lindh et al., two motions) in this vote that the committee majority wants to reject. citations.quote: The fight against crime shall be uncompromising. The full force of society shall be mobilized to push back criminals, cut off recruitment into crime, and increase safety.
Confidentiality barriers between authorities shall be torn down so that the police and other professional groups can do their job.

citations.quote: The Social Democrats will never contribute to giving power to the Sweden Democrats, a party that does not stand up for the equal value and rights of all people.

motivering: S submitted motions (Jennie Nilsson et al., items 17, 19, and 20) on rental housing that the committee proposes to reject. The manifesto emphasizes building rental housing at reasonable costs and combating overcrowding. S supports its own reservation (Alternative A) and votes No against the committee's rejection of its own motion items.

citations.quote: We shall continue to build rental housing that ordinary people can afford to live in.
Overcrowding shall be combated.

motivering: S has its own motion (Sätherberg motion 16) on animal welfare and competitiveness, which the committee proposes to reject. citations.quote: public employers and procurers should be role models in promoting sound competition

motivering: The manifesto establishes that the climate policy framework shall remain firm and that state investments should increase the pace of the transition. The party should vote No.

citations.quote: The climate policy framework shall remain firm. Through state investments we can increase the pace of industry's transition and facilitate a climate-smart life.
Sweden shall become the world's first fossil-free welfare nation.

motivering: The election manifesto does not specifically address national minorities or minority languages. citations.quote: Strong values of equality, gender equality and respect between people.
everyone takes part and contributes, and no one is left behind

citations.quote: The climate transition is the defining issue of our time.
The climate policy framework shall remain firm.

motivering: S's commitment to tough measures against honor-related violence is clear in the manifesto, and child marriage is part of this problem area. S votes with the committee's proposal to reject the SD motion.

citations.quote: We want to continue the political direction that has toughened the penalties for violence and other violations in close relationships, and that has increased resources for the important work of women's and girls' shelters.
The Social Democrats will never help give power to the Sweden Democrats, a party that does not stand up for the equal worth and rights of all people.

motivering: S wants to stop the recruitment of new members into crime through social measures and tougher penalties. The committee refers to ongoing inquiries and preparatory work on the subject. S pursues the issue of young offenders through a coherent strategy and does not need to support V's specific motion for an action plan for boys and men.

citations.quote: No young person should become a criminal. The recruitment of new members must be stopped. We want to see more and further-reaching social measures, and parents should be obliged to participate when their children need social services' interventions.
Toughen the penalties to keep criminals off the streets.

motivering: The election manifesto establishes that the climate policy framework shall remain firm and that municipalities should be given the means to adapt to climate change locally, which includes taking climate considerations into account in spatial planning and the planning of green areas. The committee majority's rejection of these motions runs counter to S's climate commitments. As an opposition party, S supports the reservation (Alternative A) and votes No.

citations.quote: The climate policy framework shall remain firm.
We want to continue the major investments so that municipalities can adapt to climate change locally.

motivering: S has no motion of its own on oversight of the taxi industry. S votes with the committee (Yes).

citations.quote: Tough measures against work-life crime. Work-life crime should have no place in the Swedish labour market

citations.quote: We stand up for open, free and fair trade. For a small, export-dependent country like Sweden, global trade is absolutely crucial, not least for keeping prices down and countering inflation.

omvarld.faktor: Inflation 12% (CPI annual rate, Feb 2023)
omvarld.effekt: Strengthens the manifesto's argument that free trade keeps prices down – makes the free-trade principle especially relevant

motivering: The committee's tillkännagivande (formal request) on a zero-vision against violence in close relationships is directly compatible with S's strong commitment against men's violence against women. The motions from C and MP concern inquiry mandates assessed as already covered by ongoing work, which S can accept in light of the positive tillkännagivande.

citations.quote: Tough measures to stop honor-related violence, sexual offenses and men's violence against women. We want to continue the political direction that has toughened the penalties for violence and other violations in close relationships

citations.quote: Discrimination in the labour market shall be countered.

motivering: The manifesto demands that tax fraud and welfare crime be stopped. citations.quote: Tax fraud, welfare crime and money laundering shall be stopped.

motivering: The manifesto emphasizes continuing the political direction already embarked upon against men's violence against women and honor-related violence, rather than new inquiries. citations.quote: We want to continue the political direction that has toughened the penalties for violence and other violations in close relationships, and that has increased resources for the important work of women's and girls' shelters.

motivering: The election manifesto does not address VAT rules for non-profit associations' internal services. citations.quote: We Social Democrats stand for responsible leadership for Sweden – both in crisis and in good times.

motivering: One of the rejected motions is S's own (Jennie Nilsson et al., item 32) on rental housing (hyresrätt). citations.quote: We will continue to build rental housing that ordinary people can afford to live in.

motivering: The election manifesto sets out overarching principles on international law, human rights and the UN's role, but does not take a specific position on the Middle East issues the motions concern. citations.quote: We will continue the work to increase respect for human rights, democracy and a rules-based world order and global security.

citations.quote: The fight against crime must be uncompromising. The full force of society must be mobilized to push back the criminals, cut off recruitment into crime and increase safety.

motivering: The manifesto does not cover the Riksdag's working procedures. The closest applicable principle is S's general demand for democratic transparency and oversight. citations.quote: The principle of public access to official records (offentlighetsprincipen) should also apply to private health and social care.

motivering: The committee rejects S's own motion 7 on compensation for mineral extraction. S supports its own position and votes No to mark support for Reservation 14. The question of compensation for mineral extraction is not explicit in the manifesto, but S's motion is in line with the green industrial transition and fair conditions.

citations.quote: Now we are manufacturing fossil-free steel in Sweden, we are building electric cars, and we are seeing closed-down industries turn into battery factories.
Strengthen the long-term conditions for entrepreneurship and innovation.

motivering: Recycling of innovation-critical metals and minerals is not specifically mentioned in S's election manifesto. There are no S motions in this vote. The committee refers to ongoing EU work, which is in line with S's confidence in EU cooperation. The author and content of Reservation 10 are unclear.

citations.quote: We are convinced that EU cooperation is the foundation for solving many of the toughest problems of our time.

motivering: The election manifesto sets language requirements within the labor market and integration but does not address language issues linked to public service broadcasting or film policy. The committee considers that work is already underway in the area, and without its own S position on precisely this point, the party follows the rejection of the motions.

citations.quote: We want to give public service broadcasting constitutional protection.
Media support should provide conditions for independent and locally rooted news reporting throughout the country.

motivering: The election manifesto establishes that the right to personal assistance must be secured and that people with disabilities should be able to live their lives like others. The Left Party's (V) motions on support for people with disabilities in crisis preparedness are consistent with these fundamental commitments. S supports the reservation against the committee's rejection and votes No.

citations.quote: We will secure the right to personal assistance and continue working on the proposals to improve sickness compensation.
The work to strengthen civil defense and crisis preparedness must continue, including through increased resources to equip and build emergency stockpiles for healthcare
citations.princip: strengthened civil defense and crisis preparedness

motivering: The Social Democrats have their own motions (6–9, Fredrik Olovsson et al. (S)) on intellectual property rights that the committee proposes to reject. The manifesto's goal of strengthening innovation and a vibrant cultural life justifies the party having defended these positions in its motion. S supports Reservation 6 (Alternative A) and votes No against the committee's rejection proposal.

citations.quote: Strengthen the long-term conditions for entrepreneurship and innovation
Sweden shall have a vibrant, free and independent cultural life that both strengthens cohesion and challenges

motivering: Zoo operations are not addressed in S's election manifesto. There are no S motions on the matter, and the committee refers to ongoing international work. Without support in the manifesto or its own motions, there is no reason to deviate from the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: At the same time, species extinction is accelerating and biological diversity is under threat.

motivering: The manifesto establishes that the tightened migration policy remains in place. The rejected motions (including from the Green Party (MP) and the Centre Party (C)) point toward a more generous asylum and migration policy than the one S supports, which is why the committee's rejection is in line with the party's position.

citations.quote: We have tightened migration policy, and this line stands firm.

motivering: Both of the rejected motions are S's own (Kristoffer Lindberg and Ardalan Shekarabi on gun crime), and the manifesto contains a clear commitment to tougher penalties for gun crime. S should therefore support its reservation and vote against the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: We want to double the penalty for aggravated gun crimes.
Toughen penalties to keep criminals off the streets.

motivering: The election manifesto emphasizes a stronger link between education and the needs of the labour market, as well as strengthened vocational learning, but does not propose any special system of industry schools (branschskolor). The committee refers to ongoing inquiry work, and without an S reservation of its own on this particular motion, the party follows the rejection.

citations.quote: There should be a stronger link between the educations offered and the need for staff that exists in society.
citations.princip: link between education and the labour market

citations.quote: Being able to learn a trade in parallel with studying Swedish is a further way to increase the chance of getting a job.

motivering: The election manifesto says nothing specifically about digitizing Sweden's film heritage. The party's cultural policy line is about a vibrant cultural life throughout the country, but it provides no concrete grounds for opposing the committee's assessment that the work is already underway. The party therefore follows the rejection.

citations.quote: Sweden shall have a vibrant, free and independent cultural life that both strengthens togetherness and challenges.

motivering: The manifesto does not directly address ANDTS policy (alcohol, drugs, doping, tobacco and gambling). The closest applicable principle is that welfare should be there in difficult moments. The established ANDTS policy, which the committee defends, supports this better than SD's reservation 17. S should support the committee's rejection and vote Yes.

citations.quote: In the biggest and most difficult moments, welfare should be there – when a child is born, when someone falls ill, perhaps hovering between life and death, when we need extra support in our old age, or when we have taken a wrong turn in life.

motivering: Family-reunification immigration (anhöriginvandring) falls under the party's overall line that the tightened migration policy should remain in place. The reservation, driven partly by the Left Party (Vänsterpartiet), points toward a more generous line on family-reunification immigration than S wants to see, which is why the committee's rejection is supported.

citations.quote: We have tightened migration policy, and this line remains firm.

motivering: The election manifesto demands that civil defence and crisis preparedness be strengthened, including through increased resources for stockpiling and the transport sector. The committee's proposal to reject the motions on the crisis-preparedness system is incompatible with S's commitments to a strong and cohesive crisis-preparedness system. S supports the reservation (Alternative A) and votes No.

citations.quote: The work to strengthen civil defence and crisis preparedness must continue, including through increased resources to equip and build stockpiles for healthcare
citations.princip: strengthened civil defence and crisis preparedness

motivering: The manifesto demands that tax fraud and welfare crime be stopped. The legislation gives the Swedish Tax Agency (Skatteverket) more effective tools against errors in the population register, with built-in privacy safeguards. C's and SD's reservations (reservation 8) diverge in different directions from this balanced proposal. The party supports the committee's line and votes Yes.

citations.quote: Tax fraud, welfare crime and money laundering shall be stopped.

motivering: The election manifesto contains no proposals for changed VAT rates or exemptions of the kind the motions (from SD, C and MP) raise. No S motion is among those rejected, and the party's focus on responsible, prudent economic policy argues for supporting the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Economic policy needs to be conducted with great care and respect for the finances of ordinary households.

motivering: The case shows that the only reservation (Reservation 20) on this point covers the same motions the committee rejects, including S's own motion (Ida Karkiainen et al., item 6) on party financing. The election manifesto does not address the issue specifically, but since S's own motion is among the proposals the reservation defends, the party should vote for its own line rather than for rejection.

citations.quote: We are equal before the paragraphs of the law book, and in our authorities dutiful officials work with high integrity.

motivering: The committee rejects S's own motions 31 and 32 on the working environment in the haulage and taxi industries. The manifesto's explicit demand that it should never pay off to neglect employees' right to a safe working environment directly supports a No vote. S votes against the committee in support of Reservation 19.

citations.quote: It should never pay off to commit crimes or gain competitive advantages by neglecting employees' right to a safe working environment.
A firm crackdown on labour-market crime. Labour-market crime shall have no place in the Swedish labour market

motivering: S has no motions of its own in this case on streamlining state administration. The manifesto states that the state should be present throughout the country and take responsibility for the supply of skilled labour, but it contains no specific demands that compel S to support V's or C's individual motions. The committee's reference to ongoing work is consistent with S's principles.

citations.quote: The state shall be present throughout the country
The state has a responsibility to secure the supply of skilled labour, not least in the welfare sector

motivering: The manifesto calls for strong multilateral aid and support for the UN's role. The committee's proposal means that the communication is filed away (lagd till handlingarna) and that SD's restrictive aid motions are rejected, which is consistent with S's line. S has no motion among those rejected, and the sponsor of Reservation 5 is unknown; S supports the committee's procedural proposal.

citations.quote: we double the climate aid.
We will continue to safeguard the UN's role in the work for international law and international cooperation

motivering: The manifesto demands that 'tax fraud, welfare crime, and money laundering must be stopped' and that confidentiality barriers between authorities be torn down. The Swedish Tax Agency's (Skatteverket) strengthened data analysis tool for preventing fraud in the population register (folkbokföring) is directly in line with this. The Social Democrats (S) support the committee's proposal to reject the Sweden Democrats' (SD) motions (items 28 and 32), which deviate from this line.

citations.quote: Tax fraud, welfare crime, and money laundering must be stopped
Confidentiality barriers between authorities shall be torn down so that the police and other professional groups can do their job

motivering: The election manifesto prioritizes decisive action against sexual offenses and men's violence against women, as well as strengthened protection for crime victims. The right to a legal counsel for the injured party (målsägandebiträde) is a central tool for strengthening crime victims' position in the legal process, consistent with these commitments. S supports the reservation against the committee's rejection and votes No.

citations.quote: Decisive action to stop honor-related violence, sexual offenses, and men's violence against women. We want to continue the political direction that has toughened penalties for violence and other violations in close relationships, and that has increased resources for the important work of women's and girls' shelters.
citations.princip: protection for crime victims and those subjected to violence

motivering: S submitted its own motion on mink farming (Sanna Backeskog et al.) which the committee is now rejecting. The existence of the party's own motion shows that the party has taken a position on the issue. S should vote No and support Reservation 16.

citations.quote: At the same time, species extinction is accelerating and biodiversity is under threat.
citations.princip: environmental and climate consequences of animal husbandry

motivering: The committee's tillkännagivande (formal request) for a zero-vision against violence in close relationships partially approves several of S's own motions (Thorell, Carvalho, Shekarabi). This is entirely in line with the manifesto's demand for decisive action against men's violence against women, so S should support the proposal.

citations.quote: Decisive action to stop honor-related violence, sexual offenses, and men's violence against women.
citations.princip: zero-vision on violence in close relationships

motivering: The committee rejects S's own motion (Anna-Caren Sätherberg et al., item 36) on legislation regarding endocrine-disrupting substances; Reservation 16 is S's alternative. The manifesto lacks specific text on chemicals but commits S to environmental protection and the polluter-pays principle. The party votes No to support its reservation.

citations.quote: the defining issue of our time. We risk destroying our only planet and the conditions for living in many places, which will lead to enormous migration pressure. At the same time, species extinction is accelerating and biodiversity is under threat.
We shall work to introduce a global carbon price based on the principle that the polluter pays

motivering: The manifesto does not address rules on division of property (bodelning) or divorce, and the rejected motions come from V (the Left Party) and SD (the Sweden Democrats), not S. Without its own documented position and without an S motion in conflict, the party reasonably aligns itself with the committee's rejection.

The question of special crime-victim status for children exploited in child pornography (a motion from MP, the Green Party) is not specifically addressed by the manifesto, and it is not S's own motion that is being rejected. S therefore reasonably aligns itself with the committee's rejection, lacking its own clear position on this particular point.

The election manifesto places great emphasis on rapidly expanding electricity production and reducing price differences to push down electricity prices, which is already the party's answer to the situation the motions on electricity price issues address. Without an S reservation of its own on this point, the party follows the committee's rejection of SD's and V's motions.

citations.quote: We need to expand electricity production to get more cheap electricity, quickly, not least in southern Sweden.
We want to ensure that revenues from capacity fees that are not used for grid investments are used both to reduce price differences and lower costs.

motivering: The rejected motion is S's own (Ardalan Shekarabi, item 70 on a special crime victims act). The manifesto does not specifically mention such an act, but since it is the party's own motion that is being rejected, S should reasonably support its reservation rather than the committee's rejection.

The party has no explicit motions in this vote on copyright. The committee rejects motions primarily from SD and C (the Centre Party). The manifesto supports the values of cultural life but gives no reason to vote for SD's or C's reservation position. S supports the committee's rejection and votes Yes.

citations.quote: Sweden shall have a living, free, and independent cultural life that both strengthens togetherness and challenges

motivering: S has several of its own motions (Järrebring, Vepsä items 2 and 11, Nilsson items 1-3) that the committee majority wants to reject. The election manifesto actively advocates building rental housing, combating overcrowding, and working against residential segregation. Supporting the committee's proposal would mean that the party's own motions are rejected, which directly conflicts with the party's housing policy commitments. The party votes No.

citations.quote: Overcrowding shall be combated. We shall continue to build rental housing that ordinary people can afford to live in.
Segregation is not broken by special solutions for the resource-poor. Housing and tenure forms shall be mixed.

motivering: The question of courts' jurisdiction in custody cases (V's motion) is not addressed in the manifesto, and it is not an S motion that is being rejected. In the absence of its own documented position, S reasonably aligns itself with the committee's rejection of V's motion.

The election manifesto explicitly states that the equalization system needs to be reviewed to ensure equivalent public services throughout the country, including in small municipalities. Several of the rejected motions, including two from S, concern precisely this system, which means the reservation's line is closer to the party's own position than the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: To secure welfare throughout the country, we need to review the tax equalization system, so that it guarantees high-quality public services throughout the country, even in small municipalities struggling with their population base.
Increase resources for welfare throughout the country.

motivering: S's climate policy is based on state investments, not private tax subsidies. The motions on a green tax deduction and green tax shift originate from MP and C, not S. Large tax cuts undermine the welfare resources that S prioritizes. S supports the committee's rejection and has no alternative of its own in Reservation 11.

citations.quote: Through state investments, we can increase the pace of industry's transition and facilitate a climate-smart life
Large tax cuts make that impossible

motivering: The committee approves S's own motion item 6 with a tillkännagivande (formal request) on the advisory and solution-oriented role of authorities in permit processes. The manifesto's demand to tear down bureaucratic obstacles and speed up permit processes coincides with the committee's proposal. S votes Yes.

citations.quote: Tear down the bureaucratic obstacles to more electricity. Slow permit processes must be sped up.
Strengthen the long-term conditions for entrepreneurship and innovation.

motivering: S has its own motion (Fredrik Lundh Sammeli et al., item 64) in the matter concerning ANDTS policy (alcohol, narcotics, doping, tobacco and gambling policy), which the committee proposes that the Riksdag reject. The manifesto states that the Swedish people should control welfare and that the fragmentary privatization should be stopped — principles that likely underpin S's motion. S votes No to uphold its own line.

citations.quote: The Swedish people should control Swedish welfare and money should not feed venture capitalists instead of securing welfare throughout our country
Enough is enough. The Swedish people should control Swedish welfare

motivering: Specific regulation of the detailed development plan requirement is not covered by S's election manifesto. The motions in the vote are from V and M — S has no reservation. Without coverage, S supports the committee's standard proposal to reject the motions.

citations.quote: We will continue to build rental housing that ordinary people can afford to live in

motivering: The committee rejects S's own motion item 2 on Natura 2000 permits within mineral policy. S supports its reservation (Reservation 3) and votes No. The manifesto's demand that the climate policy framework remain firm supports a restrictive stance on mineral extraction in protected nature areas.

citations.quote: The climate policy framework must remain firm.
The climate transition is the defining issue of our time.

motivering: The manifesto addresses youth crime primarily with social measures, early support from schools and social services, and parental responsibility, not the specific surveillance measure that SD's motion (not S's own) proposes. The committee's rejection refers to ongoing investigative and preparatory work, which matches the party's view that the issue is already being handled.

citations.quote: We want to see more and more far-reaching social measures, and parents should be obliged to participate when their children need social services' interventions.
Tougher penalties to keep criminals off the streets.

motivering: The party's weapons policy targets weapons trafficking to organized crime and serious weapons offences, not the supervision of shooting ranges or the processing of licenses for legal firearm owners, which is the content of C's motion. The committee's reference to ongoing preparatory work is in line with a responsible process already underway.

citations.quote: We want to take firm action against the trafficking of weapons and drugs, including through strengthened border control.
We want to double the penalty for serious weapons offences.

motivering: The election manifesto lacks specific positions on the organization of public health work, infection control, or vaccination issues, beyond a general desire to increase resources for welfare. The committee's rejection, which refers to ongoing work, does not conflict with any stated party position, so the closest line is to accept the proposal.

citations.quote: Increase resources for welfare throughout the country.

motivering: The manifesto states that S stands for open, free and fair trade and that WTO cooperation should be strengthened. S has no motions of its own in this trade policy matter on sustainable business. Without documentary support for adopting C's, SD's or MP's reserved motions as an alternative, S supports the committee's recommendation.

citations.quote: We stand for open, free and fair trade
Global cooperation within the WTO should be strengthened, as should cooperation with like-minded countries

motivering: The manifesto seeks to promote climate-smart travel and public transport through investments and a new travel deduction, but makes no demand for a reduced energy tax on electrically powered public transport. The motions come from C and V, and no S motion is among those rejected, which is why the committee's rejection is supported.

citations.quote: Through massive investments in both new and existing railways, more people will be able to travel in a climate-smart way by train.

motivering: S submitted its own motions on a new resource allocation system (Åsa Westlund et al., items 1–4), which are rejected. The manifesto is explicit: the school voucher (skolpeng) should become fairer and independent schools should not be overcompensated. S should support Reservation 1 and vote No.

citations.quote: The school voucher (skolpeng) must become fairer so that independent schools are not overcompensated in a way that harms students in municipal schools.
Take back control of schools. Schools should be for the children, not the owners.

motivering: S's economic policy prioritizes responsible fiscal policy and explicitly warns against measures that drive inflation. With inflation at 11.7 percent, a higher basic tax allowance risks fueling prices further, which runs counter to S's line. S prefers targeted support measures and full employment over broad tax cuts.

citations.quote: taking on debt to compensate for every single price increase would fuel inflation and, in the long run, jeopardize public finances, welfare and pensions
Economic policy needs to be conducted with great care and respect for ordinary households' finances

omvarld.faktor: Inflation 11.7% (Jan 2023)
omvarld.effekt: The high-inflation environment reinforces the manifesto's warning against inflation-driving measures and argues against a broad basic tax allowance

motivering: The manifesto explicitly states that Sweden should join NATO and that the application has already been submitted. The committee's proposal to approve the accession and the status-of-forces agreement is fully in line with S's established security policy. As a consequence, S rejects the Left Party (V) and Green Party (MP) motions against NATO accession.

citations.quote: Sweden should join NATO. Swedish membership in NATO is the best path for our country's security, and Sweden has therefore submitted its membership application.
citations.princip: NATO accession as a security policy priority

citations.quote: Russia's war of aggression has severely worsened security in our region. Swedish non-alignment served Sweden well for a long time. But now even more cooperation is needed, with security guarantees, to safeguard our peace and freedom.

motivering: S has its own motions (items 4-8, Jennie Nilsson et al.) on housing provision that the committee majority wants to reject. The party's manifesto calls for more rental housing, combating overcrowding, and mixed forms of tenure. S supports its reservation (Alternative A: Reservation 12), which reflects these commitments.

citations.quote: We will continue to build rental housing that ordinary people can afford to live in
Overcrowding must be combated
Housing and tenure forms should be mixed

motivering: The manifesto expresses strong support for women's right to decide over their own bodies and for safe abortion, but frames this as a global aid issue, not a domestic legislative change. Without any indication that the Centre Party (C) motion strengthens rather than restricts these rights, and given the committee's reference to ongoing work, the closest position is to support the rejection.

citations.quote: We Social Democrats stand up for all women's right to decide over their own bodies. Safe abortion must be a right for women throughout the world.
citations.princip: women's right over their own bodies

motivering: S has its own motions (Caroline Helmersson Olsson et al. and Ida Karkiainen et al., item 8) on transparency and information sharing that the committee rejects. The manifesto demands that confidentiality barriers between authorities be torn down and that the principle of public access be strengthened. S votes No to uphold its documented position on increased information sharing.

citations.quote: Confidentiality barriers between authorities must be torn down so that the police and other professionals can do their jobs
The principle of public access should also apply to private health and social care

motivering: The manifesto wants to build rental housing at a reasonable cost but does not take a position on the rent-setting system, presumption rents, or tenant-ownership rules in detail, and no S motion is included in the current vote. The committee's rejection, with reference to ongoing work and earlier positions, is closest to the party's cautious line.

citations.quote: We will continue to build rental housing that ordinary people can afford to live in.
citations.princip: rental housing at a reasonable cost

motivering: Protection for vulnerable women in migration cases is not specifically regulated in the manifesto, which instead establishes that the tightened migration line stands firm, and the committee refers to existing regulations. The motions come solely from the Centre Party, which is why the committee's rejection is supported despite the party's clear commitment against men's violence against women.

citations.quote: We have tightened migration policy, and this line stands firm.
Decisive action to stop honor-related violence, sexual offences and men's violence against women.
citations.princip: decisive action against violence against women

motivering: S has its own motion (item 7.1, Mattias Vepsä et al. (S)) on regulatory simplification for businesses that the committee rejects. The manifesto emphasizes that the conditions for entrepreneurship and innovation should be strengthened. The party supports its reservation (Reservation 6) and votes No against the committee's rejection proposal.

citations.quote: Strengthen the long-term conditions for entrepreneurship and innovation

motivering: The manifesto advocates a multilateral global carbon price based on the 'polluter pays principle' rather than unilateral climate tariffs, and states that S stands up for free and fair trade. Without its own motions and without documentary support for C's motions on climate tariffs specifically, S votes Yes with the committee's recommendation.

citations.quote: We will work to have a global carbon price introduced based on the polluter-pays principle
We stand up for open, free and fair trade

motivering: S has no motions of its own on the matter of registering children at two addresses in the population register. The manifesto does not address this specific issue, but S's commitment to stopping welfare crime supports the overall purpose of the committee report. S finds no documentary basis to support C's motions against the committee's recommendation.

citations.quote: Tax fraud, welfare crime and money laundering must be stopped

motivering: The manifesto states that the Social Democrats will never help give power to the Sweden Democrats. The committee's recommendation to reject the SD motion (Matheus Enholm et al., item 13) on flag-flying rules is directly supported by S. S votes Yes.

citations.quote: The Social Democrats will never help give power to the Sweden Democrats, a party that does not stand up for the equal value and rights of all people

motivering: The election manifesto does not address adoption law issues at all, and no S motion is included among those being rejected; the committee also notes that the government is already working on family law matters. Without an explicit party position to rely on, the closest stance is to accept the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Strong values of equality, gender equality and respect between people.

motivering: Hunting and wildlife management are not addressed in S's election manifesto. The motions in this vote are from C and SD; S has no reservation. Without manifesto coverage, S backs the committee's rejection as the default position.

citations.quote: At the same time, species extinction is accelerating and biological diversity is under threat

motivering: S's pension policy is built on the collective system with a raised pension contribution, not private savings deductions. The motions on deductions for private pension and housing savings do not align with S's systemic solution. SD's demand 2 is rejected, which S supports. S has no reservation in this matter.

citations.quote: Our goal is for everyone to receive at least 70 percent of their final salary in pension. For that to be possible, the pension contribution must be raised
We stand up for the security pension (trygghetspensionen), which is being challenged by forces from the right, and want to improve the pension supplement

motivering: S's own motion 28 (Shekarabi et al.) on a licensing requirement is rejected by the committee; Reservation 2 is likely S's own reservation. The party's manifesto wants to give the police more tools and tear down confidentiality barriers — a line that supports municipalities' expanded powers for supervision and crime prevention. S supports its own reservation.

citations.quote: The police also need more tools, such as better options for wiretapping and house searches. Confidentiality barriers between authorities must be torn down so that the police and other professional groups can do their job.
The fight against crime must be uncompromising

motivering: The committee's proposal approves S's own motion (Anna-Caren Sätherberg et al., motion 41) on creating and restoring wetlands. The manifesto supports climate adaptation and strengthened preparedness against extreme weather, including cloudbursts and drought. Voting Yes means S's own demands are met.

citations.quote: Strengthen preparedness against extreme weather. Otherwise cloudbursts risk flooding cities, drought risks wiping out entire harvests, and forest fires risk spreading. We want to continue the major investments so that municipalities can adapt to climate change locally.
The climate policy framework shall remain fixed. Through state investments we can increase the pace of industry's transition and make a climate-smart life easier.

motivering: S's program demands more trained staff in elderly care and a new elderly care act — reform demands that the committee's rejection, citing 'ongoing work', does not meet. Reservation 39 is assessed to represent S's demand for strengthened preventive health work and staffing in elderly care.

citations.quote: More people shall be trained and employed in elderly care, and oversight of staff's working environment shall be improved.
citations.princip: more trained staff in elderly care

citations.quote: We want a new elderly care act that ensures everyone receives equally good care throughout the country and access to nurses around the clock.
citations.princip: act on equal care and access to health services

motivering: A so-called 'class allowance' (klasspeng) that gives more resources to pupils with a weaker socioeconomic background aligns with S's principle that disadvantaged schools should be prioritized and that parents' wallets should not be decisive. S should support Reservation 3 and vote No.

citations.quote: The most disadvantaged schools and preschools must receive more resources.
Parents' wallets should not be decisive.

motivering: The manifesto's tough stance against crime — tougher sentences, more police officers, and firm action against organized crime — presupposes sufficient capacity within the correctional service for more inmates, which is the core of S member Shekarabi's rejected motion on more prison and remand places. The reservation's position is therefore closer to the party's policy than an outright rejection.

citations.quote: Toughen sentences to keep criminals off the streets. We want to toughen sentences, among other things, for gang-related crime, for those who commit repeated and serious crimes, and for those who support organized crime.
Substantially increase the number of police officers on our streets and squares.

motivering: Specific exemptions from the building permit requirement are not covered by S's election manifesto. The motions are from C; S has no reservation. Without manifesto coverage, S supports the committee's rejection of the motions.

citations.quote: We shall continue to build rental housing that ordinary people can afford to live in

motivering: Pastures, grazing land, and hay meadows are not specifically mentioned in S's election manifesto. No S motions exist. The author and content of Reservation 29 are unclear. Without manifesto support, backing the committee's rejection is most consistent.

citations.quote: At the same time, species extinction is accelerating and biological diversity is under threat.

motivering: The matter concerns social security systems for self-employed people in the cultural sector, where the party's own motion (Lawen Redar et al.) is among the motions being rejected. The party wants 'secure insurance built on the idea of duty and right' and increased financial security in case of illness, which argues for supporting its own reservation instead of the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Sweden shall have secure insurance built on the idea of duty and right.
Also in case of illness, greater financial security is necessary.
citations.princip: increased security in case of illness

motivering: S has its own motions (Morgan Johansson motion 2, Fredrik Olovsson motion 19) on international aid that the committee wants to reject. The party's manifesto demands doubled climate aid, a focus on the poor, and prioritization of women's and children's rights. S supports its own reservation (Alternative A: Reservation 6).

citations.quote: That is why we want to double the climate aid
The work to reduce poverty must continue
Poor people's perspectives and women's and children's rights shall be at the center
citations.princip: focus on the poor and gender equality

motivering: S has its own motion (6, Mathias Tegnér et al. (S)) on impact assessments that the committee rejects. The manifesto's goal of strengthening the conditions for entrepreneurship and innovation includes well-developed impact analyses of regulations. S supports Reservation 19 and votes No.

citations.quote: Strengthen the long-term conditions for entrepreneurship and innovation

motivering: Lead ammunition in hunting is not covered by S's election manifesto. S has no motions in the vote and no reservation (dissenting opinion). Without coverage, S supports the committee's rejection as the default position.

citations.quote: At the same time, species extinction is accelerating and biological diversity is under threat

motivering: The election manifesto does not address forms of ownership for the Prison and Probation Service's (Kriminalvården's) premises. The closest applicable principle is opposition to the piecemeal privatization of socially essential services, but the content of the SD motion is imprecise and the committee refers to ongoing inquiries. S therefore follows the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: No emergency hospitals shall be sold off.

motivering: S has three of its own motions (Sofia Skönnbrink et al., Eva Lindh et al., Niklas Karlsson et al., items 4 and 5) on the earned income tax credit and tax reduction for sickness and activity compensation, which the committee rejects. The manifesto states that S safeguards the sickness insurance system. Reservation 1 (dissenting opinion 1) is S's alternative, and the party votes No.

citations.quote: we safeguard the principle that anyone too sick to work should be able to rely on sickness insurance
Reduce the injustice of the waiting period (karens). The waiting-period deduction creates an economic injustice that hits members of LO's [Swedish Trade Union Confederation] unions hard
citations.princip: Reduce the injustice of the waiting period

motivering: No S motion is included in this item on social security systems for entrepreneurs; the motions come from C, SD and MP. The party's manifesto directs its social security reforms (unemployment insurance, sickness insurance) at employees rather than the self-employed and emphasizes cautious economic policy, which supports backing the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Economic policy needs to be conducted with great caution and respect for ordinary households' finances.
If parties were to outbid each other with borrowed money, it would end with higher mortgage rates and even higher prices.

motivering: The committee's proposal rejects S's own motion (Anna-Caren Sätherberg et al., item 33) on the protection of drinking water sources. S should vote No to support reservation 30 (dissenting opinion 30) and stand by its own demand. The manifesto supports climate adaptation against cloudbursts and drought, which directly concerns water supply.

citations.quote: Strengthen preparedness against extreme weather. Otherwise, cloudbursts risk flooding cities, drought risks wiping out entire harvests, and forest fires risk spreading. We want to continue the major investments so that municipalities can adapt to climate change locally.
The climate policy framework shall remain firm. Through state investments we can increase the pace of industry's transition and make a climate-smart life easier.

motivering: S has an explicit motion (Ardalan Shekarabi et al., item 58) on offenses of violation of personal integrity (fridskränkningsbrott) that the committee rejects. The manifesto commits the party to continuing the political direction that has toughened penalties for violations in close relationships. Reservation 4 (dissenting opinion 4) is S's alternative, and the party votes No to support its reservation on strengthened protection.

citations.quote: We want to continue the political direction that has toughened the penalties for violence and other violations in close relationships, and that has increased resources for the important work of women's and girls' shelters
citations.princip: Tougher penalties for violations in close relationships

citations.quote: Robust measures to stop honor-related violence, sexual offenses and men's violence against women

motivering: The election manifesto states that 'Tax fraud, welfare crime and money laundering shall be stopped' and that confidentiality barriers between authorities shall be torn down. The legislative proposal gives the Swedish Tax Agency (Skatteverket) tools to prevent population-registration fraud and crimes against the welfare systems – directly in line with these commitments. The reservation from V (the counter-proposal) works against this purpose. S should support the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: Tax fraud, welfare crime and money laundering shall be stopped.
Confidentiality barriers between authorities shall be torn down so that the police and other professional groups can do their job.
citations.princip: tear down confidentiality barriers for oversight

motivering: The election manifesto contains no specific commitments regarding municipal organization or the composition of municipal councils (fullmäktige). SD's motions are among those the Committee on the Constitution (KU) proposes to reject, and S has a principled refusal to grant power to SD. The party has no reason to support Reservation 3 (dissenting opinion 3) over the committee's proposal. S should vote Yes.

citations.quote: The Social Democrats will never help give power to the Sweden Democrats, a party that does not stand up for the equal value and rights of all people.

motivering: The election manifesto specifically highlights cooperation between police, student health services, social services and schools as crucial for breaking young people away from crime. This is closely aligned with the Left Party's (Vänsterpartiet's) motion on social intervention groups, so S should support the reservation (dissenting opinion) over the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: More cooperation is needed between police, student health services, social services and schools.
No young person should become a criminal. New recruitment [into crime] must be stopped.

motivering: The election manifesto does not address mandatory education for those convicted of purchasing sex as a policy instrument, despite a general call for robust measures against sexual offenses and violence against women. Without a specific link to this proposal, S follows the committee's rejection of the Left Party's motion.

citations.quote: Robust measures to stop honor-related violence, sexual offenses and men's violence against women.

motivering: The manifesto explicitly demands round-the-clock access to nurses within elder care. The committee's rejection of motions on medical availability conflicts with S's concrete reform demands. Reservation 23 (dissenting opinion 23) is assessed as being in line with S's position on strengthened health care for the elderly.

citations.quote: We want a new elder care act that ensures everyone receives equally good care throughout the country and access to nurses around the clock.
More people shall be trained and employed within elder care, and oversight of staff's working environment shall be improved.

motivering: The manifesto contains no specific commitments regarding a marine environment act. The motions belong to V and MP, and the committee refers to ongoing work. Without a position of its own on the matter, S should support the committee's line rather than take the initiative on the basis of other parties' specific legislative proposals.

citations.quote: Sweden shall be a strong force in the UN and the EU for the world's countries to increase their commitments to realize the ambitions of the Paris Agreement.
The climate policy framework shall remain firm.

motivering: Citizen influence in physical planning is not specifically covered by S's election manifesto. The motions are from C, SD and V; S has no reservation (dissenting opinion). Without coverage, S supports the committee's rejection as the default position.

citations.quote: The Swedish people shall govern Swedish welfare

motivering: The committee's proposal rejects SD's motions (items 1-5) on safe residential areas. The manifesto categorically states that S will never help give power to the Sweden Democrats. S also has its own housing agenda – rental housing, combating segregation and overcrowding – which differs fundamentally from SD's approach. Voting Yes is consistent with this position.

citations.quote: The Social Democrats will never help give power to the Sweden Democrats, a party that does not stand up for the equal value and rights of all people.
Get to the bottom of the causes of housing segregation.

motivering: The manifesto lacks a position on the repatriation of remains and museum objects. The items belong to C and MP, and the committee refers to ongoing work. S's cultural policy line focuses on a living cultural life and cohesion but does not specifically address the repatriation issue.

citations.quote: Sweden shall have a living, free and independent cultural life that both strengthens cohesion and challenges.

motivering: S's environmental profile supports stronger protection against substances hazardous to health and the environment. Reservation 12 involves tightened PFAS legislation, which S supports in principle since PFAS harms public health and biodiversity. However, the manifesto lacks specific PFAS text and the reservation's author (party) is unknown, which gives low confidence.

citations.quote: the defining issue of our time. We risk destroying our only planet and the conditions for living and residing in many places, which will lead to enormous migration pressure. At the same time species extinction is accelerating and biodiversity is under threat.
We shall work to introduce a global carbon price based on the principle that the polluter pays

motivering: S has its own motion (item 1, Fredrik Lundh Sammeli et al. (S)) on healthcare preparedness which the committee rejects. The manifesto explicitly demands increased resources for healthcare emergency stockpiles and that private healthcare providers contribute in crisis and war. S supports Reservation 4 and votes No.

citations.quote: The work of strengthening civil defense and crisis preparedness must continue, including through increased resources to equip and build emergency stockpiles for healthcare
Private healthcare providers shall be obliged to contribute staff and care places in the event of crisis or war.

omvarld.effekt: Demonstrates a real threat to the civilian healthcare system that reinforces the manifesto's demand

motivering: The motions seek to lower various environmental taxes (fuel, chemicals, aviation, etc.), mainly from C and SD. The party states that 'the climate policy framework shall remain in place' and warns that tax cuts to offset price increases risk fueling inflation, which speaks in favor of supporting the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: The climate policy framework shall remain in place.
But putting Sweden into debt to compensate for every single price increase would fuel inflation and, in the long run, jeopardize public finances, welfare and pensions.

motivering: Among the rejected motions are the party's own members (Lundh Sammeli and Westlund), which shows that S itself has driven the proposals on mental health. The manifesto's promise of increased welfare resources speaks in favor of S wanting to see the proposals implemented, and therefore supporting the reservation.

citations.quote: Increase resources for welfare throughout the country.

motivering: S's manifesto demands that EU trade agreements include requirements on social dialogue, human rights and the environment. A motion on revised sustainability requirements in trade agreements is directly in line with this principle. Supporting the committee's rejection would conflict with the party's explicit commitment to pursuing sustainability values in EU trade policy.

citations.quote: The EU needs to conclude more trade agreements where our values on social dialogue, human rights and the environment are also guiding.
We stand up for open, free and fair trade.

motivering: S has its own motion in the committee report (Jim Svensk Larm et al. (S)) on income taxation which the committee majority rejects. The reservation (Alternative A) represents S's tax policy line. The manifesto states that large tax cuts make increased welfare resources impossible, and S votes No to assert its own budget policy position against the center-right majority.

citations.quote: Large tax cuts make that impossible
If parties were to outbid each other with borrowed money, it would end with higher mortgage rates and even higher prices

motivering: S's own motions (items 1, 10, 12, 23 and 29) are rejected by the committee, meaning the party's trade policy positions are not reflected in the committee's proposal. The manifesto has clear commitments to free trade, fair trade conditions and strengthened WTO cooperation. Reservation 1 marks S's own positions, and the party should vote No.

citations.quote: We stand up for open, free and fair trade. For a small, export-dependent country like Sweden, global trade is absolutely crucial, not least for keeping prices down and countering inflation.
Global cooperation within the WTO shall be strengthened, as shall cooperation with like-minded countries.

motivering: The manifesto commits S to a powerful defense buildup up to 2 percent of GDP. The committee's rejection of the motions protects the ongoing rearmament program from ad hoc changes. S supports the committee's line since V's and MP's motions on organizational changes risk disrupting the planned rearmament.

citations.quote: Powerfully strengthen Sweden's military capability. Appropriations for the military defense shall increase to the equivalent of two percent of GDP.
Sweden needs to build a strong people's defense

motivering: The manifesto commits S to doubling climate aid and support for the UN's role in international cooperation. The motions from V and MP on multilateral aid are in line with S's development aid policy ambitions. S, in opposition, supports Reservation 4 and signals that the center-right majority's reference to ongoing work is insufficient.

citations.quote: we double the climate aid.
We will continue to safeguard the UN's role in the work for international law and international cooperation

motivering: The manifesto does not specifically address mineral availability and geological mapping. S has no motion of its own in this vote. The committee rejects the motions from the Sweden Democrats (SD) and the Left Party (V), and S has nothing in its documents that justifies supporting these motions. S votes Yes with the committee.

citations.quote: The climate transition is the defining issue of our time.

motivering: The motion on defector support activities (avhopparverksamhet) was written by S's own member Ardalan Shekarabi and is in line with the party's goal of stopping recruitment into crime through social interventions. S should therefore vote against the committee's rejection and support the reservation.

citations.quote: No young person should become a criminal. Recruitment must be stopped.

motivering: The manifesto lacks specific guidelines on wildlife management or hunting. However, S has submitted its own motion in the committee report (Anna-Caren Sätherberg et al., S, item 12) on strengthened local influence in wildlife management, which is rejected by the committee. S's own motion implies that the party supports Reservation 3 and votes No.

citations.quote: We want to continue the major investments so that municipalities can adapt to climate change locally.
citations.princip: municipal local responsibility in environmental matters

motivering: S has no motions of its own on the organization of the Swedish Better Regulation Council (Regelrådet). The committee rejects motions from SD and the Centre Party (C). The manifesto does not take a position on the specific organizational form of the Regulatory Council. Without an alternative of its own, S supports the committee's procedurally grounded rejection and votes Yes.

citations.quote: Strengthen the long-term conditions for entrepreneurship and innovation

motivering: S supports Nato accession but has a clear position on nuclear weapons: condemning nuclear threats and working for a world free of nuclear weapons. The party's own item 6 (Morgan Johansson et al.) is rejected, and Reservation 3 likely originates from V/MP with broader anti-Nato conditions that S cannot support. No alternative reflects S's overall position: yes to Nato, no to nuclear weapons on Swedish soil.

citations.quote: We condemn all threats of the use of nuclear weapons and continue to work toward the only reasonable ultimate goal: a world free of nuclear weapons.
citations.princip: a nuclear-weapon-free world as a political goal

citations.quote: Sweden shall join Nato. Swedish membership in Nato is the best path for our country's security, and Sweden has therefore submitted its application for membership.
citations.princip: Nato accession as a foundation for security policy

motivering: S has no motions of its own on copyright for artworks in public places. The vote concerns the rejection of items from SD and C. The manifesto's cultural policy ambitions give no support for their specific reservation position. S supports the committee's rejection and votes Yes.

citations.quote: Sweden shall have a living, free and independent cultural life that both strengthens togetherness and challenges

motivering: S's manifesto supports a global carbon price based on the polluter-pays principle, but not a specific emissions trading system for the Baltic Sea. The item belongs to C, and the committee refers to ongoing work. Without a proposal of its own for a regional Baltic Sea system, S should support the committee's line.

citations.quote: We shall work to introduce a global carbon price based on the principle that the polluter pays.
Sweden shall be a strong force in the UN and the EU so that the world's countries increase their commitments to realize the ambitions of the Paris Agreement.

motivering: The election manifesto does not mention a special victims' ombudsman, only increased resources for victim support in general. Since the committee refers to already announced reforms and the institution is absent from the manifesto, S follows the committee's rejection of the Left Party's motion.

citations.quote: increased resources for the important work of women's and girls' shelters

motivering: Simplification of regulations within agricultural policy is not specifically mentioned in S's election manifesto. No S motions are present, and the content and author of Reservation 12 are unclear. Without a clear basis in the manifesto, supporting the committee's proposal is the most defensible option.

citations.quote: Strengthen the long-term conditions for entrepreneurship and innovation.

motivering: The motions, mainly from C, seek to lower the tax on fuel. The party's line instead is to increase domestic production of renewable fuels, and it states that no responsible politician can promise full compensation for every price increase. This supports backing the committee's rejection of the tax-cut demands.

citations.quote: We want to increase Swedish production of renewable fuels, so that it becomes easier to fuel up fossil-free in Sweden.
But no responsible politician can promise full compensation for every price increase.

motivering: S's manifesto demands vigorous action against work-life crime and states that public procurers should set an example for sound competition. The Left Party's (V) motion on the number of subcontractors and fair terms in public procurement directly coincides with these commitments. Supporting the committee's rejection would conflict with the party's stated demands for fair terms throughout procurement chains.

citations.quote: Vigorous action against work-life crime. Work-life crime shall have no place in the Swedish labour market, and public employers and procurers shall set an example in working for sound competition.
It should never pay to commit crimes or gain competitive advantages by neglecting employees' right to a safe working environment.
citations.princip: safe working environment as a requirement

motivering: Among the rejected motions is one by S's own member Ingela Nylund Watz on the same issue, which shows that the party has wanted to see vigorous action against illegal trading in tenancy contracts. This is consistent with the manifesto's aim to stop criminal economic activity, so S should support the reservation.

citations.quote: Tax fraud, welfare crime and money laundering shall be stopped.

motivering: The election manifesto does not address the organizational structure of public health work, and the motions come from the Green Party with no connection to the Social Democrats' own proposals. The committee refers to ongoing work, and without a clear line of its own in the documents, the Social Democrats follow the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Increase resources for welfare throughout the country.

motivering: The manifesto demands an uncompromising fight against crime and that police be given more tools, including better capabilities for wiretapping and search of premises — precisely the procedural-law issues this matter concerns. The Social Democrats have submitted their own motion (Ardalan Shekarabi et al., S, claim 16) on strengthening the judicial system, which is rejected. The Social Democrats support Reservation 18 and vote No.

citations.quote: The police also need more tools, such as better capabilities for wiretapping and search of premises.
The fight against crime must be uncompromising.

motivering: PFAS in drinking water is not mentioned in the manifesto. The Social Democrats' closest principle is that environmental threats to life and health must be taken seriously. Given that the committee majority rejects demands for tightening the rules with reference to ongoing work, the Social Democrats, who are in opposition, support the reservation calling for more concrete threshold-value measures.

citations.quote: climate emissions that threaten life and health

motivering: The manifesto commits the Social Democrats to Sweden being a strong global voice and to EU cooperation being the foundation for solving global problems. The motion on expanding international chemicals work aligns with the principle of active international engagement. The Social Democrats support the reservation and reject the center-right majority's line of rejection.

citations.quote: Sweden shall be a strong global voice
We are convinced that EU cooperation is the foundation for solving many of the most difficult problems of our time

motivering: The Social Democrats' own motion on the direction of the food strategy (Anna-Caren Sätherberg et al., claims 3 and 4) is rejected by the committee. The manifesto's focus on climate-resilient food production — including the risk that drought will destroy harvests — supports an active food strategy. The Social Democrats support their reservation and vote no to the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Strengthen preparedness against extreme weather. Otherwise cloudbursts risk flooding cities, drought risks destroying entire harvests, and wildfires risk spreading.

motivering: The rehabilitation chain (rehabiliteringskedjan) is addressed by the party's own motion (Johanna Haraldsson et al.), together with motions from the Centre Party, the Sweden Democrats, and the Left Party, all of which call for changes. The manifesto upholds the principle that those who are too ill to work should be able to rely on the health insurance system, which argues for supporting the reservation against the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: we uphold the principle that those who are too ill to work should be able to rely on the health insurance system.
