citations.quote: It was a mistake to take away part of the wildlife management mandate from the hunters' organizations. It should go back to the organizations responsible for hunting and not be shared with those who oppose hunting in all its forms.
citations.princip: return the wildlife management mandate to the hunters' organizations

citations.quote: Give the wildlife management mandate back to the hunters' organizations

motivering: SD's own motion (Tobias Andersson et al., item 2) on deductions for pension and home savings is rejected by the committee. SD has explicitly committed to facilitating private pension saving, and the Tidöavtalet (the Tidö agreement) prescribes lower tax on savings. Reservation 24 reflects SD's line, which is why the party votes No.

citations.quote: Facilitate private pension saving
Lower tax on savings by making a base level of SEK 300,000 in an ISK (investment savings account) tax-free.

motivering: The matter concerns the permit requirement for municipalities regarding, among other things, camera surveillance. The Tidöavtalet (the Tidö agreement) establishes that municipalities' right to carry out camera surveillance without a permit should be expanded — the government is already working to reduce the permit requirement. The committee rejects the opposition from the Social Democrats (S) (Ardalan Shekarabi), citing ongoing work; the Sweden Democrats (SD) support this.

citations.quote: The Camera Surveillance Act is being reviewed to enable camera surveillance more often and in more places. Among other things, municipalities' right to carry out camera surveillance without having to apply for a permit should be expanded.
citations.princip: expanded camera surveillance without a permit

citations.quote: Cooperation between authorities within the justice system and tools for detecting and prosecuting criminals shall be improved.

motivering: Among the rejected motions is SD's own motion item 10 (Linda Lindberg et al.) on health-preventive work in elderly care. SD's election manifesto emphasizes investments in the mental health of the elderly and a new Elderly Care Act. Reservation 39 is likely SD's own reservation, and the party votes No in order to pursue its elderly care policy.

citations.quote: Invest in raising the level of knowledge and the priority given to mental ill-health among the elderly
A new Elderly Care Act must strengthen the legal basis for good living conditions, since the current term 'reasonable living conditions' is not sufficient.

motivering: The committee proposes rejecting the Left Party's (V) motion on a so-called 'class grant' (klasspeng). citations.quote: Free school choice must be safeguarded in order to give parents and pupils freedom of choice.
Restore a knowledge-focused school through proven pedagogy and a focus on traditional learning with equal conditions in all schools

SD wants to simplify building regulations but, as a supporting party, follows the government's ongoing reform work and supports the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: The Sweden Democrats want to facilitate housing construction by simplifying and speeding up decision-making processes and reviewing the extensive regulations and requirements that govern housing construction.

citations.quote: That farmland is actively used and that overgrowth is counteracted
Increase national funding in agriculture, for environmental benefit and productivity gains

Work for a secure and legally certain sickness insurance system

motivering: The committee rejects a large number of SD motions on foreign aid from Christiansson, Nordberg, Wiechel and Emilsson. citations.princip: accessible health care throughout the country

motivering: SD's own motions by Leonid Yurkovskiy et al. (SD), item 1, and Mikael Eskilandersson et al. (SD), items 1-3, on citizen influence in physical planning are explicitly rejected. SD wants classical architecture and increased citizen influence in the design of public environments. Reservation 11 is SD's position; SD votes No.

citations.quote: The Sweden Democrats want to work for pleasant and safe areas with classical architecture. Aesthetics and design are important factors for how an environment is experienced and for safety.
Allocate public cultural funds and design public environments with greater citizen influence

motivering: The committee rejects SD's own motions (Eskilandersson et al., items 1-5) on safe residential areas. The party's election manifesto demands increased housing construction, simplified processes, and that migration's strain on the housing market be reduced. Since SD's own demands are rejected, the party supports Reservation 18 against the committee majority's decision.

citations.quote: The Sweden Democrats want to facilitate housing construction by simplifying and speeding up decision-making processes and reviewing the extensive regulations and requirements that govern housing construction.
Reduce migration's strain on the housing market through return migration (återvandring)

motivering: SD's environmental policy strives for environmental efficiency without harming industry and opposes symbolic policy measures. The committee finds that Sweden already conducts consistent chemicals work, which aligns with SD's line on fact- and evidence-based measures. The Centre Party's demand for specific PFAS bans is satisfied by ongoing work. SD supports the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: Strive for environmental efficiency and find the measures that give the most environmental benefit per krona
Symbolic policy measures that risk hampering the conditions for industry shall be abolished

motivering: The committee endorses the government's bill on health care's supply preparedness — requirements for contingency stockpiling of medicines and health care products. SD's election manifesto demands an increased medical contingency stockpile and increased self-sufficiency in critical products. The Left Party's and Social Democrats' motions (Reservation 4) diverge and are correctly rejected.

citations.quote: Sweden's self-sufficiency in energy, food and medical materiel needs to increase and be able to be rapidly scaled up in the event of prolonged disruptions.
The Sweden Democrats also want to re-establish contingency stockpiles to cover critical needs that may arise based on various scenarios.

motivering: The matter includes SD's own motions (Martin Kinnunen and Per Söderlund) on other environmental taxes, which shows that the party wants to go further than the committee's rejection. The election manifesto states that environmental taxes today far exceed the cost of the emissions and calls for more cost-effective climate measures. SD should vote No and support its own reservation.

citations.quote: It is reasonable that petrol and diesel are taxed, but today environmental taxes far exceed the cost of the emissions.
Reduce the costs of migration policy, aid, EU contributions and climate measures that can be made more efficient

motivering: SD's own motion (Linda Lindberg) is among the rejected motions. The party program specifically calls for a national strategy, a research program, and a national coordinator for suicide prevention, not merely an inquiry due by September 2023. SD votes No and supports the reservation for faster implementation.

citations.quote: a national strategy for mental health and suicide prevention shall be developed.
Appoint a national coordinator responsible for suicide prevention
Develop a national strategy for the continued work on mental health

motivering: The Green Party's (MP) motion (item 22) calls for revised and tightened sustainability requirements in trade agreements. SD considers that free trade benefits society and that Swedish trade interests should be safeguarded rather than constrained by new requirement levels. Stricter sustainability requirements in agreements risk harming Swedish competitiveness, which conflicts with the party's direction. Yes supports the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: free trade between European countries is of great value to our economy
Safeguard Swedish interests in free trade agreements

motivering: The Tidö agreement (Tidöavtalet) obliges the cooperation parties to vote for the government's budget in its entirety. The Committee on Taxation endorses the government's tax policy and rejects the opposition's motions (S and C) on the earned-income tax credit (jobbskatteavdrag), household/renovation service tax deductions (rut/rot-avdrag), and green tax shifting. Through the Tidö agreement, SD has committed to budget loyalty and supports the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: The cooperation parties undertake to vote for the government's budget so that the budget in its entirety is passed through the Riksdag.
Make it profitable to work and contribute to society
citations.princip: the work-first line in tax policy

motivering: The committee wants to reject SD's own motions (Tobias Andersson et al., items 2 and 6) on international trade. Reservation 1 represents the party's position. SD views international trade as fundamental to prosperity and prioritizes Swedish industry and competitiveness. No supports the party's own motions.

citations.quote: The Sweden Democrats see that a market economy, freedom of choice within welfare, and international trade benefit society and are important to defend
improve the opportunity for global trade and Swedish exports, which are fundamental to Swedish prosperity

motivering: SD submitted no motions of its own on this matter and is a cooperation party to the government. The committee rejects the opposition's motions (MP, V, C) on the organization of the Armed Forces and expanded police assistance, on the grounds that the issues require more thorough investigation. SD does indeed want the Armed Forces to be able to support the police in peacetime, but the inquiry route is consistent with the coalition's working order, and SD has not submitted any motions of its own.

citations.quote: The Armed Forces shall be equipped for war. But the Armed Forces also need to be adapted so that they can, to a greater extent, be used to support and assist in the police mission in peacetime, in a situation where the domestic security situation requires more resources than the police have at their disposal.
citations.princip: Armed Forces support to the police

citations.quote: The Sweden Democrats want to ensure long-term funding of the Armed Forces of at least two percent of GDP within a ten-year period.

motivering: SD wants to sharply reduce multilateral aid and focus it on direct humanitarian efforts. The Left Party's (V) and Green Party's (MP) motions on prioritizing multilateral aid via UN agencies conflict directly with SD's aid policy direction. The committee's rejection is in line with SD's position, and SD supports the proposal.

citations.quote: Focus aid on humanitarian disaster relief
Reduce Swedish aid in favor of Swedish welfare and security

motivering: SD's own motion (Tobias Andersson, item 8) on the accessibility and mapping of mineral resources is rejected by the committee; Reservation 16 represents the party's position. The election platform clearly emphasizes that it should become easier to open mines and that the mineral value in rural areas should be utilized. SD should vote No and support its reservation.

citations.quote: It also needs to become easier and faster to open mines for the minerals needed for, for example, battery manufacturing.
The value of minerals in the ground, of forests, and the potential for recreation and tourism is enormous in rural areas.

motivering: The Tidö agreement mentions defector support activities (avhopparverksamhet) only in connection with tougher penalties for attacks on such premises, without any promise of new investment in the activity itself. The motion is the Social Democrats' own and has no counterpart in SD's own commitments. SD votes Yes to the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: and defector support activities shall be associated with a higher penalty value when the activity is impeded
Break the attractiveness of a criminal lifestyle
citations.princip: break the attractiveness of a criminal lifestyle

motivering: SD's election manifesto explicitly demands that the wildlife management mandate be returned to hunters' organizations and that EU influence be reduced. The committee's rejection of motions on strengthened local influence in wildlife management conflicts with this clear principle. The party votes No to uphold its position on local self-determination.

citations.quote: Give back the wildlife management mandate to hunters' organizations
The Sweden Democrats want to reduce the EU's influence over Swedish hunting and wildlife management.
Greater local influence should prevail over predator policy.

motivering: SD's own motion item 1 (Tobias Andersson et al.) on the organization of the Swedish Better Regulation Council (Regelrådet) is rejected by the committee. The election platform's demand for regulatory simplification and reduced regulatory burden supports a strengthened Regelrådet organization for independent regulatory review. SD supports its reservation (No. 16, Alternative A) against the committee's rejection decision.

citations.quote: Work for regulatory simplification and relieve the administrative burden on small businesses
Bureaucracy, regulatory burden, taxes, and administrative costs risk diverting focus from the core business and blunting an entrepreneur's drive.

motivering: SD fully supports NATO membership and wants to give Sweden the capability to meet potential aggressors. The opposition's motions seek to restrict Sweden through bans on nuclear weapons and foreign troops on Swedish soil. SD rejects such restrictions on the alliance commitments; Russia's aggression and the ICC arrest warrant against Putin underscore the need not to weaken NATO's deterrence.

citations.quote: The Sweden Democrats want to restore total defense (totalförsvaret) and for Sweden to have the capability to meet potential aggressors.
Prepare Sweden for a new security policy situation in our neighboring region

omvarld.faktor: ICC arrest warrant against Putin, ongoing Russian invasion of Ukraine
omvarld.effekt: Reinforces the need for full NATO commitment including nuclear deterrence; unwarranted to restrict the alliance's freedom of action

motivering: SD has two motions of its own (item 6 by Tobias Andersson et al. and item 16 by Michael Rubbestad et al.) on copyright-protected artworks in public places, which the committee proposes to reject. The election platform's demand to modernize copyright law underlies the reservation (No. 1, Alternative A) against the rejection decision.

citations.quote: Outdated copyright rules also need to be adapted to how people consume and create content in the digital society.
The Sweden Democrats want to prevent EU dictates that threaten to determine what content may be provided through digital services and how material may be distributed on the Internet.
citations.princip: safeguard digital content freedom against EU intervention

motivering: The SD wants to strengthen the position of crime victims through its own concrete measures such as damages, restraining orders, and targeted information efforts, not through a new ombudsman function as proposed by the Left Party. The SD therefore votes Yes to the committee's rejection of the motion.

citations.quote: Strengthen the position of crime victims and increase support for crime victims
Increased efforts should be made so that crime victims and potential crime victims have full knowledge
citations.princip: own targeted efforts for crime victims

motivering: The SD's own motions on regulatory simplification within agricultural policy (by Martin Kinnunen et al., items 47, 48, 51 and 52) are included in the committee's rejection proposal. The party demands that EU rules become fewer and more flexible, and that the regulations be simplified for agriculture and forestry. The SD has evidently filed Reservation 12 based on its own motions and votes No to support it.

citations.quote: Simplify the regulations and improve legal certainty
EU rules must become fewer and more flexible based on each member state's unique landscape, tradition and standards.
Work for regulatory simplification and relieve small businesses' administrative burden

motivering: The election manifesto is unambiguous: the SD wants to lower the price of petrol and diesel through a reduced fuel tax and a reduced reduction obligation, as well as lower fuel taxes generally. The motions on fuel taxation are in line with this goal, even though the SD has not filed a reservation in this particular matter. The party should therefore vote No and support the reservation against the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Lower the price of petrol and diesel through a reduced fuel tax and a reduced reduction obligation.
citations.princip: reduced fuel tax and reduction obligation

citations.quote: Lower the tax on fuel

motivering: The Left Party's motions (items 19-23) on limiting subcontractors and fair conditions in public procurement are rejected by the committee. The SD advocates regulatory simplification and a reduction of the administrative burden on businesses. The Left Party's proposal entails increased regulation and more requirements, which conflicts with the SD's business-policy orientation. Yes supports the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Work for regulatory simplification and relieve small businesses' administrative burden
Make it easier to hire and create the best conditions for Swedish industry

motivering: The SD's own motion (Mikael Eskilandersson) on illegal trading in tenancy agreements is among the rejected motions, in line with the party's goal of fair access to first-hand rental housing and zero tolerance for crime. The SD votes No and supports its reservation against the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Improve opportunities for young people to obtain their first home
citations.princip: fair access to first-hand rental housing

citations.quote: Introduce zero tolerance for crime so that even less serious crimes are investigated and prosecuted

motivering: The government is already pursuing its own approach to organizing public health work, including through strengthened national governance of the Public Health Agency and its own strategy for mental health. This argues for rejecting the opposition's motions on alternative organization, in line with the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: The Sweden Democrats therefore advocate clear, driving national governance in which the Public Health Agency's role is strengthened and clarified.
citations.princip: strengthened national governance of public health

citations.quote: The Sweden Democrats want to concentrate public spending on the heart of the welfare system and demand clear citizen benefit for all initiatives.

motivering: The Tido agreement contains explicit commitments to review the Camera Surveillance Act and anonymous witnesses - exactly the procedural law issues the motions (Centre Party, Social Democrats) concern. The committee's reference to ongoing work confirms that the reforms are being prepared within the framework of the Tido agreement. The SD supports the committee's rejection of the opposition's alternative demands.

citations.quote: The Camera Surveillance Act is being reviewed to enable camera surveillance more often and in more places.
citations.princip: camera surveillance within the Tido agreement

citations.quote: A system of anonymous witnesses shall be introduced.
citations.princip: anonymous witnesses within the Tido agreement

motivering: The SD's environmental policy is based on evidence and cost-effectiveness, not on unilateral national special requirements beyond EU processes. The committee notes that Sweden is already working on PFAS limit values in drinking water as part of ongoing work. The Centre Party's motion is thereby satisfied. The SD supports the committee's proposal and does not want to create symbolic-policy regulation.

citations.quote: Environmental policy must always be checked against new research findings and be based on facts rather than feelings
Strive for environmental efficiency and find the measures that give the most environmental benefit per krona

motivering: The SD safeguards national self-determination and is skeptical of expanding international commitments beyond what EU law requires. The committee notes that ongoing work already covers the Centre Party's demand for expanded international chemicals work, which is consistent with the SD's position. Unnecessarily expanding international obligations conflicts with the SD's EU-policy principles.

citations.quote: Restore intergovernmentalism and strengthen voters' opportunities for influence
Symbolic-policy measures that risk hampering the conditions for industry shall be abolished

motivering: The SD prioritizes strengthened food production and self-sufficiency, but no SD motions are included in the current rejection proposal. The committee majority, with the SD as a supporting party, rejects the motions of the Centre Party and the Social Democrats on the direction of the food strategy, citing ongoing work. The Tido agreement addresses these issues through the animal welfare inquiry on strengthened competitiveness. The SD votes Yes with the committee majority.

citations.quote: Increase the competitiveness of Swedish agriculture and Sweden's self-sufficiency in food
strengthen the competitiveness of Swedish food production while also improving global animal welfare

motivering: The matter includes the SD's own motion (Clara Aranda et al.) on the rehabilitation chain, which shows that the party wants to go further than the committee's rejection. The election manifesto itself points to the Swedish National Audit Office's criticism of shortcomings in the rehabilitation chain and calls for more resources for preventive work and rehabilitation. The SD should vote No and support its own reservation.

citations.quote: At the same time, the Swedish National Audit Office points to serious shortcomings in the rehabilitation chain linked to mental ill health.
See increased focus and more resources on preventive work and rehabilitation

motivering: The motions on strengthened protection for journalists (Green Party, Centre Party, Social Democrats) are rejected with reference to ongoing work. The SD safeguards media freedom and protection for journalists, but the party has, through the Tido agreement, committed to implementing this within the framework of its cooperation with the government. Supporting the opposition's reservations would mean departing from the joint reform work guaranteed by the Tido agreement. Yes supports the ongoing work.

citations.quote: The freedom of the media shall be safeguarded, and the diversity of different media shall be promoted.
citations.princip: media freedom via the cooperation agreement

citations.quote: Every journalist's, artist's and citizen's right to express themselves freely without being subjected to threats or reprisals shall be safeguarded and strengthened.

motivering: The party wants to safeguard freedom of choice within welfare services and sees the market economy as something to defend, which argues against the Social Democrats' motions demanding restrictions on profits in welfare. The government has also already announced a review of the equalization system, which supports the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: The Sweden Democrats consider that the market economy, freedom of choice within welfare, and international trade benefit society and are important to defend
citations.princip: defends freedom of choice in welfare

citations.quote: Investigate the municipal equalization system, including measures to address

motivering: SD has no motions of its own in this vote on goals for simplification policy. Reservation 1 likely belongs to individual Moderate or Social Democrat motioners whose claims the government's committee majority dismissed as superfluous — regulatory simplification is handled within the Tidö agreement's Growth project. SD supports the committee's rejection decision and awaits the agreed reform agenda.

citations.quote: The cooperation also means that the participating parties do not unilaterally cooperate with other parties in the Riksdag on the issues covered by the directives for the cooperation projects.
Lower administrative costs for businesses.
citations.princip: regulatory simplification in the Tidö agenda

motivering: The Elderly Care Boost (Äldreomsorgslyftet) is a Social Democratic program that the Social Democrats want to extend. The Tidö agreement and SD's election manifesto instead prioritize language requirements for elderly care staff as SD's central competence measure. Extending an S program that does not match the coalition's elderly care policy line is incompatible with SD's positions; SD votes Yes with the committee.

citations.quote: The Ministry of Health and Social Affairs is instructed to investigate and produce proposals on how a language requirement for elderly care staff could be implemented
citations.princip: language requirement for elderly care staff

citations.quote: Introduce language requirements for staff in home care and elderly care.
citations.princip: language requirement for home care and elderly care

motivering: SD's own motions (Nordberg et al., claims 4–7) on the level of foreign aid are rejected by the committee. The party's election manifesto demands sharply reduced aid and greater efficiency. Reservation 1 is likely SD's own reservation, in line with the party's aid policy position of reducing aid in favor of Swedish welfare.

citations.quote: Reduce Swedish foreign aid in favor of Swedish welfare and security
Overall, international aid must be sharply reduced and efforts made more efficient.
Make parts of aid conditional on the recipient country taking responsibility for its own citizens

motivering: The party wants to see a clear action plan and vigorous measures against intimate partner violence, which aligns well with the committee's formal request (tillkännagivande) for a zero-vision. The other rejected motions concern areas where other work is already underway.

citations.quote: The Sweden Democrats want to see, among other things, a clear action plan for those subjected to intimate partner violence.
citations.princip: action plan against intimate partner violence

citations.quote: Vigorous measures need to be taken both in preventive work and by the judicial system.
citations.princip: vigorous measures by the judicial system

motivering: No SD motions of its own on cybersecurity were explicitly rejected; the rejected motions are from the Centre Party and the Green Party. SD's election manifesto supports strengthened crisis preparedness in general, and the government is conducting ongoing work in this area. The party supports the committee's assessment rather than the opposition's alternative demands.

citations.quote: The Sweden Democrats want to strengthen society's preparedness for all types of crises that may arise.
Develop special crisis legislation

motivering: Reindeer husbandry and Sami rights are not addressed in SD's election platform or the Tidö agreement. The committee rejects a motion from the Social Democrats on reindeer husbandry, citing ongoing work; Reservation 45 is likely the Social Democrats' own claim. In the absence of a specific party position, SD supports the committee majority as a support party and votes Yes.

citations.quote: Swedish agriculture and forestry shall be safeguarded and contribute to Swedish competitiveness, good environmental standards, open landscapes, and Swedish self-sufficiency and exports.

motivering: SD's documents do not take a specific position on individual VAT (value-added tax) exemptions. The party's general tax line emphasizes competitive taxes without special solutions and that public funds should be directed toward core activities. Without a claim of its own and with reference to ongoing investigative work, the party should vote Yes and support the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Tax policy must therefore aim for competitive taxes that do not deviate too much from the rest of the world, especially the taxes imposed on businesses.
Review public spending and redirect funds to welfare and the judicial system

motivering: The Tidö agreement commits to lowering administrative costs for businesses within the Growth and Household Economy cooperation project. The committee rejects the motions, citing that the government is already conducting this work. As a cooperation party, SD accepts the committee's decision and relies on the Tidö agreement's preparatory process rather than pursuing its own separate motions.

citations.quote: Lower administrative costs for businesses.
Work for regulatory simplification and relieve small businesses' administrative burden

motivering: The Tidö agreement already establishes that the rules for criminal injuries compensation shall be reviewed to reduce the crime victim's own responsibility for recovering damages, which is exactly what the Centre Party motion calls for. Since the government is already in the process of implementing this, the party supports the committee's rejection of the motion.

citations.quote: The rules for criminal injuries compensation are reviewed with the aim of reducing the crime victim's responsibility to
citations.princip: reduced debt-collection responsibility for crime victims

citations.quote: Raise the damages

motivering: The committee approves the government's legislation on healthcare supply preparedness and rejects the Social Democrats' reservation. citations.quote: The patient's best interest shall be at the center of the reform work.
Increase Sweden's degree of self-sufficiency in critical products and goods

motivering: SD's election manifesto demands that permit processes for the mining industry be made more efficient and that authorities take on a supportive rather than obstructive role toward business. The committee's formal request (tillkännagivande) that authorities should work in a more advisory and solution-oriented way in permit processes matches this position directly. The Tidö agreement confirms this direction by advocating simplified and shortened environmental permit processes. SD should support the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: Permit processes for the mining industry, electricity grid expansion, and industry need to be made more efficient and faster.
Authorities must not become enemies of businesses who put a spoke in the wheel, but must instead take on a more supportive function.
Environmental permit processes are simplified and shortened
It also needs to become easier and faster to open mines for the minerals needed for, for example, battery manufacturing.

motivering: SD's own motion (Richard Jomshof et al., claim 1) on penalties is rejected by the committee. SD pursues a consistent line on drastically tougher penalties and abolishing the volume discount (mängdrabatt, reduced sentencing for multiple offenses), reinforced by the Tidö agreement's (Tidöavtalet) criminal justice reform. Voting against its own reservation (no. 35) would be inconsistent. SD supports the reservation and votes against the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: Drastically increase penalties and abolish the volume discount (mängdrabatt) for serious crimes against a person
citations.princip: tougher penalties and abolished volume discount

citations.quote: The sentencing ranges, penalties and the system for determining sentences shall be reviewed. Penalties for violent crimes, sexual offenses (where life imprisonment should be considered for the most serious crimes), attacks on police officers, and other crimes that threaten the foundations of the rule of law and society shall be tightened further in relation to other types of crime.
citations.princip: tougher sentencing ranges in the Tidö agreement

motivering: The documents do not specifically address vaccination programs for the elderly. The closest applicable principle is the party's general demand for high quality and accessibility in healthcare, which provides some support for following the committee's rejection of the motions rather than pursuing specific demands.

citations.quote: Swedish healthcare must always have a very high medical quality with well-developed accessibility throughout Sweden.

motivering: The committee rejects the Left Party's (V) motion on protective equipment for healthcare staff. SD supports the state's stockpiling of critical healthcare products but rejects V's alternative list of demands, which goes beyond the government's framework. SD votes yes in accordance with the Tidö agreement's (Tidöavtalet) healthcare reforms and against V's line.

citations.quote: The best interest of the patient shall be at the center of the reform work.
Increase Sweden's degree of self-sufficiency in critical products and goods

motivering: SD strongly emphasizes food self-sufficiency and crisis preparedness. The committee majority (with SD's support) rejects the Centre Party's (C) motion on supply security in the strategic plan, citing ongoing work under the Tidö agreement (Tidöavtalet). The Animal Welfare Inquiry under the Tidö agreement already addresses the balance between EU agricultural policy and the competitive conditions of Swedish food producers. SD votes Yes with the committee majority.

citations.quote: Sweden's self-sufficiency in energy, food and medical materiel needs to increase and be able to be rapidly scaled up in the event of prolonged disruptions.
balance the competitive conditions for Swedish food producers while maintaining Sweden's high animal husbandry requirements

motivering: No SD motions on the rescue services are explicitly rejected; the identified rejected motions are from the Centre Party (C) and the Green Party (MP). The committee refers to ongoing work on crisis preparedness, which SD supports in a broad sense. The party votes Yes with the committee and does not support the opposition's specific claims on the development of the rescue services.

citations.quote: The Sweden Democrats want to strengthen society's preparedness for all types of crises that may arise.
Appropriations to the agencies with overall responsibility for civil defense, crisis management and preparedness should increase

motivering: SD wants aid to focus on basic humanitarian needs and direct disaster relief, not on normative agendas such as SRHR (sexual and reproductive health and rights) and gender equality indicators via multilateral organizations. The Left Party's (V) claims about prioritizing precisely these issues in multilateral aid conflict with SD's view on aid. The committee's rejection is correct.

citations.quote: aid is focused around direct efforts to meet basic needs and efforts in disasters and war, and otherwise to improve the life situation of vulnerable children and women under strain in poor or oppressed parts of the world
citations.princip: humanitarian aid, not a normative agenda

citations.quote: Reduce Swedish aid in favor of Swedish welfare and security

motivering: The Tidö agreement (Tidöavtalet) already contains concrete measures against men's violence against women and violence in close relationships, including restraining orders (vistelseförbud), while the party's program calls for firm action by the judicial system on the issue. Since the work is already underway through the government's initiative, the committee's rejection of further motions on raising awareness is supported.

citations.quote: men's violence against women and other forms of violence in close relationships.
citations.princip: measures against violence in close relationships

citations.quote: Firm action needs to be taken both in preventive work and by the judicial system.
citations.princip: firm action by the judicial system

motivering: SD's specific policy on housing for the elderly focuses on needs-assessed sheltered housing (biståndsbedömt trygghetsboende), not on the solutions pursued by C and MP in their claims (Reservation 24). citations.princip: concentrate funds on the core of welfare

motivering: The Tidö agreement (Tidöavtalet) prescribes a thorough review of aggravating circumstances in the Penal Code, which covers the issues addressed by the motions from C and S. The committee's reference to ongoing preparatory work is correct — the reform work is taking place within the cooperation project on crime. SD accepts this arrangement and supports the committee's proposal rather than the opposition's reservations.

citations.quote: The mitigating grounds (billighetsskälen) as well as the aggravating and mitigating circumstances in the Penal Code are reviewed
aggravating 24 circumstances, such as crimes against the elderly and against children, affect the sentencing value to a greater extent than

motivering: SD's environmental policy emphasizes cost-effectiveness and rejects symbolic politics that burden business and rural areas. The committee majority rejects C's and MP's motions on sustainable design and circular economy, citing ongoing EU work. These motions risk pushing toward a more costly and heavily regulated stance than SD's evidence-based environmental principle warrants. SD votes Yes with the committee majority.

citations.quote: Sweden Democrat environmental policy starts from the idea of stewardship and strives to find the most environmentally effective and cost-effective methods, which at the same time do not harm industries and rural areas.
Stop symbolic politics that undermine the ability to conduct industry and business

motivering: MP's motion on AI and privacy (claim 30) is rejected by the committee. SD's platform contains no specific commitments on AI legislation or privacy rules. The party is skeptical of excessive digital regulation and, as a cooperation party, supports the government's assessment that existing provisions are sufficient. Yes supports the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: The Sweden Democrats want to prevent lecturing (pekpinnar) from the EU that threatens to determine what content may be provided through digital services and how material may be spread on the Internet.

motivering: The party's family policy emphasizes legally secure, quality-assured processes and early mediation in family disputes, which fits well with the committee's tillkännagivande (formal request) for a more well-functioning and legally secure process for division of property. The many individual motions on custody etc. are rejected in line with other work already underway.

citations.quote: We want to offer family mediation at an early stage. This can involve disputes over custody, in legal proceedings, or barnfridsbrott (child-peace offenses) in cases of violence in close relationships.
Investigations concerning children shall be quality-assured and legally secure.

motivering: The committee rejects V's own motions (Jessica Wetterling et al. (V), claims 1 and 2), which form Reservation 1. The party votes No to defend its own reservation. citations.quote: Restoring the role of politics, and holding those who govern accountable, is something you help do.

motivering: The election manifesto states that 'we are in a climate emergency' and emphasizes the protection of biological diversity as a central environmental principle. Uranium extraction is environmentally harmful and conflicts with the party's demand for ecological sustainability and nature protection. The party supports the reservation (no. 6), which likely calls for stronger restrictions on uranium extraction, and votes No.

citations.quote: We are in a climate emergency.
The protection of forest and shore areas is an important part of safeguarding the Swedish allemansrätten (right of public access) and biological diversity.

motivering: The manifesto does not specifically cover GPS monitoring during prisoner transports. The Left Party emphasizes that crime-fighting should above all be done by addressing deeper societal causes rather than through expanded control technology. citations.quote: In a safe society, we take firm action against violence, honor-related oppression, and sexual violations against women, children, and LGBTQI people.

motivering: V supports solidarity-financed healthcare and state actors in the healthcare sector. motivering: The manifesto states that 'it is the most vulnerable in society who are hit hardest' by drug use and that 'repression and tougher measures' are put forward instead of taking the problems seriously. citations.quote: Too often, repression and tougher measures are put forward as solutions instead of taking the problems seriously.

motivering: The Left Party strongly emphasizes preventive and coordinated efforts for young people at risk of crime. citations.quote: Schools and leisure activities need to be given better resources, as does social services. Give children and young people access to municipally supported leisure activities, give schools better resources to support students who need it to pass their grades, and strengthen social services with sufficient resources and knowledge to work both preventively and with child protection.
citations.princip: coordinated preventive efforts for young people

citations.quote: This requires extensive preventive efforts. To bring down crime, it is not enough to be tough on criminals — you have to be smarter than the criminals.

motivering: The Left Party is critical of the influence business lobbying organizations have over politics and wants to hold those in power accountable. Restoring the role of politics, and holding those who govern accountable, is something you help do.

motivering: The case concerns activity compensation and sickness compensation, and the committee rejects, among other things, the Left Party's own motion on sickness insurance. motivering: The committee rejects the Left Party's own motion item 19 (Nooshi Dadgostar et al.) on protection against eviction of families with children. raise study support so that more people can choose further education

citations.princip: stop discrimination in the labour market

citations.quote: The Left Party is a socialist, feminist and anti-racist party on an ecological basis.

citations.quote: A school that gives children equal chances is also compensatory, that is, it is able to give more support to those who come from worse conditions.
Swedish preschool and school shall be equal and equitable, where all children and young people are given the same right to education.
The Left Party is a socialist, feminist and anti-racist party on an ecological basis.

citations.quote: Wage dumping, economic crime and exploitation are central threats today.
The Left Party will continue to defend the right to negotiate and strong labour law legislation.

motivering: The election manifesto lacks a specific position on mineral compensation. It is important that culture stands free from both commercial and political control and exists throughout the country.

Racism grows between neighbors and workmates, people who actually have everything to gain from sticking together.

motivering: The election manifesto states that 'all political decisions need to take into account the acute crisis we are in' and acknowledges a climate emergency. Revised sustainability requirements in trade agreements are a direct application of the party's climate principle. The party supports the reservation (no. 5) and votes No against rejecting the Green Party's motion.

citations.quote: The transition needs to happen immediately, and all political decisions need to take into account the acute crisis we are in.
citations.princip: Climate consideration in all political decisions

citations.quote: We are in a climate emergency.

motivering: The committee endorses the center-right government's (M+KD+L+SD) tax policy, which V clearly opposes. V does not want to favor the RUT deduction (tax deduction for household services) and other tax benefits for the well-off, but instead redistribute resources to shared welfare. V supports Reservation 13 against the committee's position.

citations.quote: We do not want to raise taxes on ordinary wage earners, but on multi-million inheritances, luxury villas, and large capital gains that one doesn't even need to work for.
Instead of the RUT deduction for cleaning services for fully healthy people, we can use the tax revenue to improve home care services.

motivering: The election manifesto lacks explicit positions on overall free trade or protectionism. The motions that were rejected came from SD and S, whose specific trade policy demands cannot be directly linked to V's documented principles. Without an identified V reservation, the party supports the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: The future cannot be left to the whims of market forces; the future belongs to all of us.

motivering: The committee rejects V's own motions 2 and 9 (Nooshi Dadgostar et al.) on the organization of the Armed Forces. The election platform is unambiguous: Sweden should be a voice for peace and justice, not for increased militarization, and V opposes deepened military cooperation. V votes No and supports its reservation (Alternative A: Reservation 3).

citations.quote: The Left Party believes that Sweden should be a voice for peace and justice, not for increased militarization
The Left Party is opposed to Sweden's ever-deepening military cooperation with NATO and the EU, and we are the only parliamentary party that consistently upholds and wants to restore

motivering: The committee rejects V's own motion demands (Lotta Johnsson Fornarve et al.) on multilateral aid. V's platform explicitly demands increased aid and a strengthened UN. Voting Yes would mean the party supports the rejection of its own motion, which is out of the question. V supports Reservation 4.

citations.quote: Sweden shall increase aid, strengthen the UN, and sign the Nuclear Weapons Convention.
citations.princip: increased aid and a strengthened UN

citations.quote: The Left Party is a socialist, feminist, and anti-racist party on an ecological basis.

motivering: The committee proposes to reject the Left Party's motion on accessibility and mapping within mineral policy (Dadgostar, motion item 16). The party advocates democratic control over natural resources and does not want to leave raw material issues to market forces. No supports the party's reservation and own motion.

citations.quote: The state must increase its control over the infrastructure and resources needed to carry out the climate transition.
The future cannot be left to the whims of market forces; the future belongs to all of us.
citations.princip: resources belong to all of us

motivering: The election platform explicitly highlights an effective defector program (avhopparprogram) as one of the tools against gang crime, alongside more police officers and measures against weapons and drugs. This gives clear documentary support for backing the Social Democrats' (S) motion's reservation on defector-support activities rather than the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: work against drug trafficking, the fight against access to illegal firearms, and an effective defector program

motivering: The election manifesto does not take a position on wildlife management, hunting law, or the composition of the wildlife management delegations. The Left Party's (V) environmental policy focuses on forest protection and biological diversity but gives no guidance on this specific question of local influence in wildlife management. The party has no clear position that corresponds to either the committee's proposal or the counter-proposal.

citations.quote: Protecting forest and shoreline areas is an important part of safeguarding the Swedish right of public access (allemansrätten) and biological diversity.

motivering: The question of the organization of the Swedish Better Regulation Council (Regelrådet) concerns regulatory simplification for businesses, which the election manifesto does not address directly. The party's overall line emphasizes state governance over deregulation in favor of business interests. There is no Left Party (V) motion in this matter, so V votes with the committee's rejection of the motions from the Sweden Democrats (SD) and the Centre Party (C).

citations.quote: The state must increase its control over the infrastructure and resources needed to carry out the climate transition

motivering: The committee rejects the Left Party's (V) own motions 3-12 (Håkan Svenneling et al.) on nuclear weapons and foreign troops on Swedish soil. The election platform demands non-alignment (alliansfrihet) and opposition to military cooperation with NATO; nuclear weapons and a permanent foreign troop presence conflict with the party's peace line. V votes No and supports its reservation (Alternative A: Reservation 3).

citations.quote: The Left Party is opposed to Sweden's ever-deeper military cooperation with NATO and the EU, and we are the only Riksdag party that consistently safeguards and wants to restore Swedish non-alignment. The Left Party wants Sweden to abrogate the Host Nation Support Agreement (värdlandsavtalet)
Sweden shall increase development aid, strengthen the UN, and sign the Nuclear Weapons Convention
citations.princip: the Nuclear Weapons Convention and the UN

motivering: The election manifesto does not address copyright-protected artworks in public places. The motions come from the Sweden Democrats (SD) and the Centre Party (C), and there is no Left Party (V) motion in this matter. Without a documented position of its own, V follows the committee's rejection of the motions.

citations.quote: market ideology has been allowed to govern and politics has shifted away responsibility

motivering: The motion on a crime victims' ombudsman is the Left Party's own (Nordborg et al.) and is in line with the party's demand that crime victims' experiences, particularly women's, be taken seriously and that the justice system functions properly. The party therefore votes for its own reservation.

citations.quote: It is important that the justice system functions, that women's experiences are taken seriously, and that those who commit crimes are convicted.

motivering: The motions on regulatory simplification in agriculture are driven by the Centre Party (C) and the Sweden Democrats (SD) with the aim of reducing the regulatory burden, which risks undermining environmental and climate governance. The Left Party holds that 'blind faith in the market and turning a blind eye to the climate crisis is yesterday's politics' and demands stricter climate targets, not deregulation. The committee's rejection of these motions is consistent with V's principles.

citations.quote: Blind faith in the market and turning a blind eye to the climate crisis is yesterday's politics.
citations.princip: Against market deregulation on environmental issues

citations.quote: The transition needs to happen immediately, and all political decisions need to take into account the acute crisis we are in.
citations.princip: Climate considerations in all political decisions

motivering: The Left Party wants to transition away from fossil fuels through state investments in railways, electrification, and public transport, not through lower fuel taxes. The Centre Party's motions on lower fuel taxes conflict with this line, which is why the committee's rejection should be supported.

citations.quote: Heavy transport needs to be directed toward rail and sustainable shipping.
We are in a climate emergency.

motivering: The election manifesto explicitly states that 'the Left Party demands collective agreements in public procurement.' The motion on fair conditions and limiting subcontractor chains has been put forward by V's own members (Ciczie Weidby et al.). The committee's rejection conflicts directly with the party's documented policy; V supports its reservation no. 9 and votes No.

citations.quote: The Left Party demands collective agreements in public procurement.
The role of trade unions and collective agreements is central both to the economy and to democracy.
citations.princip: Strong labor law and collective agreements

motivering: The election platform focuses on lower rents and massive housing construction but does not explicitly take a position on illegal trading in rental contracts. Without a clear position of its own on this particular question, and since the committee refers to ongoing work, there is no documentary support for opposing the proposal.

citations.quote: The Left Party's next step is about a policy for massive housing construction, climate-smart renovations, and lower rents

motivering: The election manifesto does not address the organizational form of public health work or the current motions specifically. Without a clear V position on this particular narrow question, and since the committee refers to ongoing work, the party follows the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: Health care must be equal, gender-equal, and accessible, regardless of where in the country you live and regardless of who you are.

motivering: V wants a functioning justice system with more police officers, witness protection, and effective crime fighting. The committee's rejection of motions on witness protection, legal counsel, and trial costs conflicts with V's demand for an accessible and strong justice system for crime victims. V supports reservation 18.

citations.quote: Crime needs to be met both with a functioning and present justice system, such as more patrolling police officers, work against drug trafficking, the fight against access to illegal firearms, and an effective defector program

motivering: PFAS in drinking water is a direct public health issue. The Left Party's demand for immediate political action on environmental and health issues means the party cannot accept the committee's rejection of a motion on limit values. Referring to ongoing work is not enough — the Left Party supports Reservation 13 for stricter regulation.

citations.quote: The transition needs to happen immediately, and all political decisions need to take into account the acute crisis we find ourselves in.
We are in a climate emergency.

motivering: The Left Party emphasizes that chemical and environmental problems require international solutions and that politics must take these issues seriously. Rejecting expanded international chemical work conflicts with the party's principled support for international cooperation on environmental issues. The Left Party supports Reservation 3.

citations.quote: Some solutions need to be international, but much can be achieved nationally, if only the political will exists.
We are in a climate emergency.
citations.princip: environmental and health crisis requires action

motivering: The manifestos support sustainable food production but do not specify the concrete direction of the food strategy. The motions include the Centre Party's competition-focused demands, which do not match the Left Party's sustainability profile, and without a clear Left Party reservation, the committee's rejection is supported as the default position.

citations.quote: Another important part of the green transition is investments in sustainable food production.

motivering: The Left Party's own motion (Ida Gabrielsson et al.) is among those the committee proposes to reject, and the party demands a humane sickness insurance system and an end to the disqualification of sick people from benefits via the rehabilitation chain. The party should therefore support its own reservation against the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: The Left Party wants to see a humane sickness insurance system and an end to sick people being disqualified from benefits.
citations.princip: stop disqualifying sick people from benefits

citations.quote: When you fall ill or give birth, you should be able to trust that you will receive compensation from the Swedish Social Insurance Agency without having to fight tooth and nail for it.

motivering: The election manifesto emphasizes that 'a free culture is crucial for a strong democracy' and that it is important to counteract right-wing populist forces controlling information and content. Strengthened protection for journalists and artists is a natural application of the party's principled defense of the freedom of culture. The party supports the reservation and votes No.

citations.quote: We live in a time when right-wing populist forces are trying to control information and content ever more harshly. That is why it is particularly important to invest in and develop public libraries, popular education, and the independent standing of public service. A free culture is crucial for a strong democracy.
Politics should create the conditions for a broad culture that benefits everyone and keep an arm's length from its content.

motivering: The Left Party demands a total ban on profit-driven operations in welfare and wants to stop the pursuit of profit. The matter concerns precisely profits in welfare, which aligns directly with the party's core demand, so the party should support the reservation against the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: The Left Party wants to introduce a total ban on all profit-driven forms of operation within welfare.
citations.princip: total ban on profits in welfare

citations.quote: A significant majority of Sweden's population wants to put a stop to the neoliberal privatizations and stop the pursuit of profit in welfare.
citations.princip: stop the pursuit of profit in welfare

motivering: The goals of the simplification policy concern the regulatory burden on businesses, an area the election manifesto does not directly address. The party's stance emphasizes state governance and regulation rather than deregulation in favor of business. No Left Party motion exists in the matter, and the Left Party therefore votes with the committee's rejection of the motions from the Moderates and the Social Democrats.

citations.quote: The state must increase its control over the infrastructure and resources needed to carry out the climate transition

motivering: The Left Party's own motions are not included in the vote. The committee rejects Social Democrat motions on extending the Elderly Care Boost. The election platform demands strengthened staff conditions and more resources for elderly care; an extension of the skills investment for staff is in line with this position. The Left Party votes No and supports Reservation 16.

citations.quote: That is why the Left Party wants to invest more resources in healthcare and elderly care, as well as invest in staff so that we simultaneously eliminate the staff shortage and strengthen staff conditions and working environment

motivering: The election manifesto explicitly demands that Sweden increase its foreign aid. The committee rejects the Left Party's own motions (Lotta Johnsson Fornarve et al.) on the aid level. The Left Party supports Reservation 1, which demands increased aid, directly in accordance with the party's written program.

citations.quote: Sweden should increase its foreign aid, strengthen the UN, and sign the nuclear weapons convention.
we are a movement that places international solidarity high on the agenda.

motivering: The Left Party wants to see decisive action against men's violence against women and a justice system that works for crime victims. The committee's formal request (tillkännagivande) for a zero-vision against violence in close relationships is a step in that direction, which the party can reasonably be expected to support, even though the party's own more far-reaching demands appear elsewhere among the motions.

citations.quote: In a safe society, we take decisive action against violence, honor-based oppression, and sexual violations against women, children, and LGBTQI people.
citations.princip: decisive action against violence against women

citations.quote: It is important that the justice system works, that women's experiences are taken seriously, and that those who commit crimes are convicted.
citations.princip: functioning justice system for crime victims

motivering: The election manifesto does not address cybersecurity or technical information preparedness. The Left Party's statements on state control of infrastructure concern the climate transition and the power grid, not knowledge-building in the field of cybersecurity. The documents do not provide sufficient guidance to take a position on the substantive issue.

citations.quote: The state must increase its control over the infrastructure and resources needed to carry out the climate transition.

motivering: The election manifesto addresses neither the reindeer husbandry industry nor Sami rights specifically. The Social Democrats' motion on reindeer husbandry falls outside what the documents cover, and without a clear Left Party position or reservation, the committee's rejection is supported as the default position.

citations.quote: Regardless of where in the country we live, we have a common interest in ensuring that rural areas are not depleted.
citations.princip: Safeguarding the interests of rural areas

motivering: The election platform does not address value-added tax issues specifically, but the Left Party's tax policy prioritizes directing tax revenue to welfare and targeting relief at ordinary wage earners rather than general exemptions. Without support for the Centre Party's specific VAT motion, the party should follow the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: The Left Party has a tax policy that considers what needs exist and where those with large capital assets or high salaries contribute more to welfare than they do today.

motivering: The Left Party advocates state control and regulation of the economy rather than market-oriented deregulation. The motions from the Sweden Democrats, the Centre Party and the Social Democrats on reducing regulatory burdens for businesses do not align with the Left Party's principle that politics — not the market — should govern societal development. The Left Party supports the committee's decision to reject these motions.

citations.quote: The future cannot be handed over to the arbitrariness of market forces — the future belongs to all of us.
Collective agreements and labour law legislation ensure basic influence and protect us as employees from arbitrary abuse of power.

motivering: The manifesto generally describes the need for a functioning justice system for crime victims but does not specifically address compensation for violation and debt collection. In the absence of a clear Left Party stance on this technical issue, the party follows the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: It is important that the justice system works, that women's experiences are taken seriously, and that those who commit crimes are convicted.
citations.princip: a functioning justice system for crime victims

motivering: The Left Party demands a well-equipped and crisis-resilient healthcare system with strong state capacity. The proposal for an expanded public-service mandate for the state-owned company Apotek P&L (Pharmacy Producer & Laboratory), along with stricter requirements for care providers to hold necessary supplies, fits well with the Left Party's demand to upgrade the entire care sector for times of crisis. The Left Party supports the committee's proposal.

citations.quote: Sweden needs to upgrade the entire care sector in order to cope with more normal fluctuations in care needs, but also to be able to scale up capacity in times of crisis.
citations.princip: upgrading the care sector for crisis preparedness

citations.quote: Care that is funded through solidarity by tax revenue, where the money goes to operations and not to corporate profits, is a basic prerequisite for achieving equal care throughout Sweden.

motivering: The committee's tillkännagivande (formal request to the government) aims to make the permitting process for mineral extraction more accommodating to industry, which conflicts with the Left Party's principles of strengthening environmental protection and state control over natural resources. The manifesto emphasizes protecting forest and natural areas and increasing, not deregulating, state governance. The Left Party therefore supports reservation 18 and votes no on the committee's main proposal.

citations.quote: Protection of forest and coastal areas is an important part of safeguarding the Swedish right of public access (allemansrätten) and biological diversity
citations.princip: protection of nature and biological diversity

citations.quote: The state must increase its control over the infrastructure and resources needed to carry out the climate transition

motivering: The Left Party's criminal justice policy emphasizes preventive measures over harsher penalties and clearly distances itself from the Sweden Democrats' (Jomshof's) punitive line. The committee's rejection of the Sweden Democrats' demand for harsher penalties is consistent with the Left Party's emphasis on prevention and rehabilitation. The Left Party supports the committee's rejection of the Sweden Democrats' punitively oriented motion.

citations.quote: This requires extensive preventive measures.
much more focus must be directed at preventing the recruitment of new children into gang crime
Too often, repression and harsher measures are put forward as solutions instead of tackling the problems seriously.

motivering: The rejected motion is the Left Party's own (Karin Rågsjö et al.), which is in line with the demand to upgrade the care sector and invest more resources in healthcare and elder care, not least since the pandemic showed how vulnerable the elderly are. The party should therefore support its own reservation.

citations.quote: That is why the Left Party wants to invest more resources in healthcare and elder care, and invest in staff so that we can eliminate staff shortages while strengthening staff conditions and work environment.
citations.princip: more resources for healthcare and elder care

citations.quote: Sweden needs to upgrade the entire care sector in order to cope with more normal fluctuations in care needs, but also to be able to scale up capacity in times of crisis.

motivering: The committee rejects the Left Party's own motion item 2 (Karin Rågsjö et al.) on equipment to protect healthcare staff. The party pursues its reservation 2 and votes No to assert its position on strengthened equipment and safety for healthcare staff, in line with the Left Party's demand for a well-equipped and crisis-resilient care system.

citations.quote: Sweden needs to upgrade the entire care sector in order to cope with more normal fluctuations in care needs, but also to be able to scale up capacity in times of crisis.
Healthcare must be equal, gender-equal and accessible, regardless of where in the country you live and regardless of who you are.

motivering: The Centre Party's motion on security of supply in the CAP's strategic plan 2023-2027 is not covered by the Left Party's election manifesto. The manifesto supports sustainable domestic food production but gives no guidance on the CAP's specific strategic direction. Without a Left Party reservation, the committee's rejection is supported.

citations.quote: Another important part of the green transition is investment in sustainable food production.

motivering: The Left Party demands that publicly essential activities be strengthened and that resources be reclaimed from privatizations. The committee's rejection of motions on the development of the rescue services conflicts with the Left Party's general demand for a well-funded and strong public sector. The Left Party supports reservation 3, which calls for active development of the rescue services.

citations.quote: It is high time to act and reclaim the socially essential activities and infrastructure that have been privatized.

motivering: The committee rejects the Left Party's own motion items (Lotta Johnsson Fornarve et al.) on gender equality, SRHR (sexual and reproductive health and rights) and aid effectiveness. The Left Party is a feminist party that demands increased development aid and strengthened international gender equality work. Voting Yes would mean the party approves the rejection of its own motion — out of the question. The Left Party supports Reservation 1.

citations.quote: Sweden should increase its development aid, strengthen the UN and sign the nuclear weapons convention.
The Left Party is a socialist, feminist and anti-racist party on an ecological basis.

motivering: The Left Party explicitly demands increased knowledge within the justice system about violence against women and children. The rejected motions are about exactly this, so the party should support the reservation instead of the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: more police officers are needed, increased knowledge within the justice system about consent and about violence against women and children, and penalties that ensure such crimes are prioritized by law enforcement authorities
citations.princip: increased knowledge in the justice system about violence

motivering: V demands that everyone has the right to a good home and that the elderly should be able to live securely and not merely survive on their pension. The committee's rejection of motions on housing for the elderly conflicts with V's clear commitments to security and good living conditions for the elderly. V supports Reservation 24.

citations.quote: Ensuring that everyone who lives in Sweden has a good home is one such example.
citations.princip: right to a good home for everyone

citations.quote: You should feel secure when you grow old. The Left Party wants a new pension system that does not make people poor

motivering: The committee rejects, among other things, an unidentified motion (probably V's) on the rights of the elderly. The election platform demands that the dignity of the elderly and their right to care based on need be safeguarded and that market logic must not govern. V votes No and supports Reservation 1 (Alternative A).

citations.quote: That you are dependent on care should not, as today, limit your ability to control your own life

The testimonies of elderly people who almost never get to go outside or who must eat their dinner early in the afternoon so that staff schedules can be made to work bear witness to a shift in the view of human dignity
citations.princip: the human dignity of the elderly

motivering: The election manifesto consistently criticizes how market solutions have eroded the public good and how privatizations have led to negative consequences for citizens. Farm-gate sales of alcohol represent a liberalization that conflicts with the party's principled opposition to market solutions in publicly regulated areas. The party supports the committee's rejection of the market-liberal motions from the SD, C and M parties.

citations.quote: In recent decades, policy has relied on the market to solve our need for security, but market solutions have eroded our shared welfare
Privatizations have led to higher electricity prices, and pharmacies moving from rural areas to cities and from poor to rich areas

motivering: The manifesto does not address the SD's specific proposal on the role of the municipal sector. As an anti-racist party with a different view on state redistribution to municipalities, the Left Party does not share the SD's line and instead follows the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: The Left Party is a socialist, feminist and anti-racist party on an ecological foundation.
citations.princip: anti-racist party, different line than the SD

citations.quote: Redistribution from the state to regions and municipalities must increase, and special consideration must be given to the many municipalities and regions that today cannot make their finances balance

motivering: The Left Party wants to take firm action against violence, honor-related oppression and sexual abuse against women, children and LGBTQI people. Motions from the C and S parties on strengthening aggravating circumstances for such crimes align with V's feminist and anti-racist values. V does not support the committee's rejection of these motions — the party supports Reservation 32.

citations.quote: In a safe society we take firm action against violence, honor-related oppression and sexual abuse against women, children and LGBTQI people.
Inequality has a high price.

motivering: The motions from the C and MP parties on sustainable design and the circular economy coincide with V's clear commitments to increased reuse and recycling. The manifesto states that 'reuse and recycling of materials need to increase' and advocates products that can be reused. V supports Reservation 4.

citations.quote: Reuse and recycling of materials need to increase.
products that last and can easily be reused and shared instead of throwaway consumption

motivering: The election manifesto states that 'the future cannot be surrendered to the whims of market forces' and supports democratic governance of societal functions. Increased control over how the public sector uses AI and personal data falls within the principle of democratic transparency and accountability. The party supports the reservation on AI integrity and votes No against the committee's rejection.

citations.quote: The future cannot be surrendered to the whims of market forces; the future belongs to all of us.
Welfare is society's responsibility and ought to be governed democratically.

motivering: The rejected motion is partly the Left Party's own (Nadja Awad et al.) and the matter concerns custody, residence and contact in cases of family violence. The manifesto demands a strengthened child perspective in custody disputes and that perpetrators of violence should not be able to retain joint custody, so the party should support the reservation.

citations.quote: The child's perspective must be strengthened in custody disputes, and it should not be possible for perpetrators of violence to retain joint custody.
citations.princip: child perspective in custody disputes involving violence
